# ARS v3.6.4 — Literature Corpus Input Port and Reference Adapters

Source: https://github.com/imbad0202/academic-research-skills/blob/main/docs/design/2026-04-23-ars-v3.6.4-literature-corpus-adapters-design.md

# ARS v3.6.4 — Literature Corpus Input Port and Reference Adapters

- **Status**: Design approved, awaiting implementation plan
- **Author**: Cheng-I Wu (with AI collaborator)
- **Created**: 2026-04-23
- **ARS version target**: 3.6.4
- **Predecessor**: v3.6.3 (passport reset boundary)
- **Relates to**: [Material Passport data-layer boundary](../../academic-pipeline/references/passport_as_reset_boundary.md), Schema 9 in [`shared/handoff_schemas.md`](../../shared/handoff_schemas.md)

## 1. Scope and Non-Goals

### 1.1 In-scope

1. **Schema 9 extension**: add optional `literature_corpus: list[object]` field to the Material Passport.
2. **Entry contract**: `shared/contracts/passport/literature_corpus_entry.schema.json`. Entries use CSL-JSON name format for authors. Required set: `citation_key`, `title`, `authors`, `year`, `source_pointer`.
3. **Language-neutral adapter contract**: `academic-pipeline/references/adapters/overview.md` defines what any adapter must do (input assumptions, output files, error handling, rejection-log shape, provenance conventions, extension points).
4. **Three reference adapter implementations** in Python: `scripts/adapters/{folder_scan,zotero,obsidian}.py`, with tests and input/expected-output fixtures.
5. **Rejection log contract**: `shared/contracts/passport/rejection_log.schema.json`. Always emitted; empty when no rejections.
6. **CI lint**: schema validation (lint A), adapter-example validation (lint B), and schema→docs sync check (lint C) via `scripts/sync_adapter_docs.py --check`.
7. **pytest CI job** for `scripts/adapters/tests/`.
8. **Docs**: CHANGELOG, README EN + zh-TW, `.claude/CLAUDE.md`, version bump to 3.6.4, PERFORMANCE docs, and retirement of the "deferred to v3.6.4, PR-B" placeholders in `passport_as_reset_boundary.md`.

### 1.2 Out-of-scope (explicit)

- PDF parsing, OCR, text extraction. Data-layer responsibility.
- Zotero Web API client, Obsidian live vault daemon, or any service integration. Reference adapters read local files only.
- Paywall bypass, authenticated library crawling, cloud mirror fetching.
- Full-text ingestion. `full_text_ref` is reserved for a future release (tentatively v3.7.x), not v3.6.4.
- Privacy / copyright CI enforcement. `abstract` and `user_notes` carry text-only caveats in schema descriptions and `overview.md`. No lint blocks public passports that carry these fields.
- Non-Python reference implementations. `overview.md` is the language-neutral contract; Python is one reference implementation.
- Auto-ingestion from `literature_corpus[]` into `deep-research` or `synthesis_agent`. Consumer-side integration is deferred to v3.6.5+. This release only defines the input port and its producers.

### 1.3 Boundary rationale

ARS data-layer boundary is set by prior design decision: ARS defines `Material Passport` as the single input port; users own the corpus-to-passport adapter. v3.6.4 formalizes the `literature_corpus` portion of that contract and ships three reference adapters so the boundary is concrete, not aspirational. It does NOT ship production data-layer tooling.

## 2. Architecture and File Layout

### 2.1 Three layers

| Layer | Role | Artifact |
|-------|------|----------|
| **Contract** | Source of truth for passport and rejection shapes. | `shared/contracts/passport/literature_corpus_entry.schema.json`, `shared/contracts/passport/rejection_log.schema.json` |
| **Specification** | Language-neutral adapter behaviour. | `academic-pipeline/references/adapters/overview.md` |
| **Reference implementation** | Python adapters, tests, CI validation. | `scripts/adapters/**` |

Dependency direction: `overview.md` references the schemas; reference adapters read `overview.md` for the behavioural contract and emit output conforming to the schemas; `sync_adapter_docs.py` regenerates `overview.md`'s field tables from the schema so the two cannot drift.

## 3. `literature_corpus_entry` schema

File: `shared/contracts/passport/literature_corpus_entry.schema.json`.

### 3.1 Shape

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://github.com/Imbad0202/academic-research-skills/shared/contracts/passport/literature_corpus_entry.schema.json",
  "title": "Material Passport Literature Corpus Entry",
  "description": "One entry in Material Passport Schema 9 literature_corpus[]. Represents a single piece of literature the user has included in their corpus. Produced by user-written adapters; see academic-pipeline/references/adapters/overview.md. ARS does NOT produce these entries itself.",

  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,

  "required": [
    "citation_key",
    "title",
    "authors",
    "year",
    "source_pointer"
  ],

  "properties": {
    "citation_key": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "pattern": "^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_:-]*$",
      "description": "Stable unique identifier for this entry within the passport. Typically BibTeX citekey (e.g., 'chen2024ai'). MUST be unique within literature_corpus[]. Uniqueness is enforced by the CI lint, not by JSON Schema."
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1
    },
    "authors": {
      "type": "array",
      "minItems": 1,
      "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/csl_name" },
      "description": "CSL-JSON name format. Each item is either a personal name ({family, given, ...}) or a corporate/institution name ({literal}). See CSL-JSON spec at https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html#names."
    },
    "year": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1000,
      "maximum": 2100,
      "description": "Publication year. If the adapter cannot determine a year, the entry MUST be rejected (go to rejection_log.yaml) rather than coerced to a placeholder."
    },
    "source_pointer": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "Stable URI locating this work in the user's own KB. Examples: 'zotero://select/items/0_ABCD1234', 'obsidian://open?vault=kb&file=Chen2024', 'file:///path/to/refs/chen2024.pdf', 'https://doi.org/10.1234/xyz'. ARS does NOT dereference this; consumers that want the full text fetch it from the pointer themselves."
    },

    "venue":                  { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "doi": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^10\\.[0-9]{4,9}/[^\\s]+$",
      "description": "DOI without leading 'doi:' or URL prefix."
    },
    "tags": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
      "description": "User-assigned tags from the source KB. Adapter-specific; treat as free-form."
    },

    "obtained_via": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["zotero-api", "zotero-bbt-export", "obsidian-vault", "folder-scan", "manual", "other"],
      "description": "Strongly recommended. Which adapter produced this entry. 'other' is permitted for user-written custom adapters; those SHOULD also set adapter_name. Note: v3.6.4 reference implementations only use 'zotero-bbt-export', 'obsidian-vault', and 'folder-scan'. The remaining enum values ('zotero-api', 'manual') are reserved for user-written adapters and are permitted in the schema so such adapters remain valid without schema extension."
    },
    "obtained_at": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date-time",
      "description": "Strongly recommended. ISO 8601 timestamp when the adapter produced this entry."
    },
    "adapter_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "Optional. Required when obtained_via='other'."
    },
    "adapter_version": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1
    },

    "abstract": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "PRIVATE FIELD. May contain publisher-copyrighted material. Do NOT share passports containing this field publicly without confirming your right to do so. ARS consumers treat this as optional input; absence never causes failure."
    },
    "user_notes": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "PRIVATE FIELD. User's own annotations from their KB. May contain copyrighted excerpts. Same sharing caveat as abstract."
    }
  },

  "$defs": {
    "csl_name": {
      "oneOf": [
        { "$ref": "#/$defs/csl_personal_name" },
        { "$ref": "#/$defs/csl_literal_name" }
      ]
    },
    "csl_personal_name": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["family"],
      "properties": {
        "family":                { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
        "given":                 { "type": "string" },
        "suffix":                { "type": "string" },
        "dropping-particle":     { "type": "string" },
        "non-dropping-particle": { "type": "string" },
        "comma-suffix":          { "type": ["string", "boolean"] },
        "static-ordering":       { "type": ["string", "boolean"] },
        "parse-names":           { "type": ["string", "boolean"] }
      }
    },
    "csl_literal_name": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["literal"],
      "properties": {
        "literal": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 3.2 Rationale

- **β required set** (citation_key / title / authors / year / source_pointer): downstream consumers can safely index `authors[0]` and format citations without null checks. Looser α would produce unusable entries for synthesis; stricter γ would make `folder_scan` unviable.
- **CSL-JSON full name schema** (not `list[string]` and not `{family, given}` only): matches Zotero's internal representation, handles institution authors via `literal`, supports `non-dropping-particle` for "van der Berg" and similar.
- **`year` is integer, not CSL date-parts**: keeps schema simple. In-press / "n.d." / forthcoming entries go to `rejection_log`, where the user can correct the source or decide to skip. A future release may widen this to the CSL date-parts form if need arises.
- **`obtained_via` splits `zotero-api` from `zotero-bbt-export`**: the two have different freshness and auth surfaces; downstream tooling may want to distinguish.
- **`additionalProperties: false`**: the schema is a hard contract. Custom fields go via `tags[]` or via user-maintained forks of the schema.
- **`abstract` and `user_notes` as private optional fields**: publishers typically retain rights to abstracts; user notes often contain copyrighted excerpts. The schema description is the warning; no CI block. Users who publish passports are responsible for pruning these fields themselves.

## 4. Rejection log schema

File: `shared/contracts/passport/rejection_log.schema.json`.

### 4.1 Shape

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://github.com/Imbad0202/academic-research-skills/shared/contracts/passport/rejection_log.schema.json",
  "title": "Literature Corpus Rejection Log",
  "description": "Output companion to passport.yaml. Records entries that the adapter could not include in literature_corpus[]. Always emitted; empty when no rejections. Consumers are not required to read this; it exists for user debugging and audit.",

  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,

  "required": ["adapter_name", "adapter_version", "generated_at", "rejected"],

  "properties": {
    "adapter_name":   { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "adapter_version":{ "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "generated_at":   { "type": "string", "format": "date-time" },
    "input_source":   { "type": "string", "minLength": 1,
                        "description": "Optional. Human-readable description of the adapter input (path, URL, etc.)." },
    "rejected":       { "type": "array", "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/rejection" } },
    "summary": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "properties": {
        "total_input":    { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 },
        "total_accepted": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 },
        "total_rejected": { "type": "integer", "minimum": 0 }
      }
    }
  },

  "$defs": {
    "rejection": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["source", "reason"],
      "properties": {
        "source": {
          "type": "string",
          "minLength": 1,
          "description": "Where the rejected item came from. Adapter-specific: filename for folder_scan, Zotero item key for zotero, .md path for obsidian."
        },
        "reason": {
          "type": "string",
          "enum": [
            "missing_required_field",
            "invalid_field_format",
            "duplicate_citation_key",
            "unresolvable_source_pointer",
            "year_unparseable",
            "authors_unparseable",
            "adapter_error",
            "other"
          ]
        },
        "detail": {
          "type": "string",
          "description": "Free-text explanation. Required when reason='other'. Recommended otherwise."
        },
        "raw": {
          "type": ["object", "string"],
          "description": "Optional. Adapter's best-effort reproduction of the original input item. Object for structured sources (Zotero export entry, Obsidian frontmatter dict); string for raw filenames or text lines."
        },
        "missing_fields": {
          "type": "array",
          "items": { "type": "string" },
          "description": "Optional but strongly recommended when reason='missing_required_field'. Enables batch fix in the user's KB."
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### 4.2 Rationale

- **Always emit, even when empty**: removes "file-exists?" branching in downstream tooling.
- **Categorical `reason` enum**: users can `grep` / filter to batch-fix their KB.
- **`raw` typed as `object | string`**: lets structured adapters (Zotero) dump the whole input entry while letting unstructured adapters (`folder_scan`) dump just a filename. Rules out `null`, `array`, numeric types, so downstream viewers can assume printable shapes.
- **No `rejection_id`**: rejection is a snapshot; re-running the adapter produces a fresh log. No cross-run tracking needed.
- **`missing_fields` separate from `detail`**: batch-fix tooling can consume the structured list without parsing free text.

## 5. Adapter specifications

### 5.1 Common contract (applies to all adapters)

**Inputs**
- User-specified source: filesystem path, exported JSON file, or vault directory.
- Adapters do NOT make network requests. Zotero adapter reads a local Better BibTeX JSON export; it does not call the Zotero Web API.
- Adapters do NOT parse PDF content, run OCR, or extract full text.

**Outputs**
Each adapter always emits exactly two files, paths configurable via CLI:

- `passport.yaml`: contains a top-level `literature_corpus` key holding a list of entries conforming to `literature_corpus_entry.schema.json`.
- `rejection_log.yaml`: conforms to `rejection_log.schema.json`, always present, `rejected: []` when no rejections.

**Error-handling protocol (fail-soft)**
- Entry-level schema violation: push into `rejection_log.rejected[]`, continue processing.
- Adapter-level error (input file missing, JSON parse failure, vault dir not readable): fail-loud with `exit 1` and a stderr message. Do NOT produce a partial passport.
- All-rejections case: `passport.yaml` contains `literature_corpus: []`; `rejection_log.yaml` lists rejected entries normally.

**Provenance**
- Each entry SHOULD carry `obtained_via` and `obtained_at`. Schema marks these optional; the contract marks them strongly recommended.
- `rejection_log.yaml` MUST carry `adapter_name`, `adapter_version`, and `generated_at`.

**Determinism**
- Same input → same output (excluding `generated_at` in the rejection log and `obtained_at` on each entry).
- `literature_corpus[]` entries sorted ascending by `citation_key`.
- `rejection_log.rejected[]` entries sorted by `source`.

**CLI shape** (reference implementations; custom adapters may adopt their own)
```bash
python scripts/adapters/zotero.py \
  --input path/to/export.json \
  --passport out/passport.yaml \
  --rejection-log out/rejection_log.yaml
```

### 5.2 `folder_scan.py`

**Input**: a folder that contains PDF or other files. Scanned recursively.

**Filename convention** (best-effort parsing):
- `{AuthorLastname}{Year}{optional_title_slug}.{ext}` → author family=Lastname, year=Year.
- `{AuthorLastname}_{Year}_{title_slug}.{ext}` → same.
- Fallback: regex `(19|20)\d{2}` for year, first capitalized Latin word before the year for family.
- Single author only per filename. The adapter does NOT attempt to extract multiple authors from filenames like `Anderson_Chen_2024.pdf`; the first capitalized Latin word before the year is taken as the single family name, and additional names in the filename are dropped without warning. Users with multi-author corpora should use `zotero.py` or `obsidian.py` instead of relying on filename parsing for co-author metadata.
- If `authors` or `year` cannot be recovered: reject (`authors_unparseable` or `year_unparseable`).

**citation_key**: `{lastname_lowercase}{year}` plus first non-stopword title slug token when available; append `a`, `b`, `c`, … on collision.

**source_pointer**: `file://` URL using the absolute path.

**obtained_via**: `folder-scan`.

**Optional fields**: `abstract`, `user_notes`, `tags`, `venue`, `doi` are always omitted (no source for them).

**Known limitations** (documented in `overview.md`):
- Unicode filenames (e.g., Chinese names) are not parsed; such files are rejected. Unicode support is a future extension opportunity.
- No PDF metadata extraction; the adapter does not open PDF files.
- Empty or mis-named folders produce a high rejection rate — by design.

### 5.3 `zotero.py`

**Input**: Better BibTeX Extension's JSON export (not native CSL-JSON; BBT is a superset that includes `citationKey`).

**Field mapping**:

| BBT field | Entry field |
|-----------|-------------|
| `citationKey` | `citation_key` |
| `title` | `title` |
| `creators[type=author]` | `authors[]` (1:1 CSL-JSON mapping) |
| `date` / `issued` | `year` (parse 4-digit year) |
| `itemID` / `key` | `source_pointer: zotero://select/items/0_{key}` |
| `tags[].tag` | `tags[]` |
| `publicationTitle` / `proceedingsTitle` / `bookTitle` | `venue` (first non-empty wins) |
| `DOI` | `doi` (lowercased, leading URL/prefix stripped) |
| `abstractNote` | `abstract` (with copyright caveat) |
| `notes[].note` (HTML) | stripped to plain text, concatenated into `user_notes` |

**obtained_via**: `zotero-bbt-export`.

**Known limitations**:
- Only `creators[type=author]` are ingested; editors, translators, chairs are dropped (or, if the user has zero `type=author`, the entry is rejected as `authors_unparseable`).
- Date formats like "Spring 2024", "forthcoming", "n.d." are rejected (`year_unparseable`).
- This adapter does not call the Zotero Web API. Users who want live-sync behaviour are expected to write their own adapter based on `zotero.py`; see `overview.md` extension-point guidance.

### 5.4 `obsidian.py`

**Input**: an Obsidian vault directory. A vault is a folder full of `.md` files.

**Two supported conventions**. Detection runs per file and is deterministic: the adapter reads the frontmatter block first; if a `citekey` key is present, the file is processed as Convention A. If `citekey` is absent (including the case where there is no frontmatter at all), the file falls through to Convention B. Files that parse as neither A nor B are rejected.

Convention A — frontmatter-based (preferred):
```markdown
---
citekey: chen2024ai
title: "AI assessment in higher education"
authors:
  - family: Chen
    given: Cindy
year: 2024
venue: "Assessment & Evaluation"
doi: "10.1234/xyz"
tags: [assessment, ai]
---

Note body becomes user_notes (with copyright caveat).
```

Convention B — Karpathy-style (detected when `citekey` frontmatter absent):
- Filename: `{citekey}.md`
- Frontmatter contains a `source:` field holding the original URL/DOI/path.
- Body first H1 line (`# ...`) is the title.
- Second line like `**Authors**: Chen, C.; Wang, J.` parsed as semicolon-separated CSL names.
- Year parsed from either `**Year**: 2024` line or first 4-digit year in the `source:` field.
- Any parse failure → reject.

**source_pointer**: `obsidian://open?vault={vault_name}&file={url_encoded_relative_path}`.

**obtained_via**: `obsidian-vault`.

**user_notes**: the markdown body, preserved as-is (copyright caveat applied).

**Known limitations**:
- Obsidian wikilinks (`[[other note]]`) are NOT resolved; they appear as literal text in `user_notes`.
- Files under `_templates/`, `.obsidian/`, and hidden directories are skipped.
- Obsidian plugin config is not read; no Dataview queries are executed.
- Convention B is sensitive to formatting; files that match neither A nor B are rejected.

## 6. CI lint and pytest job

### 6.1 `scripts/check_literature_corpus_schema.py` (lint A + B)

Runs on every PR. Validates:

1. **A1 — schema self-consistency**: each JSON schema under `shared/contracts/passport/*.schema.json` validates as a valid JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 (`jsonschema.Draft202012Validator.check_schema`).
2. **A2 — passport-level invariants**: in every `expected_passport.yaml`, `literature_corpus[*].citation_key` values are unique. This is a global constraint JSON Schema cannot express.
3. **B — example output validation**: each `scripts/adapters/examples/*/expected_passport.yaml` and `expected_rejection_log.yaml` validates against its schema.

Exit 1 on any violation with a summary of which files failed and why.

### 6.2 `scripts/sync_adapter_docs.py` (lint C)

**Purpose**: generate the field reference tables in `overview.md` from the schemas, so the two cannot drift.

**Modes**:
- `python scripts/sync_adapter_docs.py`: rewrites the marked sections of `overview.md` in place.
- `python scripts/sync_adapter_docs.py --check`: diffs the generated tables against what is currently in `overview.md`; exit 1 on mismatch, showing the diff.

**Anchor format in `overview.md`**:
```markdown
<!-- GENERATED:LITERATURE_CORPUS_FIELDS:START -->
(generated table)
<!-- GENERATED:LITERATURE_CORPUS_FIELDS:END -->
```

Multiple anchors allowed (one per table). The script reads the schema `properties` block, grouping by `required` vs. optional, and emits a markdown table with field name, type, and description.

### 6.3 pytest CI job

New file `.github/workflows/pytest.yml` (or a new job in the existing CI workflow):

```yaml
name: pytest

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - 'scripts/adapters/**'
      - 'shared/contracts/passport/**'
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'scripts/adapters/**'
      - 'shared/contracts/passport/**'

jobs:
  pytest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - name: Install deps
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install pytest pyyaml jsonschema
      - name: Run adapter tests
        run: pytest scripts/adapters/tests/ -v
```

The `paths:` filter prevents pytest from running on docs-only commits.

### 6.4 Test coverage per adapter

Each adapter test module exercises:

**Happy path**
- Read input fixture → produce passport and rejection log; output compared to `expected_passport.yaml` and `expected_rejection_log.yaml` byte-for-byte (after clearing non-deterministic timestamps).

**Rejection path**
- Input contains known-bad entries; rejection log carries them with the correct `reason` enum; passport excludes them.

**Edge cases (per adapter)**
- `folder_scan`: empty folder, non-parseable filename, duplicate citekey collision suffix.
- `zotero`: empty JSON array, malformed JSON (fail-loud path), corporate/institution author (`literal` variant), `creators` array with zero `type=author`.
- `obsidian`: vault with mixed A and B convention files, broken wikilink (handled as literal text), `_templates/` is skipped, `.obsidian/` hidden dir is skipped.

**Determinism**
- Running an adapter twice on the same input produces byte-identical output after removing `generated_at` and `obtained_at`.

**Common (`test_common.py`)**
- CSL name parsing helpers (e.g., `parse_semicolon_names("Chen, C.; van der Berg, J.")`).
- YAML emission (stable key order, proper multiline handling).
- citation_key sanitization (lowercase, strip punctuation, collision suffix `a`/`b`/`c`).

### 6.5 Existing CI workflow additions

In the existing CI workflow, add before the existing `check_passport_reset_contract.py` step:

```yaml
- name: Validate literature_corpus schemas and examples
  run: python scripts/check_literature_corpus_schema.py

- name: Check adapter docs up-to-date
  run: python scripts/sync_adapter_docs.py --check
```

- `README.md` and `README.zh-TW.md` (version / skill table)
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (Skills Overview version, v3.6.4 Key Additions)
- `scripts/check_spec_consistency.py` (version pin)
- `academic-pipeline/SKILL.md`, `academic-paper/SKILL.md`, `academic-paper-reviewer/SKILL.md`, `deep-research/SKILL.md` (suite version footer)
- `shared/handoff_schemas.md` (Schema 9 optional-fields table: add `literature_corpus` row)
- `academic-pipeline/references/passport_as_reset_boundary.md` (replace "deferred to v3.6.4, PR-B" placeholders with forward references)
- `docs/PERFORMANCE.md` and `docs/PERFORMANCE.zh-TW.md` (new "Literature corpus ingestion" section)
- `MODE_REGISTRY.md` (sweep check; no-op expected but verified by hand)

### 7.2 CHANGELOG entry

```markdown
## [3.6.4] — 2026-04-XX

### Added

- **Material Passport `literature_corpus[]` input port**. Schema 9 gains an optional
  `literature_corpus[]` field defined by
  `shared/contracts/passport/literature_corpus_entry.schema.json`. Each entry
  carries citation_key, CSL-JSON authors, year, title, and a source_pointer back
  to the user's own KB. `abstract` and `user_notes` are private optional fields
  with copyright caveats.

- **Adapter contract** (`academic-pipeline/references/adapters/overview.md`):
  language-neutral specification for producing literature_corpus entries from
  user-owned corpus sources. Covers fail-soft error handling, mandatory
  rejection-log output, deterministic ordering, and extension points.

- **Three reference adapter implementations** (`scripts/adapters/`):
  `folder_scan.py`, `zotero.py` (Better BibTeX export), `obsidian.py` (frontmatter
  or Karpathy-style convention). Each ships with tests and fixtures.

- **Rejection log contract** (`shared/contracts/passport/rejection_log.schema.json`).
  Always emitted; empty when no rejections.

- **CI lint and pytest job**: schema validation, adapter-example validation,
  schema→docs sync check, and pytest runs for adapter tests.

### Changed

- `academic-pipeline/references/passport_as_reset_boundary.md`: "deferred to v3.6.4"
  placeholders replaced with forward references.
- `shared/handoff_schemas.md`: Schema 9 optional fields table adds `literature_corpus`.

### Not changed (explicit non-goals)

- No ARS agent consumes `literature_corpus[]` yet. Consumer-side integration is
  deferred to a later release. v3.6.4 defines the input port only.
- No PDF parsing, no text extraction, no live API clients, no authenticated
  library crawling. ARS remains a writing/review-layer framework; data-layer
  integration belongs to user-owned adapters.
```

### 7.3 Release order

1. Feature branch: `feat/v3.6.4-literature-corpus-adapters`. Spec commit first, then schemas + adapters + tests + CI + docs, commit-by-commit.
2. Local test battery before push:
   ```
   pytest scripts/adapters/tests/
   python scripts/check_literature_corpus_schema.py
   python scripts/sync_adapter_docs.py --check
   python scripts/check_spec_consistency.py
   python scripts/check_passport_reset_contract.py
   ```
3. Push branch → open PR.
4. **Round 1 codex audit** (`/codex review --base main`). Apply P0/P1 fixes; commit.
5. **Round 2 codex audit**. Apply P0/P1 fixes; commit.
6. **Round 3+ codex audit until 0 P0/P1 remain**.
7. Run full local test battery again. Run `sync_adapter_docs.py --check` one more time.
8. **Fresh `codex review --base main`** in a new codex session (not resume). Apply any new P0/P1 findings; commit.
9. PR merge (via GitHub PR, not direct push to main).
10. Tag `v3.6.4`; publish GitHub release with notes from CHANGELOG entry.
11. Update memory: `project_academic_research_skills.md` → record v3.6.4 shipped, main SHA, tag.
12. Deferred: Substack / Michael follow-ups referencing the published spec and released adapters.

### 7.4 Rollback

v3.6.4 is additive and opt-in:
- Users who do not produce `literature_corpus[]` are unaffected. The field is optional.
- Adapters are reference examples under `scripts/`, not wired into any runtime.
- If a bug is found post-merge:
  - **Schema / adapter issue**: open v3.6.5 hotfix. Existing passports without `literature_corpus[]` continue to work.
  - **Sweep-level issue** (version pin drift, CLAUDE.md inconsistency): standard follow-up PR.

Worst-case revert: single `git revert` on the merge commit; no downstream system depends on the new field.

## 8. Open questions deferred to plan stage

- Exact Python version for `.github/workflows/pytest.yml`: confirm against existing CI (currently assumed 3.11). Align at plan stage.
- Whether `pytest.yml` is a new workflow file or a new job inside the existing CI workflow: either works; pick whichever reduces CI YAML duplication at implementation time.
- `_common.py` API surface: names of helper functions, whether to use `ruamel.yaml` vs `pyyaml` for YAML emission. Decided at plan stage; the spec only requires deterministic, round-tripped YAML.
- Exactly how to detect convention A vs. B in `obsidian.py`: the spec says "auto-detect"; the concrete rule (presence of `citekey` frontmatter key) is confirmed but the precise parse order can be tuned during TDD.

These are implementation-level details, not spec-level; they do not affect the contracts defined above.

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Ship ARS v3.6.4: the Material Passport `literature_corpus[]` input port, its JSON schemas, three Python reference adapters (folder_scan / zotero / obsidian), a rejection log contract, CI validation, a pytest job, and the full version-bump sweep.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.11, `pyyaml`, `jsonschema`, `pytest`. JSON Schema Draft 2020-12. YAML for passport/rejection outputs. GitHub Actions for CI.

**Branch:** `feat/v3.6.4-literature-corpus-adapters` (already exists, head `56639ae` with spec commit). All tasks commit to this branch.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Create `scripts/adapters/tests/test_literature_corpus_entry_schema.py`:

```python
"""Validates literature_corpus_entry.schema.json self-consistency and
round-trips a known-good example entry against it."""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import pytest
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
SCHEMA_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "shared/contracts/passport/literature_corpus_entry.schema.json"

def _load_schema():
    with SCHEMA_PATH.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)

def test_schema_file_exists():
    assert SCHEMA_PATH.exists(), f"schema missing at {SCHEMA_PATH}"

def test_schema_is_valid_draft_2020_12():
    schema = _load_schema()
    Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema)

def test_required_set_matches_spec():
    schema = _load_schema()
    assert schema["required"] == [
        "citation_key",
        "title",
        "authors",
        "year",
        "source_pointer",
    ]

def test_additional_properties_is_false():
    schema = _load_schema()
    assert schema["additionalProperties"] is False

def test_valid_personal_author_entry_passes():
    schema = _load_schema()
    entry = {
        "citation_key": "chen2024ai",
        "title": "AI assessment",
        "authors": [{"family": "Chen", "given": "Cindy"}],
        "year": 2024,
        "source_pointer": "https://doi.org/10.1234/xyz",
    }
    Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(entry)

def test_valid_institution_author_entry_passes():
    schema = _load_schema()
    entry = {
        "citation_key": "who2024report",
        "title": "World report",
        "authors": [{"literal": "World Health Organization"}],
        "year": 2024,
        "source_pointer": "https://www.who.int/report",
    }
    Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(entry)

def test_missing_required_field_fails():
    from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError
    schema = _load_schema()
    entry = {
        "citation_key": "chen2024ai",
        "title": "AI assessment",
        # missing authors
        "year": 2024,
        "source_pointer": "file:///x.pdf",
    }
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(entry)

def test_author_must_be_either_personal_or_literal():
    from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError
    schema = _load_schema()
    entry = {
        "citation_key": "bad2024",
        "title": "Bad author",
        "authors": [{}],  # neither family nor literal
        "year": 2024,
        "source_pointer": "file:///x.pdf",
    }
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(entry)

def test_year_out_of_range_fails():
    from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError
    schema = _load_schema()
    entry = {
        "citation_key": "old1",
        "title": "Ancient",
        "authors": [{"family": "X"}],
        "year": 999,
        "source_pointer": "file:///x.pdf",
    }
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(entry)

def test_citation_key_pattern_rejects_leading_digit():
    from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError
    schema = _load_schema()
    entry = {
        "citation_key": "2024chen",
        "title": "T",
        "authors": [{"family": "C"}],
        "year": 2024,
        "source_pointer": "file:///x.pdf",
    }
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(entry)

def test_additional_property_fails():
    from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError
    schema = _load_schema()
    entry = {
        "citation_key": "chen2024",
        "title": "T",
        "authors": [{"family": "C"}],
        "year": 2024,
        "source_pointer": "file:///x.pdf",
        "custom_field": "should_not_be_allowed",
    }
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(entry)

def test_obtained_via_enum_constrained():
    from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError
    schema = _load_schema()
    entry = {
        "citation_key": "chen2024",
        "title": "T",
        "authors": [{"family": "C"}],
        "year": 2024,
        "source_pointer": "file:///x.pdf",
        "obtained_via": "rubber-duck",
    }
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(entry)
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the schema**

Create `shared/contracts/passport/literature_corpus_entry.schema.json`:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$id": "https://github.com/Imbad0202/academic-research-skills/shared/contracts/passport/literature_corpus_entry.schema.json",
  "title": "Material Passport Literature Corpus Entry",
  "description": "One entry in Material Passport Schema 9 literature_corpus[]. Represents a single piece of literature the user has included in their corpus. Produced by user-written adapters; see academic-pipeline/references/adapters/overview.md. ARS does NOT produce these entries itself.",

  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,

  "required": [
    "citation_key",
    "title",
    "authors",
    "year",
    "source_pointer"
  ],

  "properties": {
    "citation_key": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "pattern": "^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_:-]*$",
      "description": "Stable unique identifier for this entry within the passport. Typically BibTeX citekey (e.g., 'chen2024ai'). MUST be unique within literature_corpus[]. Uniqueness is enforced by the CI lint, not by JSON Schema."
    },
    "title": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1
    },
    "authors": {
      "type": "array",
      "minItems": 1,
      "items": { "$ref": "#/$defs/csl_name" },
      "description": "CSL-JSON name format. Each item is either a personal name ({family, given, ...}) or a corporate/institution name ({literal}). See CSL-JSON spec at https://docs.citationstyles.org/en/stable/specification.html#names."
    },
    "year": {
      "type": "integer",
      "minimum": 1000,
      "maximum": 2100,
      "description": "Publication year. If the adapter cannot determine a year, the entry MUST be rejected (go to rejection_log.yaml) rather than coerced to a placeholder."
    },
    "source_pointer": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "Stable URI locating this work in the user's own KB. Examples: 'zotero://select/items/0_ABCD1234', 'obsidian://open?vault=kb&file=Chen2024', 'file:///path/to/refs/chen2024.pdf', 'https://doi.org/10.1234/xyz'. ARS does NOT dereference this; consumers that want the full text fetch it from the pointer themselves."
    },

    "venue":                  { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
    "doi": {
      "type": "string",
      "pattern": "^10\\.[0-9]{4,9}/[^\\s]+$",
      "description": "DOI without leading 'doi:' or URL prefix."
    },
    "tags": {
      "type": "array",
      "items": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
      "description": "User-assigned tags from the source KB. Adapter-specific; treat as free-form."
    },

    "obtained_via": {
      "type": "string",
      "enum": ["zotero-api", "zotero-bbt-export", "obsidian-vault", "folder-scan", "manual", "other"],
      "description": "Strongly recommended. Which adapter produced this entry. 'other' is permitted for user-written custom adapters; those SHOULD also set adapter_name. Note: v3.6.4 reference implementations only use 'zotero-bbt-export', 'obsidian-vault', and 'folder-scan'. The remaining enum values ('zotero-api', 'manual') are reserved for user-written adapters and are permitted in the schema so such adapters remain valid without schema extension."
    },
    "obtained_at": {
      "type": "string",
      "format": "date-time",
      "description": "Strongly recommended. ISO 8601 timestamp when the adapter produced this entry."
    },
    "adapter_name": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1,
      "description": "Optional. Required when obtained_via='other'."
    },
    "adapter_version": {
      "type": "string",
      "minLength": 1
    },

    "abstract": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "PRIVATE FIELD. May contain publisher-copyrighted material. Do NOT share passports containing this field publicly without confirming your right to do so. ARS consumers treat this as optional input; absence never causes failure."
    },
    "user_notes": {
      "type": "string",
      "description": "PRIVATE FIELD. User's own annotations from their KB. May contain copyrighted excerpts. Same sharing caveat as abstract."
    }
  },

  "$defs": {
    "csl_name": {
      "oneOf": [
        { "$ref": "#/$defs/csl_personal_name" },
        { "$ref": "#/$defs/csl_literal_name" }
      ]
    },
    "csl_personal_name": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["family"],
      "properties": {
        "family":                { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
        "given":                 { "type": "string" },
        "suffix":                { "type": "string" },
        "dropping-particle":     { "type": "string" },
        "non-dropping-particle": { "type": "string" },
        "comma-suffix":          { "type": ["string", "boolean"] },
        "static-ordering":       { "type": ["string", "boolean"] },
        "parse-names":           { "type": ["string", "boolean"] }
      }
    },
    "csl_literal_name": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["literal"],
      "properties": {
        "literal": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

```python
"""Validates rejection_log.schema.json self-consistency and example round-trip."""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import pytest
from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
SCHEMA_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "shared/contracts/passport/rejection_log.schema.json"

def _load_schema():
    with SCHEMA_PATH.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)

def test_schema_exists():
    assert SCHEMA_PATH.exists()

def test_schema_self_consistent():
    schema = _load_schema()
    Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema)

def test_empty_rejected_is_valid():
    schema = _load_schema()
    log = {
        "adapter_name": "zotero.py",
        "adapter_version": "1.0.0",
        "generated_at": "2026-04-23T00:00:00Z",
        "rejected": [],
    }
    Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(log)

def test_missing_required_top_level_fails():
    schema = _load_schema()
    log = {"adapter_name": "x", "adapter_version": "1", "rejected": []}
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(log)

def test_rejection_with_object_raw():
    schema = _load_schema()
    log = {
        "adapter_name": "zotero.py",
        "adapter_version": "1.0.0",
        "generated_at": "2026-04-23T00:00:00Z",
        "rejected": [
            {
                "source": "0_ABCD1234",
                "reason": "missing_required_field",
                "missing_fields": ["authors"],
                "raw": {"title": "Foo", "date": "n.d."},
            }
        ],
    }
    Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(log)

def test_rejection_with_string_raw():
    schema = _load_schema()
    log = {
        "adapter_name": "folder_scan.py",
        "adapter_version": "1.0.0",
        "generated_at": "2026-04-23T00:00:00Z",
        "rejected": [
            {
                "source": "paper1.pdf",
                "reason": "authors_unparseable",
                "raw": "paper1.pdf",
            }
        ],
    }
    Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(log)

def test_rejection_with_array_raw_rejected():
    schema = _load_schema()
    log = {
        "adapter_name": "x",
        "adapter_version": "1",
        "generated_at": "2026-04-23T00:00:00Z",
        "rejected": [
            {
                "source": "s",
                "reason": "other",
                "detail": "d",
                "raw": ["not", "allowed"],
            }
        ],
    }
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(log)

def test_reason_enum_constrained():
    schema = _load_schema()
    log = {
        "adapter_name": "x",
        "adapter_version": "1",
        "generated_at": "2026-04-23T00:00:00Z",
        "rejected": [{"source": "s", "reason": "invented_reason"}],
    }
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(log)

def test_additional_properties_false_on_rejection():
    schema = _load_schema()
    log = {
        "adapter_name": "x",
        "adapter_version": "1",
        "generated_at": "2026-04-23T00:00:00Z",
        "rejected": [
            {"source": "s", "reason": "other", "detail": "d", "bogus": 1}
        ],
    }
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
        Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(log)
```

```python
"""Tests for the CI lint that validates passport/rejection-log examples
against their schemas and enforces citation_key uniqueness."""
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import yaml
import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
SCRIPT = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/check_literature_corpus_schema.py"

def _write_yaml(tmp_path, name, data):
    p = tmp_path / name
    with p.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        yaml.safe_dump(data, f, sort_keys=True)
    return p

def _run(args, cwd=None):
    return subprocess.run(
        ["python", str(SCRIPT)] + args,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=cwd or REPO_ROOT,
    )

def test_script_exists():
    assert SCRIPT.exists()

def test_passes_on_valid_passport(tmp_path):
    passport = {
        "literature_corpus": [
            {
                "citation_key": "chen2024",
                "title": "T",
                "authors": [{"family": "Chen"}],
                "year": 2024,
                "source_pointer": "file:///x.pdf",
            }
        ]
    }
    _write_yaml(tmp_path, "passport.yaml", passport)
    r = _run(["--passport", str(tmp_path / "passport.yaml")])
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr

def test_fails_on_schema_violation(tmp_path):

            {

                "year": 2024,
                "source_pointer": "file:///x.pdf",
            }
        ]

    assert r.returncode != 0
    assert "schema" in r.stderr.lower() or "validation" in r.stderr.lower()
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the script**

Create `scripts/check_literature_corpus_schema.py`:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate literature_corpus_entry.schema.json and rejection_log.schema.json
self-consistency, and validate adapter example output against them.

Usage:
    python scripts/check_literature_corpus_schema.py
        Scans scripts/adapters/examples/**/expected_passport.yaml and
        **/expected_rejection_log.yaml. Validates each against its schema.
        Enforces citation_key uniqueness per passport.

    python scripts/check_literature_corpus_schema.py --passport PATH
        Validate one passport YAML only.

    python scripts/check_literature_corpus_schema.py --rejection-log PATH
        Validate one rejection log YAML only.

Exit codes:
    0 - all validations passed
    1 - one or more validations failed
    2 - invocation error (e.g., schema file missing)
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

try:
    import yaml
    from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
    from jsonschema.exceptions import ValidationError
except ImportError as e:
    print(f"Missing dependency: {e}. Install with: pip install pyyaml jsonschema", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
ENTRY_SCHEMA_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "shared/contracts/passport/literature_corpus_entry.schema.json"
REJECTION_SCHEMA_PATH = REPO_ROOT / "shared/contracts/passport/rejection_log.schema.json"
EXAMPLES_ROOT = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples"

def load_schema(path: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if not path.exists():
        print(f"ERROR: schema missing at {path}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        schema = json.load(f)
    try:
        Draft202012Validator.check_schema(schema)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR: schema at {path} is not valid Draft 2020-12: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    return schema

def validate_passport(path: Path, entry_schema: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    errors: list[str] = []
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = yaml.safe_load(f)
    if data is None:
        errors.append(f"{path}: empty YAML file")
        return errors
    corpus = data.get("literature_corpus", [])
    if not isinstance(corpus, list):
        errors.append(f"{path}: 'literature_corpus' must be a list")
        return errors
    validator = Draft202012Validator(entry_schema)
    citation_keys: dict[str, int] = {}
    for i, entry in enumerate(corpus):
        for err in validator.iter_errors(entry):
            errors.append(f"{path}: literature_corpus[{i}] schema validation error: {err.message}")
        key = entry.get("citation_key")
        if key:
            citation_keys[key] = citation_keys.get(key, 0) + 1
    for key, count in citation_keys.items():
        if count > 1:
            errors.append(f"{path}: duplicate citation_key '{key}' appears {count} times (must be unique)")
    return errors

def validate_rejection_log(path: Path, log_schema: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    errors: list[str] = []
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = yaml.safe_load(f)
    if data is None:
        errors.append(f"{path}: empty YAML file")
        return errors
    validator = Draft202012Validator(log_schema)
    for err in validator.iter_errors(data):
        errors.append(f"{path}: schema validation error: {err.message}")
    return errors

def scan_examples(entry_schema: dict[str, Any], log_schema: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    errors: list[str] = []
    if not EXAMPLES_ROOT.exists():
        return errors
    for passport in EXAMPLES_ROOT.glob("*/expected_passport.yaml"):
        errors.extend(validate_passport(passport, entry_schema))
    for log in EXAMPLES_ROOT.glob("*/expected_rejection_log.yaml"):
        errors.extend(validate_rejection_log(log, log_schema))
    return errors

def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Validate literature_corpus passport + rejection log YAMLs.")
    ap.add_argument("--passport", type=Path, help="Validate a single passport YAML.")
    ap.add_argument("--rejection-log", type=Path, help="Validate a single rejection log YAML.")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    entry_schema = load_schema(ENTRY_SCHEMA_PATH)
    log_schema = load_schema(REJECTION_SCHEMA_PATH)

    errors: list[str] = []
    if args.passport:
        errors.extend(validate_passport(args.passport, entry_schema))
    if args.rejection_log:
        errors.extend(validate_rejection_log(args.rejection_log, log_schema))

    if not args.passport and not args.rejection_log:
        errors.extend(scan_examples(entry_schema, log_schema))

    if errors:
        for e in errors:
            print(e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

```python
def test_make_citation_key_simple():

    key = make_citation_key(family="Chen", year=2024, title_hint="AI assessment", existing=existing)
    assert key == "chen2024ai"
    assert "chen2024ai" in existing

    key = make_citation_key(family="Chen", year=2024, title_hint="AI analysis", existing=existing)
    assert key == "chen2024aia"

    existing: set[str] = {"chen2024", "chen2024a", "chen2024b"}
    key = make_citation_key(family="Chen", year=2024, title_hint=None, existing=existing)

def test_parse_csl_name_institution_with_paren_marker():
    # Names wrapped in {} are CSL's literal-name marker (institution author).
    assert parse_csl_name("{World Health Organization}") == {"literal": "World Health Organization"}

def test_parse_csl_name_bare_single_token_literal():
    # A single token that does not look like "Family, Given" is treated as literal
    # only when followed by "(literal)" marker; otherwise treat as family name.
    assert parse_csl_name("Einstein") == {"family": "Einstein"}

def test_parse_semicolon_names():
    names = parse_semicolon_names("Chen, C.; Wang, J.")
    assert names == [
        {"family": "Chen", "given": "C."},
        {"family": "Wang", "given": "J."},
    ]

def test_parse_semicolon_names_empty_returns_empty_list():
    assert parse_semicolon_names("") == []
    assert parse_semicolon_names("   ") == []

def test_dump_yaml_stable_is_sorted():
    data = {"b": 2, "a": 1}
    out = dump_yaml_stable(data)
    # Keys serialized in sorted order
    assert out.index("a:") < out.index("b:")

    # "2026-04-23T10:11:12Z" or with microseconds
    assert ts.endswith("Z")
    assert "T" in ts
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `_common.py`**

Create `scripts/adapters/_common.py`:

```python
"""Shared helpers for ARS reference adapters.

These helpers are used by folder_scan.py, zotero.py, and obsidian.py.
They are also what a user-written adapter would copy and adapt.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import datetime
import io
import re
from typing import Any

import yaml

ADAPTER_SPEC_VERSION = "1.0.0"  # bump when overview.md contract changes

_NON_ALNUM = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+")
_TITLE_WORD = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]+")
_STOPWORDS = {
    "a", "an", "the", "of", "in", "on", "at", "by", "for", "to", "with",
    "and", "or", "but", "is", "are", "was", "were",
}

def sanitize_citation_key(raw: str) -> str:
    """Strip non-alphanumeric characters. Does NOT lowercase."""
    return _NON_ALNUM.sub("", raw)

def _first_title_word_non_stopword(title_hint: str | None) -> str:
    if not title_hint:
        return ""
    for word in _TITLE_WORD.findall(title_hint):
        if word.lower() not in _STOPWORDS:
            return word.lower()
    return ""

def make_citation_key(
    *, family: str, year: int, title_hint: str | None, existing: set[str]
) -> str:
    """Build a collision-safe citation key.

    Pattern: {family_lower}{year}{first_title_word_or_empty}. If that is
    already in `existing`, append `a`, `b`, `c`, ... (and then aa, ab, ...).
    The chosen key is added to `existing` by reference.
    """
    base = f"{family.lower()}{year}{_first_title_word_non_stopword(title_hint)}"
    base = sanitize_citation_key(base)
    if not base:
        base = "ref"

    if base not in existing:
        existing.add(base)
        return base

    # Collision — append suffix
    for suffix in _alpha_suffixes():
        candidate = f"{base}{suffix}"
        if candidate not in existing:
            existing.add(candidate)
            return candidate
    raise RuntimeError("exhausted citation key suffix space")  # practically unreachable

def _alpha_suffixes():
    """Yield 'a', 'b', ..., 'z', 'aa', 'ab', ..., 'zz'. Enough for plan purposes."""
    for c in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz":
        yield c
    for c1 in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz":
        for c2 in "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz":
            yield c1 + c2

def parse_csl_name(raw: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Parse a single name string into a CSL-JSON name object.

    Rules:
    - "{Institution Name}" → {"literal": "Institution Name"}
    - "Family, Given" → {"family": "Family", "given": "Given"}
    - "Family" (single token) → {"family": "Family"}
    """
    raw = raw.strip()
    if raw.startswith("{") and raw.endswith("}"):
        return {"literal": raw[1:-1].strip()}
    if "," in raw:
        family, _, given = raw.partition(",")
        return {"family": family.strip(), "given": given.strip()}
    return {"family": raw}

def parse_semicolon_names(raw: str) -> list[dict[str, str]]:
    """Parse 'A, B; C, D' into CSL name list."""
    raw = raw.strip()
    if not raw:
        return []
    return [parse_csl_name(part) for part in raw.split(";") if part.strip()]

def dump_yaml_stable(data: Any) -> str:
    """Dump YAML with sorted keys and deterministic formatting."""
    buf = io.StringIO()
    yaml.safe_dump(
        data,
        buf,
        sort_keys=True,
        default_flow_style=False,
        allow_unicode=True,
        width=1000,
    )
    return buf.getvalue()

def now_iso() -> str:
    """ISO 8601 in UTC with trailing 'Z'. Deterministic except for the time itself."""
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")

def write_passport(path, entries: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
    """Write passport.yaml with sorted literature_corpus entries."""
    sorted_entries = sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e.get("citation_key", ""))
    doc = {"literature_corpus": sorted_entries}
    path.write_text(dump_yaml_stable(doc), encoding="utf-8")

def write_rejection_log(
    path, *, adapter_name: str, adapter_version: str,
    rejected: list[dict[str, Any]], input_source: str | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Write rejection_log.yaml with sorted rejected[] by source."""
    sorted_rejected = sorted(rejected, key=lambda r: r.get("source", ""))
    doc: dict[str, Any] = {
        "adapter_name": adapter_name,
        "adapter_version": adapter_version,
        "generated_at": now_iso(),
        "rejected": sorted_rejected,
    }
    if input_source is not None:
        doc["input_source"] = input_source
    summary = {
        "total_accepted": doc.get("_accepted_hint", 0) if False else 0,  # set by caller when known
        "total_rejected": len(sorted_rejected),
    }
    doc["summary"] = {"total_rejected": len(sorted_rejected)}
    path.write_text(dump_yaml_stable(doc), encoding="utf-8")
```

## Task 6: `scripts/adapters/tests/conftest.py` test infrastructure

**Files:**
- Create: `scripts/adapters/tests/conftest.py`

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the conftest**

Create `scripts/adapters/tests/conftest.py`:

```python
"""pytest configuration + shared fixtures for adapter tests.

Provides:
- `repo_root` : Path to the ARS repo root
- `adapters_dir` : Path to scripts/adapters/
- `examples_dir` : Path to scripts/adapters/examples/
- `clean_timestamps(doc)` : helper that blanks `generated_at` and
   `obtained_at` fields so byte-identical comparisons are possible.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
from pathlib import Path
import copy
import pytest
import yaml

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def repo_root() -> Path:
    return REPO_ROOT

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def adapters_dir() -> Path:
    return REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters"

@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def examples_dir() -> Path:
    return REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples"

def _strip_keys(obj, keys_to_blank: set[str]):
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {
            k: ("<TIMESTAMP>" if k in keys_to_blank else _strip_keys(v, keys_to_blank))
            for k, v in obj.items()
        }
    if isinstance(obj, list):
        return [_strip_keys(v, keys_to_blank) for v in obj]
    return obj

@pytest.fixture
def clean_timestamps():
    """Return a function that returns a copy of a dict/list with all
    `generated_at` and `obtained_at` values blanked to '<TIMESTAMP>'. Used to
    compare adapter output against expected fixtures without flakiness."""
    def _clean(doc):
        return _strip_keys(copy.deepcopy(doc), {"generated_at", "obtained_at"})
    return _clean

@pytest.fixture
def load_yaml():
    """Return a function that loads a YAML file into a Python dict."""
    def _load(path: Path):
        with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return yaml.safe_load(f)
    return _load
```

```python
"""Tests for scripts/adapters/folder_scan.py."""
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
ADAPTER = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/folder_scan.py"
FIXTURE_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples/folder_scan/input_fixture"
EXPECTED_PASSPORT = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples/folder_scan/expected_passport.yaml"
EXPECTED_REJECTION = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples/folder_scan/expected_rejection_log.yaml"

def _run(*args, cwd=None):
    return subprocess.run(
        ["python", str(ADAPTER)] + list(args),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=cwd or REPO_ROOT,
    )

def test_adapter_exists():
    assert ADAPTER.exists()

def test_happy_path(tmp_path, load_yaml, clean_timestamps):
    passport_out = tmp_path / "passport.yaml"
    rejection_out = tmp_path / "rejection_log.yaml"
    r = _run(
        "--input", str(FIXTURE_DIR),
        "--passport", str(passport_out),
        "--rejection-log", str(rejection_out),
    )
    assert r.returncode == 0, r.stderr

    got = load_yaml(passport_out)
    expected = load_yaml(EXPECTED_PASSPORT)
    assert clean_timestamps(got) == clean_timestamps(expected)

    got_rej = load_yaml(rejection_out)
    expected_rej = load_yaml(EXPECTED_REJECTION)
    assert clean_timestamps(got_rej) == clean_timestamps(expected_rej)

def test_empty_folder_emits_empty_passport(tmp_path):
    empty = tmp_path / "empty"
    empty.mkdir()
    passport_out = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    rej_out = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    r = _run(
        "--input", str(empty),
        "--passport", str(passport_out),
        "--rejection-log", str(rej_out),
    )
    assert r.returncode == 0
    import yaml
    with passport_out.open() as f:
        doc = yaml.safe_load(f)
    assert doc == {"literature_corpus": []}

def test_missing_input_dir_fails_loud(tmp_path):
    r = _run(
        "--input", str(tmp_path / "does-not-exist"),
        "--passport", str(tmp_path / "p.yaml"),
        "--rejection-log", str(tmp_path / "r.yaml"),
    )
    assert r.returncode == 1
    assert "not found" in r.stderr.lower() or "exist" in r.stderr.lower()

def test_deterministic_output(tmp_path, load_yaml, clean_timestamps):
    p1 = tmp_path / "p1.yaml"
    r1_log = tmp_path / "r1.yaml"
    p2 = tmp_path / "p2.yaml"
    r2_log = tmp_path / "r2.yaml"
    _run("--input", str(FIXTURE_DIR), "--passport", str(p1), "--rejection-log", str(r1_log))
    _run("--input", str(FIXTURE_DIR), "--passport", str(p2), "--rejection-log", str(r2_log))
    assert clean_timestamps(load_yaml(p1)) == clean_timestamps(load_yaml(p2))
    assert clean_timestamps(load_yaml(r1_log)) == clean_timestamps(load_yaml(r2_log))

def test_duplicate_collision_handled(tmp_path):
    # Two files that would produce the same base citation_key should each be
    # accepted with a disambiguating suffix.
    dup_dir = tmp_path / "dup"
    dup_dir.mkdir()
    (dup_dir / "Smith2024_alpha.pdf").touch()
    (dup_dir / "Smith2024_beta.pdf").touch()
    passport_out = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    rej_out = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    r = _run(
        "--input", str(dup_dir),
        "--passport", str(passport_out),
        "--rejection-log", str(rej_out),
    )
    assert r.returncode == 0
    import yaml
    with passport_out.open() as f:
        doc = yaml.safe_load(f)
    keys = {e["citation_key"] for e in doc["literature_corpus"]}
    assert len(keys) == 2  # no collisions
```

The expected fixture will be regenerated relative to the actual fixture dir at test time via a helper; do NOT hardcode the path. - [ ] **Step 5: Implement `folder_scan.py`**

Create `scripts/adapters/folder_scan.py`:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""folder_scan: produce a literature_corpus passport from a directory of
files (typically PDFs). Parses citation metadata from filenames using
best-effort conventions. Never parses PDF content.

Filename conventions recognized:
  - {Family}{Year}{optional_title_slug}.{ext}
  - {Family}_{Year}_{title_slug}.{ext}
  - fallback: first capitalized Latin word before the year.

Files whose filename cannot be parsed for both family and year are rejected.
Non-Latin filenames (e.g. CJK characters) are rejected; Unicode filename
support is a future extension opportunity.

Usage:
  python scripts/adapters/folder_scan.py \
      --input <dir> --passport <out.yaml> --rejection-log <out.yaml>
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from scripts.adapters._common import (
    ADAPTER_SPEC_VERSION,
    make_citation_key,
    write_passport,
    write_rejection_log,
    now_iso,
)

ADAPTER_NAME = "folder_scan.py"
ADAPTER_VERSION = "1.0.0"

# Family{Year} style: "Chen2024..."
RE_FAMILY_YEAR = re.compile(r"^([A-Z][A-Za-z]*)\s*((?:19|20)\d{2})\s*[_\-.\s]?(.*?)\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$")
# Family_Year_title style
RE_FAMILY_UNDERSCORE = re.compile(r"^([A-Z][A-Za-z]*)_((?:19|20)\d{2})(?:_(.*?))?\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$")
# fallback year anywhere
RE_ANY_YEAR = re.compile(r"((?:19|20)\d{2})")
RE_FIRST_CAPITAL = re.compile(r"\b([A-Z][A-Za-z]+)\b")

# Reject entries with any non-ASCII char in the filename stem
RE_NON_ASCII = re.compile(r"[^\x00-\x7f]")

def parse_filename(name: str) -> dict | None:
    """Return {'family', 'year', 'title'} or None if unparseable."""
    if RE_NON_ASCII.search(name):
        return None

    m = RE_FAMILY_UNDERSCORE.match(name)
    if m:
        family, year, tail = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), (m.group(3) or "").strip()
        title = tail.replace("_", " ").strip() or f"{family} {year} {tail}".strip()
        return {"family": family, "year": year, "title": f"{family} {year} {tail}".strip()}

    m = RE_FAMILY_YEAR.match(name)
    if m:
        family, year, tail = m.group(1), int(m.group(2)), (m.group(3) or "").strip()
        stem = Path(name).stem
        return {"family": family, "year": year, "title": stem.replace("_", " ")}

    year_match = RE_ANY_YEAR.search(name)
    fam_match = RE_FIRST_CAPITAL.search(name.split(str(int(year_match.group(1))))[0] if year_match else "")
    if year_match and fam_match:
        return {
            "family": fam_match.group(1),
            "year": int(year_match.group(1)),
            "title": Path(name).stem.replace("_", " "),
        }
    return None

def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True, help="Directory to scan")
    ap.add_argument("--passport", type=Path, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--rejection-log", dest="rejection_log", type=Path, required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    if not args.input.exists() or not args.input.is_dir():
        print(f"ERROR: input directory not found: {args.input}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    entries: list[dict] = []
    rejected: list[dict] = []
    existing_keys: set[str] = set()

    files = sorted(p for p in args.input.rglob("*") if p.is_file() and p.name != ".gitkeep")
    for f in files:
        parsed = parse_filename(f.name)
        if not parsed:
            missing = []
            if RE_NON_ASCII.search(f.name):
                missing = ["authors"]
            elif not RE_ANY_YEAR.search(f.name):
                missing = ["authors", "year"]
            else:
                missing = ["authors"]
            rejected.append({
                "source": f.name,
                "reason": "authors_unparseable",
                "raw": f.name,
                "missing_fields": missing,
            })
            continue

        title_hint = parsed["title"]
        citation_key = make_citation_key(
            family=parsed["family"],
            year=parsed["year"],
            title_hint=title_hint,
            existing=existing_keys,
        )
        entries.append({
            "citation_key": citation_key,
            "title": title_hint,
            "authors": [{"family": parsed["family"]}],
            "year": parsed["year"],
            "source_pointer": f"file://{f.resolve()}",
            "obtained_via": "folder-scan",
            "obtained_at": now_iso(),
            "adapter_name": ADAPTER_NAME,
            "adapter_version": ADAPTER_VERSION,
        })

    write_passport(args.passport, entries)
    write_rejection_log(
        args.rejection_log,
        adapter_name=ADAPTER_NAME,
        adapter_version=ADAPTER_VERSION,
        rejected=rejected,
        input_source=str(args.input),
    )
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```


```python
"""Tests for scripts/adapters/zotero.py."""
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import json
import yaml
import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
ADAPTER = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/zotero.py"
FIXTURE_INPUT = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples/zotero/input_fixture/export.json"
EXPECTED_PASSPORT = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples/zotero/expected_passport.yaml"
EXPECTED_REJECTION = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples/zotero/expected_rejection_log.yaml"

def _run(*args):
    return subprocess.run(
        ["python", str(ADAPTER)] + list(args),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
    )

def test_adapter_exists():
    assert ADAPTER.exists()

def test_happy_path(tmp_path, load_yaml, clean_timestamps):
    p = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    r = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    res = _run("--input", str(FIXTURE_INPUT), "--passport", str(p), "--rejection-log", str(r))
    assert res.returncode == 0, res.stderr
    assert clean_timestamps(load_yaml(p)) == clean_timestamps(load_yaml(EXPECTED_PASSPORT))
    assert clean_timestamps(load_yaml(r)) == clean_timestamps(load_yaml(EXPECTED_REJECTION))

def test_malformed_json_fails_loud(tmp_path):
    bad = tmp_path / "bad.json"
    bad.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
    p = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    r = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    res = _run("--input", str(bad), "--passport", str(p), "--rejection-log", str(r))
    assert res.returncode == 1
    assert "json" in res.stderr.lower() or "parse" in res.stderr.lower()

def test_empty_array_emits_empty_passport(tmp_path, load_yaml):
    empty = tmp_path / "empty.json"
    empty.write_text("[]", encoding="utf-8")
    p = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    r = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    res = _run("--input", str(empty), "--passport", str(p), "--rejection-log", str(r))
    assert res.returncode == 0
    doc = load_yaml(p)
    assert doc == {"literature_corpus": []}

def test_institution_author_preserved(tmp_path, load_yaml):
    data = [
        {
            "citationKey": "who2024",
            "itemType": "report",
            "title": "World report",
            "creators": [{"creatorType": "author", "name": "World Health Organization"}],
            "date": "2024",
            "itemID": "AAAA1111",
        }
    ]
    infile = tmp_path / "i.json"
    infile.write_text(json.dumps(data), encoding="utf-8")
    p = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    r = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    res = _run("--input", str(infile), "--passport", str(p), "--rejection-log", str(r))
    assert res.returncode == 0
    doc = load_yaml(p)
    assert doc["literature_corpus"][0]["authors"] == [{"literal": "World Health Organization"}]

def test_no_authors_rejected(tmp_path, load_yaml):
    data = [
        {
            "citationKey": "anon2024",
            "itemType": "journalArticle",
            "title": "Untitled",
            "creators": [{"creatorType": "editor", "firstName": "A", "lastName": "B"}],
            "date": "2024",
            "itemID": "BBBB1111",
        }
    ]
    infile = tmp_path / "i.json"
    infile.write_text(json.dumps(data), encoding="utf-8")
    p = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    r = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    res = _run("--input", str(infile), "--passport", str(p), "--rejection-log", str(r))
    assert res.returncode == 0
    pp = load_yaml(p)
    rr = load_yaml(r)
    assert pp["literature_corpus"] == []
    assert len(rr["rejected"]) == 1
    assert rr["rejected"][0]["reason"] == "authors_unparseable"

def test_unparseable_date_rejected(tmp_path, load_yaml):
    data = [
        {
            "citationKey": "fwd2024",
            "itemType": "journalArticle",
            "title": "Forthcoming",
            "creators": [{"creatorType": "author", "firstName": "A", "lastName": "B"}],
            "date": "forthcoming",
            "itemID": "CCCC1111",
        }
    ]
    infile = tmp_path / "i.json"
    infile.write_text(json.dumps(data), encoding="utf-8")
    p = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    r = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    res = _run("--input", str(infile), "--passport", str(p), "--rejection-log", str(r))
    assert res.returncode == 0
    rr = load_yaml(r)
    assert rr["rejected"][0]["reason"] == "year_unparseable"
```

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement `zotero.py`**

Create `scripts/adapters/zotero.py`:

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""zotero: produce a literature_corpus passport from a Better BibTeX
Extension JSON export. Reads only local files; does not call the Zotero
Web API.

See design doc §5.3. Users who want a live-sync API-based variant are
expected to write their own adapter using this file as a starting point
(see overview.md extension-point guidance).

Usage:
  python scripts/adapters/zotero.py \
      --input <bbt_export.json> --passport <out.yaml> --rejection-log <out.yaml>
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from scripts.adapters._common import (
    write_passport,
    write_rejection_log,
    now_iso,
)

ADAPTER_NAME = "zotero.py"
ADAPTER_VERSION = "1.0.0"

RE_YEAR = re.compile(r"\b((?:19|20)\d{2})\b")

def extract_authors(creators: list[dict]) -> list[dict] | None:
    """Pull only author-type creators. Return CSL-name list or None when no authors."""
    out: list[dict] = []
    for c in creators or []:
        if c.get("creatorType") != "author":
            continue
        if "name" in c:  # institution / corporate author
            out.append({"literal": c["name"].strip()})
            continue
        family = (c.get("lastName") or "").strip()
        given = (c.get("firstName") or "").strip()
        if not family:
            continue
        entry = {"family": family}
        if given:
            entry["given"] = given
        out.append(entry)
    return out if out else None

def extract_year(date_str: str) -> int | None:
    if not date_str:
        return None
    m = RE_YEAR.search(date_str)
    if m:
        return int(m.group(1))
    return None

def strip_doi(doi: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not doi:
        return None
    doi = doi.strip()
    for prefix in ("doi:", "DOI:", "https://doi.org/", "http://doi.org/"):
        if doi.lower().startswith(prefix.lower()):
            doi = doi[len(prefix):]
            break
    return doi.strip() or None

def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--input", type=Path, required=True, help="BBT JSON export file")
    ap.add_argument("--passport", type=Path, required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--rejection-log", dest="rejection_log", type=Path, required=True)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    try:
        raw = args.input.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    except FileNotFoundError:
        print(f"ERROR: input not found: {args.input}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    try:
        data = json.loads(raw)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        print(f"ERROR: input is not valid JSON: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not isinstance(data, list):
        print(f"ERROR: expected top-level JSON array, got {type(data).__name__}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    entries: list[dict] = []
    rejected: list[dict] = []

    for item in data:
        citekey = item.get("citationKey") or ""
        item_id = item.get("itemID") or ""
        source_key = item_id or citekey or "<unknown>"

        authors = extract_authors(item.get("creators", []))
        year = extract_year(item.get("date", ""))

        missing: list[str] = []
        if not authors:
            missing.append("authors")
        if not year:
            missing.append("year")

        if missing:
            reason = "authors_unparseable" if "authors" in missing else "year_unparseable"
            rejected.append({
                "source": source_key,
                "reason": reason,
                "raw": item,
                "missing_fields": missing,
            })
            continue

        venue = (
            item.get("publicationTitle")
            or item.get("proceedingsTitle")
            or item.get("bookTitle")
            or None
        )

        entry: dict = {
            "citation_key": citekey,
            "title": item.get("title", "").strip(),
            "authors": authors,
            "year": year,
            "source_pointer": f"zotero://select/items/0_{item_id}" if item_id else f"zotero://select/items/@{citekey}",
            "obtained_via": "zotero-bbt-export",
            "obtained_at": now_iso(),
            "adapter_name": ADAPTER_NAME,
            "adapter_version": ADAPTER_VERSION,
        }
        if venue:
            entry["venue"] = venue
        doi = strip_doi(item.get("DOI"))
        if doi:
            entry["doi"] = doi
        tags = [t.get("tag") for t in item.get("tags", []) if t.get("tag")]
        if tags:
            entry["tags"] = tags
        abstract = item.get("abstractNote")
        if abstract:
            entry["abstract"] = abstract
        notes = item.get("notes") or []
        if notes:
            plain = "\n\n".join(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", n.get("note", "")) for n in notes if n.get("note"))
            if plain.strip():
                entry["user_notes"] = plain

        entries.append(entry)

    write_passport(args.passport, entries)
    write_rejection_log(
        args.rejection_log,
        adapter_name=ADAPTER_NAME,
        adapter_version=ADAPTER_VERSION,
        rejected=rejected,
        input_source=str(args.input),
    )
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```


```python
"""Tests for scripts/adapters/obsidian.py."""
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import pytest

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
ADAPTER = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/obsidian.py"
VAULT = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples/obsidian/input_fixture/vault"
EXPECTED_PASSPORT = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples/obsidian/expected_passport.yaml"
EXPECTED_REJECTION = REPO_ROOT / "scripts/adapters/examples/obsidian/expected_rejection_log.yaml"

def _run(*args):
    return subprocess.run(
        ["python", str(ADAPTER)] + list(args),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        cwd=REPO_ROOT,
    )

def test_adapter_exists():
    assert ADAPTER.exists()

def test_happy_path(tmp_path, load_yaml, clean_timestamps):
    p = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    r = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    res = _run("--input", str(VAULT), "--passport", str(p), "--rejection-log", str(r))
    assert res.returncode == 0, res.stderr
    assert clean_timestamps(load_yaml(p)) == clean_timestamps(load_yaml(EXPECTED_PASSPORT))
    assert clean_timestamps(load_yaml(r)) == clean_timestamps(load_yaml(EXPECTED_REJECTION))

def test_missing_vault_fails_loud(tmp_path):
    p = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    r = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    res = _run("--input", str(tmp_path / "nope"), "--passport", str(p), "--rejection-log", str(r))
    assert res.returncode == 1

def test_templates_dir_skipped(tmp_path, load_yaml):
    vault = tmp_path / "v"
    (vault / "_templates").mkdir(parents=True)
    (vault / "_templates/tmpl.md").write_text(
        "---\ncitekey: tmpl2024\ntitle: T\nauthors:\n  - family: X\nyear: 2024\n---\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    (vault / "note.md").write_text(
        "---\ncitekey: note2024\ntitle: Real\nauthors:\n  - family: Y\nyear: 2024\n---\nbody\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    p = tmp_path / "p.yaml"
    r = tmp_path / "r.yaml"
    res = _run("--input", str(vault), "--passport", str(p), "--rejection-log", str(r))
    assert res.returncode == 0
    doc = load_yaml(p)
    keys = [e["citation_key"] for e in doc["literature_corpus"]]
    assert "tmpl2024" not in keys
    assert "note2024" in keys

def test_obsidian_dir_skipped(tmp_path, load_yaml):
    vault = tmp_path / "v"
    (vault / ".obsidian").mkdir(parents=True)
    (vault / ".obsidian/ignored.md").write_text(
        "---\ncitekey: skip2024\ntitle: T\nauthors:\n  - family: X\nyear: 2024\n---\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    (vault / "real.md").write_text(
        "---\ncitekey: real2024\ntitle: R\nauthors:\n  - family: Y\nyear: 2024\n---\n",

    )

    doc = load_yaml(p)
    keys = [e["citation_key"] for e in doc["literature_corpus"]]
    assert "skip2024" not in keys
    assert "real2024" in keys
```
