## §2 — Findings to fix in v3.6.5.1

Source: local Codex audit on `docs/SETUP.md` 2026-04-27.

### F1 (P0) — `docs/SETUP.md:213-229` Method 3 wrong path

**Problem**: Current Option A says clone repo to `.claude/skills/academic-research-skills/`. This produces:

```
.claude/skills/academic-research-skills/deep-research/SKILL.md   ← buried, not discovered
```

instead of the required:

```
.claude/skills/deep-research/SKILL.md   ← Cowork finds this
```

Same problem in Option B if it follows the same pattern.

**Authoritative source**: Claude Code Skills paths and discovery convention — https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills

**Fix**: Rewrite Option A and Option B to install each of the four skill folders separately into `.claude/skills/`. Two acceptable approaches:

- **Option A — symlink (fastest, single-machine)**: `git clone` repo to a stable path (e.g. `~/academic-research-skills`), then `ln -s <repo>/<skill-name> ~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>` for each of the four skills. Must include a caveat: if the user syncs `~/.claude/skills` across machines via cloud folders, prefer `cp -R` because absolute-path symlinks break on a fresh checkout (this is a real ARS lesson from `feedback_relative_symlinks_in_repos.md`).
- **Option B — copy (cross-machine safe, no auto-update)**: `git clone` repo, then `cp -R <repo>/<skill-name> ~/.claude/skills/<skill-name>` for each of the four skills. Note that updates require re-running cp.

The four skill folder names are exact: `deep-research`, `academic-paper`, `academic-paper-reviewer`, `academic-pipeline`. Use bash code blocks with explicit per-skill commands.

**Hard rule on consolidation** (resolves apparent conflict with §8 drafter judgement zone): the drafter MAY consolidate Option A and Option B into a single section if it improves readability, BUT every final command must name all four skill folders explicitly. No `for skill in ...` loop, no parameterised one-liner, no "repeat for each skill" instruction without showing each command. Reason: readers copy-paste in a hurry and skip iteration syntax; explicit four-line blocks have ~zero misuse rate.

### F2 (P0) — `docs/SETUP.md:237` Method 4 conceptually wrong

**Problem**: Current text says "use these skills on claude.ai via the Project feature with GitHub integration". This frames GitHub integration as a Skill install path. It is not — GitHub integration loads files into Project knowledge (static retrieval context), not the Skills system. Skill auto-loading and trigger phrase routing do not happen via this method.

**Authoritative sources**:
- Projects (claude.ai static knowledge): https://support.claude.com/en/articles/9517075-what-are-projects
- GitHub integration: https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10167454-using-the-github-integration
- Custom Skills packaging (zip per skill, ≤200-char description): https://claude.com/docs/skills/how-to

**Fix**: Restructure Method 4 into two clearly labelled sub-methods. Use neutral framing — neither is "recommended" right now (4a is blocked on v3.6.5.2; 4b is documented-but-limited):

- **Method 4a — Custom Skill upload (claude.ai's standard Skill install path)**: Settings → Capabilities → Skills, upload one zip per skill (the zip's top-level entry must be `<skill-name>/SKILL.md`, matching the `name` field in the skill's frontmatter). **State the current blocker explicitly**: the four skill `description` fields in this repo currently exceed the 200-char cap and would be rejected by the upload UI; the description trim ships in patch v3.6.5.2 immediately after this v3.6.5.1 doc patch. The path is documented here so the install instructions are correct in advance; until v3.6.5.2 ships, prefer Methods 1, 2, or 3.
- **Method 4b — Project + GitHub integration (fallback knowledge mode, not a Skill install)**: GitHub integration loads files into Project knowledge for retrieval. **Explicitly state**: "this is NOT a Skill install. Skill auto-loading does not happen. Trigger phrases do not route. Claude can read the repo content but does not execute the skills as agentic workflows. Useful when you want claude.ai to have access to the repo content for reading/citation but you do not need agentic skill execution."

- Paid plan: Pro, Max, Team, or Enterprise (cite the Cowork article above for current plan availability — do not paraphrase the plan list, link to it because Anthropic adjusts plan tiers)

### F6 (P2) — `docs/SETUP.md:231` Trigger phrase oversimplified

**Problem**: Current text says skills are invoked "via trigger phrases". True but incomplete — Cowork now also surfaces installed plugin Skills via the `/` command palette and the `+` (add capability) visual UI. The audit also notes that "trigger phrase" is itself a slight overstatement: Claude uses the skill description to decide relevance, not literal trigger-phrase matching.

**Authoritative sources**:
- Skills invocation (Claude uses description for relevance, not literal trigger matching): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
- Cowork Skills via plugins (`/` and `+` UI): https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13837440-use-plugins-in-claude-cowork

**Fix**: List three discovery surfaces and correct the trigger-phrase framing:

- Description-based relevance (the primary mechanism, per Claude Code Skills doc): Claude reads each skill's `description` and routes the user request to whichever skill it judges most relevant. The example phrases in the SETUP table are illustrative, not literal triggers.
- `/` command palette in Cowork: type `/` and the four skills appear as completions for explicit invocation.
- `+` capability picker in Cowork: visual UI to add a skill to the current Task.

Reader should know that explicit `/` and `+` UI exist as a fallback when description-based routing does not pick the desired skill, and that paraphrased intent ("help me draft a paper") works equally well as the example phrases.

**Fix**:

- Rewrite the capacity section: state current Anthropic Project limits per the linked page (file count is not artificially capped at 200; per-file 30 MB; total subject to context-window limits at runtime). ## §5 — Validation gate

Validation has two tiers: **required (filesystem path-shape)** and **optional (live discovery)**. Required must pass before opening PR; optional is documented when environment supports it, otherwise reported as "not validated in this run" without blocking ship.

### 5.0 Environment protection (mandatory before any validation)

The drafter / validator MUST NOT pollute the developer's real `~/.claude/skills` while validating instructions. Two acceptable approaches:

- **Disposable HOME**: `tmpdir=$(mktemp -d)` then run validation steps with `HOME=$tmpdir`. Filesystem checks resolve against `$tmpdir/.claude/skills/`. Cleanup is `rm -rf $tmpdir` when done.
- **Backup + restore**: `mv ~/.claude/skills ~/.claude/skills.backup-pre-v3.6.5.1-validation`, run validation, then `rm -rf ~/.claude/skills && mv ~/.claude/skills.backup-pre-v3.6.5.1-validation ~/.claude/skills` after. Riskier — if the validation step fails partway, the backup might not get restored. Disposable HOME is preferred.

Document which approach was used in the validation report.

### 5.1 Required: filesystem path-shape validation

These steps verify that the corrected SETUP.md instructions produce the right paths on disk. They do NOT require Claude Desktop, Claude Code session, Cowork, or claude.ai access.

For each install method below, run the exact commands from the v3.6.5.1 SETUP.md draft (no edits, no shortcuts) inside the protected environment from §5.0:

1. **Method 1 (project skills)**: confirm `<project>/.claude/skills/deep-research/SKILL.md` exists at the expected path and is the file from the repo (not a placeholder). Repeat for the other three skills.
2. **Method 3 Option A (symlink)**: confirm `~/.claude/skills/deep-research/SKILL.md` resolves (test with `test -f`, not `ls -L`, to follow symlinks). Confirm `readlink` shows the absolute path back to the cloned repo. Repeat for all four skills.
3. **Method 3 Option B (copy)**: confirm `~/.claude/skills/deep-research/SKILL.md` exists, is a regular file (not symlink), and content matches `<repo>/deep-research/SKILL.md` (e.g. `diff` returns 0). Repeat for all four skills.

All three must pass. If any path-shape check fails, the SETUP.md instructions are still wrong and the rewrite is not done.

### 5.2 Optional: live discovery validation

These steps verify that platforms actually discover the installed skills. Run them only when the corresponding platform is available; otherwise mark as "not validated in this run" in the validation report.

4. **Method 1 live**: open Claude Code in the project directory, start a session, confirm the four skills appear in the available-skills list. (Available if Claude Code is installed locally.)
5. **Method 3 live (Cowork)**: with the protected `$HOME` from §5.0 set as the active HOME for the Claude Desktop session, restart Claude Desktop, switch to Cowork mode, confirm the four skills appear under the `+` capability picker. (Available only if Claude Desktop is installed and Cowork is enabled on the account.)
6. **Method 4a live**: zip one skill folder per the SETUP.md instructions, attempt upload via Settings → Capabilities → Skills. Expected outcome **before v3.6.5.2 ships**: rejection with a description-too-long error, which validates that the documented upload path is the right one and that v3.6.5.2 description trim is the correct unblocker.
7. **Method 4b live**: connect a claude.ai Project to the GitHub repo per Method 4b instructions, confirm the file tree appears in Project knowledge and is selectable for Claude to read.

### 5.3 Validation report format

The validation report is a Markdown block included in the PR description (or attached as a file under `examples/v3.6.5.1-validation/` if it is large). Required content:

- Which §5.0 environment-protection approach was used
- For each of steps 1-3: PASS / FAIL with the exact command output that proves it
- For each of steps 4-7: PASS / FAIL / NOT VALIDATED (reason: e.g. "no Claude Desktop on validation machine"). Marking "NOT VALIDATED" is acceptable for steps 4-7; it is not acceptable for steps 1-3.

Open the PR only after steps 1-3 pass. Steps 4-7 results inform reviewers but do not block.

## §6 — Codex review iteration

After the SETUP.md draft is complete (and sweep is done):

1. Bundle the draft + this brief + the original audit findings into a single file.
2. Run `codex exec --sandbox read-only` with a verification task: "Apply the v3.6.5.1 brief constraints; flag any deviation. Output severity-tagged findings."
3. Iterate fixes; re-run Codex.

**Ship gate** (refined from `feedback_codex_iterative_spec_review_to_zero.md` discipline for the doc-patch context):

- **Zero P1 and zero P2 findings**: required. Every P1 and P2 finding must be fixed before ship. No "reject with rationale" path for P1/P2 — they are blockers by definition. If a Codex P1 or P2 is technically wrong (e.g. Codex misread the brief), the response is to clarify the brief or argue the finding back, not to declare it rejected and ship.
- **P3 findings**: either fixed, OR accepted with one-line rationale in the PR description (e.g. "P3 wording preference declined: deviates from the user's vetted issue #44 phrasing"). P3 wording or stylistic findings should not block ship indefinitely; rejection-with-rationale is the P3-only escape hatch.
- The "zero findings" phrasing was developed for high-blast-radius schema/contract spec (e.g. v3.6.2 sprint contract) where any drift could cascade through validators and runtime. SETUP.md is moderate blast radius (broken instructions harm new users but do not corrupt data); P3 acceptance is the correct trade-off here. P1/P2 are non-negotiable in both contexts.

Reviewing prose against a brief is what Codex is good at; reviewing prose against vague stylistic preferences is not. Keep the brief as the contract. When Codex raises a P3 that the brief does not actually constrain, accept-with-rationale rather than re-engineering the brief mid-iteration.

Do NOT reference internal terminology (e.g. "blast radius", "Codex second-opinion"). PR is public-facing.

These are explicitly delegated; no follow-up question needed.

# ARS v3.6.5.2 — claude.ai Method 4a scope clarification — Implementation Brief

Source: https://github.com/imbad0202/academic-research-skills/blob/main/docs/design/2026-04-27-ars-v3.6.5.2-claude-ai-method-4a-scope-implementation-brief.md

# ARS v3.6.5.2 — claude.ai Method 4a scope clarification — Implementation Brief

**Date**: 2026-04-27
**Target release**: v3.6.5.2 (patch, doc-only)
**Branch**: `hotfix/v3.6.5.2-clarify-claude-ai-method-4a-scope`
**Trigger**: GitHub issue #44 (philpav, 2026-04-27) — second half of the issue, originally planned as a `SKILL.md` description trim under claude.ai's 200-character cap. Repositioned 2026-04-27 after design re-examination.
**Author**: Cheng-I Wu

## Purpose of this document

This brief is the constraint sheet for v3.6.5.2 in its repositioned form. v3.6.5.2 was originally going to trim four `SKILL.md` `description` fields below 200 characters so claude.ai's Custom Skills upload UI would accept them. After examining what claude.ai's Method 4a actually offers for this suite versus what trimming costs the platforms ARS was built for (Claude Code and Cowork), the trim direction was abandoned. v3.6.5.2 instead documents that Method 4a is not a recommended path for this suite, points users at the paths that work, and closes issue #44.

This brief replaces the obsolete `2026-04-27-ars-v3.6.5.2-description-trim-implementation-brief.md` (deleted on the branch before this brief was committed).

## §1 — Why the trim direction was abandoned

The earlier plan was: trim each of the four `description` fields from their current 440-842 characters down to ≤200, add a CI lint to prevent regression. This would unblock claude.ai Custom Skills upload (Method 4a). Three findings stopped that plan.

### 1.1 The 200-char cap is a claude.ai client limit, not a spec limit

The Agent Skills specification (https://agentskills.io/specification) allows `description` up to **1024 characters**. Claude Code Skills follows the spec ceiling, with a separate 1,536-character listing budget for combined description + when_to_use (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills). Only claude.ai's Custom Skills upload UI enforces 200 (https://claude.com/docs/skills/how-to). Trimming to 200 across the suite means the strictest client dictates what every client sees.

### 1.2 Trimming would lose Claude Code / Cowork routing signal

ARS is a Claude Code-native suite. The four current descriptions front-load function, modes, and trigger keywords because Claude reads `description` to decide which skill to load when the user types a request. The four skills span related territory (research, write, review, orchestrate) and need discriminating language to route correctly. Trimming from 440-842 to 200 across the board removes routing-relevant content that Claude Code and Cowork actually use, in exchange for unblocking a path described in 1.3.

### 1.3 Method 4a's runtime scope is narrower than Claude Code's

claude.ai Custom Skills support multi-file packages with `scripts/` and code execution per Anthropic's [Custom Skills documentation](https://claude.com/docs/skills/how-to) and [How to create custom Skills](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512198-how-to-create-custom-skills), so Method 4a is mechanically capable of hosting skills with executable assets. The gap relevant here is not "no scripts" — it is that ARS depends on Claude Code-specific orchestration features that the Anthropic-documented claude.ai Custom Skill runtime does not include:

- **Claude Code Task / subagent dispatch**. Each ARS skill drives 12-13 specialised agents through Claude Code's Task / Skill tooling. The Anthropic [Use Skills in Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512180-use-skills-in-claude) doc describes claude.ai skill activation but does not document multi-agent dispatch via Task / subagent on the claude.ai surface.
- **Material Passport cross-session handoffs**. ARS pipelines record state in a Material Passport YAML and resume across Claude Code sessions. claude.ai's containerised code-execution environment is per-session; cross-session passport resume is not part of the documented Method 4a contract.

Method 4a is therefore expected to surface ARS as the SKILL.md body's instructions plus whatever scripts the runtime can execute in one session, without the multi-agent dispatch and cross-session continuation that produce the suite's actual outputs. This is a forward-looking assessment based on the documented claude.ai runtime scope, not a measured failure — we have not run a live upload to characterise the actual surfacing.

### 1.4 Method 4b remains valid for claude.ai users

Method 4b (claude.ai Project + GitHub integration) brings the entire repo into Project knowledge for retrieval. It is not a Skill install; Claude reads the files for context and citation. For users who want claude.ai to know ARS rather than execute it, Method 4b works without any description trimming.

## §2 — What v3.6.5.2 ships

### 2.1 SETUP.md Method 4a section rewrite

Replace the current Method 4a section (which currently says "blocked on v3.6.5.2 description trim, prefer Methods 1-3 until then") with a recommendation against Method 4a for this suite. The replacement should:

- State plainly: Method 4a is the standard claude.ai Skill install path, but it is not the recommended path for ARS.
- Give the rationale at one paragraph of depth (mirror §1.2 + §1.3 in user-readable form). Do not link to this brief — the rationale must be self-contained for a reader who arrives via the SETUP doc.
- Point users at alternatives: Method 3 (Cowork) for agentic skill execution on desktop; Method 4b (Project + GitHub) for claude.ai web access without Skill install. Method 1 and Method 2 remain the primary paths for Claude Code projects.
- Keep the install commands present in the section (the `zip -r` block, the upload step list) so a user who decides to try Method 4a anyway has the instructions. Frame the commands as "if you want to try this path despite the limitations" rather than as the recommended flow.
- Drop the inline phrasing "the description trim ships in a follow-up patch (v3.6.5.2)". That sentence was a v3.6.5.1-era forward-promise. v3.6.5.2 is no longer that patch; the sentence is obsolete and misleading.

### 2.2 SETUP.zh-TW.md Method 4a section mirror

Mirror the §2.1 changes in Traditional Chinese. Match the existing zh-TW translation's voice (no AI-style connectors, no over-use of em dash, no "吾人").

### 2.3 CHANGELOG.md v3.6.5.2 entry

Append above the v3.6.5.1 entry. Cover:

- What changed: SETUP.md + SETUP.zh-TW.md Method 4a recommendation
- Why: rationale summary (~3 lines)
- Note that no SKILL.md, no agent file, no schema, no script, no test changed
- Reference issue #44 with closure deferred to post-merge consolidated reply

### 2.4 What v3.6.5.2 does NOT change

- No `SKILL.md` (frontmatter, body, metadata) anywhere
- No `.claude/CLAUDE.md` (Skills Overview table stays)
- No `MODE_REGISTRY.md`
- No agent file under `*/agents/`
- No schema under `shared/`
- No script under `scripts/` (no new lint, no edits to existing lints)

- No version bumps anywhere (the four skill semvers stay; the suite semver in `.claude/CLAUDE.md` Version Info stays at 3.6.5)

The patch is exclusively `docs/SETUP.md`, `docs/SETUP.zh-TW.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and this brief itself.

## §5 — Validation gate

This patch is doc-only. Validation is light.

### 5.1 Required: link check

For every URL introduced or retained in `docs/SETUP.md`, `docs/SETUP.zh-TW.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md`, run:

```bash
for f in docs/SETUP.md docs/SETUP.zh-TW.md CHANGELOG.md; do
  grep -oE "https?://[^ )\"]+" "$f"
done | sort -u | while read url; do
  curl -sIL -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective}\n" "$url" --max-time 10
done
```

Expected: every link returns 200 (or a documented redirect to a 200). Anthropic support article URLs occasionally rewrite; if a redirect lands on a working article, that is fine.

### 5.2 Required: EN anchor link check

`docs/SETUP.md` introduces in-document anchor links to `#method-1-…`, `#method-2-…`, `#method-3-…`, `#method-4b-…`. GitHub computes anchors from heading text by lowercasing, replacing spaces with `-`, and stripping most punctuation. For each `[text](#anchor)` in `docs/SETUP.md`, confirm a matching `## ` or `### ` or `#### ` heading exists whose computed slug equals the anchor. `docs/SETUP.zh-TW.md` deliberately does not use anchor links because Chinese-character slug behaviour is fragile across renderers; this is intentional and not a finding.

### 5.3 Required: claim-source matrix for Method 4a runtime statements

Any sentence in `docs/SETUP.md`, `docs/SETUP.zh-TW.md`, or `CHANGELOG.md` that describes claude.ai Custom Skill runtime behaviour (what it can host, what it cannot dispatch, how `description` is enforced, what plans support it) must either (a) cite a specific Anthropic doc URL whose current content supports the claim, or (b) state explicitly that the claim is forward-looking and based on documented orchestration assumptions rather than measured behaviour. The drafter compiles a small matrix per claim — claim → source URL or "forward-looking, no live validation" — and includes it in the validation report. Claims that fail both (a) and (b) must be cut or rewritten.

### 5.4 Required: prose self-check

The drafter rereads §2.1's replacement Method 4a section and confirms:

1. A reader arriving cold (no prior context) understands that Method 4a is technically possible but not recommended.
2. The rationale answers "why not" without requiring the reader to read this brief.
3. The alternative paths (Method 3, Method 4b) are pointed at clearly.
4. The install commands are still present for a user who wants to try Method 4a, including the zip-root packaging constraint.

Document this self-check as a one-paragraph note in the validation report.

### 5.5 Required: zh-TW prose mirror

Diff §2.2 zh-TW changes against §2.1 EN changes. Confirm:

- Same structural sections present
- Same factual claims made (especially the runtime-limitation claims must mirror, not drift)
- Voice is consistent with existing SETUP.zh-TW.md

### 5.6 Optional: live test

If the validator has claude.ai access: try uploading one ARS skill via Method 4a. Expected: rejection with description-too-long error, confirming the upload constraint is real and that the SETUP doc's recommendation is grounded. Mark NOT VALIDATED if no claude.ai access.

### 5.7 Validation report format

Markdown block in PR description:

- §5.1 link check across all three docs: PASS/FAIL per URL
- §5.2 EN anchor link check: PASS/FAIL per anchor
- §5.3 claim-source matrix: each runtime claim with source URL or "forward-looking" note
- §5.4 prose self-check: paragraph per the four sub-questions
- §5.5 zh-TW mirror: PASS/FAIL with diff summary
- §5.6 live upload: PASS/NOT VALIDATED with reason

# ARS v3.6.6 — Generator/Evaluator Sprint Contract Design

Source: https://github.com/imbad0202/academic-research-skills/blob/main/docs/design/2026-04-27-ars-v3.6.6-generator-evaluator-contract-design.md

# ARS v3.6.6 — Generator/Evaluator Sprint Contract Design

**Date**: 2026-04-27
**Target release**: v3.6.6 (academic-paper full-mode writer/evaluator sprint contract)
**Roadmap anchor**: `academic-research-skills-ROADMAP.md` §3.6.4 (description correction) + §3.6.5 exit criteria last item
**Spec status**: draft — §1 sanity-checked via codex round-1 (1 P1 + 7 P2 + 3 P3 applied), §2-§9 pending
**Author**: Cheng-I Wu

## §1 — Scope and Goals

### Target release

v3.6.6 (`academic-paper/full` writer/evaluator sprint contract)

**Roadmap anchor**: §3.6.4 description correction + §3.6.5 exit criteria last item
**Schema impact**: Schema 13.1 backward-compatible add. Schema 14 explicitly rejected per Approach 1 decision.

### In scope

1. `shared/sprint_contract.schema.json` Schema 13.1 upgrade:
   - `mode` enum adds `writer_full` + `evaluator_full`
   - New optional top-level fields: `pre_commitment_artifacts`, `disagreement_handling`
   - Reviewer-specific required fields gated behind `allOf` / `if mode startsWith reviewer_`, including `measurement_procedure.reviewer_must_output_before_paper`, reviewer scoring-plan requirements, `failure_conditions[].cross_reviewer_quantifier`, and editorial `failure_conditions[].action`
   - Writer conditional gate requires `pre_commitment_artifacts` for `writer_full`
   - Evaluator conditional gate requires `disagreement_handling` for `evaluator_full`
   - **Note**: `agreement_audit` is intentionally NOT a schema field. It is a runtime artifact (see item 10), not pre-registered acceptance criteria. Keeping it out of the schema preserves the v3.6.2 design philosophy that contract = "what good looks like before the work runs", not "what was observed during the work".

2. `shared/contracts/writer/full.json` + `shared/contracts/evaluator/full.json` contract templates.

3. `shared/contracts/README.md` update documenting writer/evaluator contract directories, mirroring v3.6.2 convention.

4. `scripts/check_sprint_contract.py` mode branching for reviewer, writer, and evaluator contracts; structure unchanged, logic extended.

5. `scripts/test_check_sprint_contract.py` extension + CI coverage for `shared/contracts/writer/` and `shared/contracts/evaluator/`. The test module is the same one CI invokes via `python3 -m unittest scripts.test_check_sprint_contract` (workflow `spec-consistency.yml`); v3.6.6 extends rather than relocates it.

6. `academic-paper/agents/draft_writer_agent.md` Phase 4 hard gate:
   - Phase 4a paper-blind commitment: output `acceptance_criteria_paraphrase` + writer pre-commitment artifacts
   - Phase 4b paper-visible drafting against the Phase 4a commitments

7. `academic-paper/agents/peer_reviewer_agent.md` Phase 6 hard gate:
   - Phase 6a paper-blind commitment: output `contract_paraphrase` + evaluator scoring/disagreement commitments
   - Phase 6b paper-visible evaluation; verdict logic unchanged

8. `academic-paper` orchestration wiring for the actual two-call Phase 4 and Phase 6 split. The spec must name the orchestration file(s) that call `draft_writer_agent.md` and `peer_reviewer_agent.md`, or explicitly document that existing orchestration already supports separate paper-blind and paper-visible calls.

9. Model selection mirrors existing `ARS_CROSS_MODEL` env pattern: unset → warning + same-model; set → use that model ID for evaluator/cross-runtime comparison. No new env var.

10. Agreement audit split:
    - `academic-paper/references/agreement_audit_protocol.md` for the versioned protocol/template
    - `examples/ab_evidence/v3.6.6/agreement_audit_results.md` for runtime example output

11. A/B evidence in `tests/fixtures/v3.6.6-ab/` (per §6.2 / §6.5):
    - Seven-paper fixture: six paper-A (three paper types × two repetitions, drawn from existing deep-research synthesis reports) for H1–H3 averaging + one paper-C (v3.6.5 known-fail sanity case carrying `known_failure_mode` + `failure_evidence`) for categorical signal
    - Process-metric-only, delta-based comparison
    - Codex gpt-5.5 + xhigh verdict-only judge for H1 (acceptance dimension pass rate) and H3 (deduped self-detected issue count); Semantic Scholar API Tier 0 programmatic verification for H2 (Tier 0 unverified citation rate — Tier 0 fail does not by itself classify a citation as fabricated; later-tier classification is implementation-PR concern per §6.3 / §6.6)
    - Pre-declared directional hypotheses with frozen ship thresholds (per §6.4): H1 hard ≥ +10 percentage points (buffered from initial +20 pp estimate after fixture-sizing pass); H2 soft ≤ 0% relative delta (must not regress); H3 soft ≥ 0 mean count delta (must not regress); paper-C categorical fail = P1 review, not auto-block

12. ROADMAP §3.6.4 description correction + new decision-log entry recording that v3.6.6 extends contracts to the existing writer/evaluator pair, rather than splitting a single agent.

13. CHANGELOG / `.claude/CLAUDE.md` / README / `scripts/check_spec_consistency.py` version bump sweep.

### Out of scope

1. `academic-paper/revision` mode.

2. `academic-pipeline` orchestrator-level contract.

3. External `academic-paper-reviewer` skill integration; it already received reviewer contracts in v3.6.2 and is zero-touch in v3.6.6.

4. Internal/external two-reviewer merge. This is known technical debt and remains a v3.7.x follow-up.

5. New evaluator agent file; `peer_reviewer_agent.md` is the evaluator.

6. Schema 14. Schema 13.1 is the approved backward-compatible add.

7. New CLI flag, contract negotiation UI, or runtime contract editing.

8. Real retracted-paper fixtures or hard FNR/FPR calibration gates.

### Design goals

1. **Mirror v3.6.2 pattern** — schema evolution is backward-compatible, validator structure stays familiar, templates live under `shared/contracts/`, and the load-bearing runtime behavior is a two-call paper-blind/paper-visible hard gate.

2. **Evaluator anti-drift** — `peer_reviewer_agent` commits its contract paraphrase, scoring plan, and disagreement-handling plan before reading the full draft.

3. **Writer pre-commitment** — `draft_writer_agent` commits acceptance criteria and pre-commitment artifacts before drafting against the full paper context.

4. **Cross-model compatible via existing env pattern** — v3.6.6 supports cross-model/cross-runtime comparison through `ARS_CROSS_MODEL` without changing default same-model behavior when unset.

5. **Open-ended task evidence discipline** — A/B evidence uses process metrics and deltas, not absolute claims that a generated paper is objectively good.

### Non-goals

- Do not set an absolute paper-quality threshold; contract-on/off delta is the signal.

- Do not introduce contract negotiation protocol; inherit fixed baseline template + bounded `agent_amendments` append slot from v3.6.2.

- Do not change current Accept/Minor/Major/Reject verdict mapping.

- Do not merge, replace, or coordinate the internal `peer_reviewer_agent` with the external `academic-paper-reviewer` skill.

### Known limitations

- `academic-paper` still has an internal `peer_reviewer_agent`, while the repository also has the external `academic-paper-reviewer` skill. v3.6.6 documents this as known technical debt and leaves merge/routing decisions to v3.7.x.

### Notes for next review round

- §5 must verify whether existing `academic-paper` orchestration already supports separate paper-blind and paper-visible calls. If not, v3.6.6 must include the concrete orchestration change rather than treating the split as a prompt-only edit.

- §3 must spell out the `pre_commitment_artifacts` field shape (subfields, validation rules) — currently named but not structurally specified.

- §6 A/B evidence ship thresholds: initial estimates of +20 pp / 15% / +2 findings have been tuned after fixture sizing to **H1 hard ≥ +10 pp / H2 soft ≤ 0% relative delta / H3 soft ≥ 0 mean count delta**, with paper-C categorical pass/fail as a separate signal. Frozen in §6.4; further revision requires §6 spec amendment per §6.6 boundary.

## §2 — Key decisions (settled during brainstorm)

Two rounds of decisions converged before this spec started: a 7-question clarification with the user (Q1-Q7), then a codex round-1 sanity check on §1 that surfaced four design-level corrections (D1-D4). The decisions table records both rounds with their consequences for §3 onwards.

No `expected_findings.yaml` ground truth file — H1 / H3 use codex gpt-5.5 + xhigh verdict-only judge against the contract acceptance dimensions; H2 uses Semantic Scholar API programmatic verification; paper-C categorical signal uses the v3.6.5 session-log Stage 3 reviewer excerpt as the known-failure-mode evidence (§6.2 manifest `failure_evidence` field). |

### 2.2 Codex round-1 design corrections (D1-D4)

After §1 was drafted from Q1-Q7, a codex sanity check on §1 surfaced four design-level issues that survived clarification because they only become visible when the spec meets the existing schema and protocol. All four were applied to §1 and shape §3-§6.

| # | Issue codex surfaced | Decision | Consequence |
|---|----------------------|----------|-------------|
| D1 | Schema 13 has reviewer-specific **required** fields (`measurement_procedure.reviewer_must_output_before_paper`, `failure_conditions[].cross_reviewer_quantifier`, editorial enum on `failure_conditions[].action`). A bare `mode` enum addition will fail validation for `writer_full` / `evaluator_full`. The "13.1 simple add" framing was too optimistic. | **Apply v3.6.2's `allOf` / `if mode startsWith reviewer_` conditional pattern to all four reviewer-specific fields.** Mirror the technique v3.6.2 already used for `cross_reviewer_quantifier` (v3.6.2 spec §3.3). | §3 specifies four reviewer-conditional gates (not one). Existing reviewer contracts validate identically (zero-touch promise preserved). New writer/evaluator contracts are unaffected by reviewer-specific fields. |
| D2 | `disagreement_handling` was originally proposed as a single field for both writer and evaluator. But "disagreement" is meaningless for a solo writer (no peer to disagree with). | **Split into two fields.** Writer mode requires `pre_commitment_artifacts` (what to commit pre-paper). Evaluator mode requires `disagreement_handling` (how to resolve writer-evaluator disagreement). Each gated to its respective mode. | Schema 13.1 adds two optional top-level fields, not one. Two new conditional gates: `if mode == writer_full` requires `pre_commitment_artifacts`; `if mode == evaluator_full` requires `disagreement_handling`. |
| D3 | "Cross-model by default" framing in original Design Goal 4 contradicts the actual decided behaviour (Q3: unset → same-model with warning, set → cross-model). The framing inflated the truthful claim. | **Reword Design Goal 4 to "Cross-model compatible via existing env pattern."** Truthful framing matches actual behaviour. | Design Goal 4 in §1 reflects the change. README / CHANGELOG sweep (in-scope 13) carries the same wording so no claim of "default cross-model" reaches users. |
| D4 | Codex P2 #18 flagged that `agreement_audit.md` placed under `academic-paper/references/` mixes versioned source with runtime artifact, and recommended splitting protocol-doc from runtime-output. Reading that finding against v3.6.2's contract philosophy raised a deeper question: should `agreement_audit` be a **schema field** at all? Agreement-audit data is observed during the run, not pre-registered acceptance criteria (the v3.6.2 contract definition). Embedding observed data in the schema violates v3.6.2's load-bearing principle that contract = "what good looks like before the work runs". | **Extension of codex's P2 #18 finding (not codex's own recommendation):** remove `agreement_audit` from schema entirely. Keep only the protocol document (versioned, in `academic-paper/references/agreement_audit_protocol.md`) and runtime example output (in `examples/ab_evidence/v3.6.6/agreement_audit_results.md`). Audit data lives in runtime artifacts, never in the contract. | §1 in-scope item 1 lists only two new optional schema fields. The audit/runtime separation appears in in-scope item 10 (split-path delivery). Note that codex's original recommendation only addressed file location (split protocol from runtime output); the schema-removal decision is one step further. |

### 2.3 Decisions deferred

L1-L4 are tracked in §8 "Risks and open questions" (mirroring v3.6.2 spec §10 convention; v3.6.6 has fewer sections so risks and open questions live in the same section). They were raised during brainstorm or codex sanity check but settling them needs the schema or protocol detail in §3-§6.

## §3 — Schema 13.1 spec

Schema 13.1 is a **backward-compatible extension** of Schema 13. The schema file path stays `shared/sprint_contract.schema.json`. The `title` updates to `"ARS Sprint Contract (Schema 13.1)"`. No file rename, no `$id` change.

This section closes open questions L1 (`pre_commitment_artifacts` shape) and L4 (`acceptance_criteria_paraphrase` vs `pre_commitment_artifacts` parity). L2 (orchestration) is closed by §5; L3 (final A/B thresholds) in §6.

### 3.1 What changes vs Schema 13

Three categories of change. None remove or rename existing fields.

| Category | Change | Backward-compat impact |
|---|---|---|
| **Enum extension** | `mode` enum gains `writer_full` + `evaluator_full` (5 → 7 values) | Reviewer contracts unchanged. Enum addition is non-breaking. |
| **Existing-field gating** | Four currently-required fields become reviewer-conditional: `measurement_procedure`, `panel_size`, `failure_conditions[].cross_reviewer_quantifier` (already conditional in §3.3 of Schema 13), `failure_conditions[].action` enum membership | Reviewer contracts validate identically. Writer/evaluator contracts are no longer forced to carry reviewer-specific structure. |
| **New optional fields** | Two new top-level optional fields: `pre_commitment_artifacts`, `disagreement_handling`. Two new conditional gates require them for `writer_full` / `evaluator_full`. | Reviewer contracts ignore both fields (still pass). Writer/evaluator contracts must carry the field that matches their mode. |

`agreement_audit` is **explicitly not added** to the schema (D4 in §2.2). Audit data is a runtime artifact, captured in `examples/ab_evidence/v3.6.6/agreement_audit_results.md`, never in pre-registered acceptance criteria.

### 3.2 Mode enum extension

```json
"mode": {
  "enum": [
    "reviewer_full",
    "reviewer_methodology_focus",
    "reviewer_re_review",
    "reviewer_calibration",
    "reviewer_guided",
    "writer_full",
    "evaluator_full"
  ]
}
```

`reviewer_quick` remains **excluded** from the enum (v3.6.2 Q3-A' boundary). `revision_full`, `evaluator_revision`, `pipeline_full`, etc. are **out of scope** for v3.6.6 (v3.6.7+ / v3.7.x candidates).

### 3.3 Existing-field gating (D1 application)

Schema 13 has four reviewer-specific surfaces that must move from "required for all modes" to "required only for `reviewer_*` modes". This applies the v3.6.2 §3.3 `allOf if mode startsWith reviewer_` pattern to additional fields.

#### 3.3.1 `measurement_procedure` becomes reviewer-conditional

Current state (Schema 13): top-level `required` includes `measurement_procedure`, and the object's three subfields are all reviewer-specific (`reviewer_must_output_before_paper`, `scoring_plan_schema`, `paraphrase_minimum_dimensions`).

Schema 13.1 change: remove `measurement_procedure` from top-level `required`. Add it back conditionally:

```json
{
  "if": {
    "properties": { "mode": { "pattern": "^reviewer_" } },
    "required": ["mode"]
  },
  "then": {
    "required": ["measurement_procedure"]
  }
}
```

Writer and evaluator modes do NOT need `measurement_procedure` because their pre-commitment artifacts live in dedicated new fields (`pre_commitment_artifacts` / `disagreement_handling`) with different shapes — see §3.4.

#### 3.3.2 `failure_conditions[].cross_reviewer_quantifier` (already conditional)

Schema 13 §3.3 already gates this:

```json
{
  "if": { "properties": { "mode": { "pattern": "^reviewer_" } }, "required": ["mode"] },
  "then": { "properties": { "failure_conditions": { "items": { "required": ["cross_reviewer_quantifier"] } } } }
}
```

No Schema 13.1 change needed. Writer/evaluator failure_conditions are not required to carry this field.

#### 3.3.3 `failure_conditions[].action` enum membership becomes mode-conditional

Current state: `action` enum is hardcoded to five `editorial_decision=*` values. These are reviewer-only outcomes (an evaluator does not issue an editorial decision; a writer cannot fail itself into an editorial decision).

Schema 13.1 change: **remove the base `action` enum entirely**. Move the constraint to three `allOf` mode-conditional branches (reviewer / writer / evaluator). The base property keeps only `"type": "string"` as a structural placeholder.

This change is forced by JSON Schema semantics: `if/then` does not override the base — the base enum and the `then` enum intersect, and a value must satisfy both. A writer/evaluator-specific enum cannot override the base reviewer enum; both are simultaneously enforced and the writer/evaluator values are rejected. The only valid pattern is to drop the base enum and constrain entirely in `allOf`.

```json
"action": { "type": "string" }
```

with the three `allOf` branches:

```json
{
  "if": {
    "properties": { "mode": { "pattern": "^reviewer_" } },
    "required": ["mode"]
  },
  "then": {
    "properties": {
      "failure_conditions": {
        "items": {
          "properties": {
            "action": {
              "enum": [
                "editorial_decision=accept",
                "editorial_decision=minor_revision",
                "editorial_decision=major_revision",
                "editorial_decision=reject_or_major_revision",
                "editorial_decision=reject"
              ]
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
},
{
  "if": {
    "properties": { "mode": { "const": "writer_full" } },
    "required": ["mode"]
  },
  "then": {
    "properties": {
      "failure_conditions": {
        "items": {
          "properties": {
            "action": {
              "enum": [
                "writer_decision=accept",
                "writer_decision=revise_in_phase_4b",
                "writer_decision=escalate_to_evaluator"
              ]
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
},
{
  "if": {
    "properties": { "mode": { "const": "evaluator_full" } },
    "required": ["mode"]
  },
  "then": {
    "properties": {
      "failure_conditions": {
        "items": {
          "properties": {
            "action": {
              "enum": [
                "evaluator_decision=accept",
                "evaluator_decision=accept_with_dissent_note",
                "evaluator_decision=request_revision",
                "evaluator_decision=flag_for_reviewer_stage"
              ]
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Notes on the action vocabulary:

- Reviewer enum is unchanged from Schema 13 (zero-touch promise to existing reviewer contracts).
- Writer enum has three values: `writer_decision=accept` (F0 success — see §3.3.4), `writer_decision=revise_in_phase_4b` (writer self-repair within the same phase), `writer_decision=escalate_to_evaluator` (writer hits a condition it cannot self-repair, hands off to evaluator).
- Evaluator enum mirrors ROADMAP §3.6.4's three decisions (`accept` / `request_revision` / `flag_for_reviewer_stage`) plus `accept_with_dissent_note` for cases where the evaluator's own pre-committed `scoring_plan.per_dimension_criteria.what_triggers_warn` matches on a high or normal-priority dimension and no mandatory dimension scores 'block' or 'warn' — the draft is acceptable overall, but a non-mandatory concern is logged rather than silenced. The `accept_with_dissent_note` action is referenced by `disagreement_handling.disagreement_resolution.on_dimension_disagreement` in §3.4.2 — both surfaces use the same vocabulary. Crucially, neither surface relies on numeric writer pre-commitments (the writer's `pre_commitment_artifacts` carries only `acceptance_criteria_paraphrase` per §3.4.1, not per-dimension numeric score predictions); evaluator-side dissent is anchored on the evaluator's own scoring plan plus the upstream structural artefacts the writer follows in Phase 4b (Structure Architect's approved outline, Argument Blueprint, Paper Configuration Record).

#### 3.3.4 `failure_conditions` `contains` F0 — concept stays universal, mechanics become mode-conditional

The **concept** of a universal F0 accept condition stays — every contract must carry an explicit success condition so the synthesizer/evaluator/writer always has a "no-failure-fired" terminal state to emit. Writer F0 means "draft meets all writer pre-commitment artifacts"; evaluator F0 means "draft passes evaluator's pre-committed scoring plan"; reviewer F0 stays "every mandatory dimension scores 'pass'".

The **mechanics** must change. Schema 13 hardcodes `contains.properties.action` to `"const": "editorial_decision=accept"`. With the §3.3.3 mode-conditional action enum, writer/evaluator F0 actions are `writer_decision=accept` / `evaluator_decision=accept` respectively. The hardcoded const will reject them. F0 `contains` must therefore become mode-conditional too:

```json
"failure_conditions": {
  "type": "array",
  "minItems": 1,
  "items": { /* unchanged */ }
}
```

Remove the inline `contains` from the base `failure_conditions` definition. Re-add it via three `allOf` mode-conditional branches that each pin F0's action to the mode's accept variant:

```json
{
  "if": {
    "properties": { "mode": { "pattern": "^reviewer_" } },
    "required": ["mode"]
  },
  "then": {
    "properties": {
      "failure_conditions": {
        "contains": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "condition_id": { "const": "F0" },
            "action": { "const": "editorial_decision=accept" }
          },
          "required": ["condition_id", "action"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
},
{
  "if": {
    "properties": { "mode": { "const": "writer_full" } },
    "required": ["mode"]
  },
  "then": {
    "properties": {
      "failure_conditions": {
        "contains": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "condition_id": { "const": "F0" },
            "action": { "const": "writer_decision=accept" }
          },
          "required": ["condition_id", "action"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
},
{
  "if": {
    "properties": { "mode": { "const": "evaluator_full" } },
    "required": ["mode"]
  },
  "then": {
    "properties": {
      "failure_conditions": {
        "contains": {
          "type": "object",
          "properties": {
            "condition_id": { "const": "F0" },
            "action": { "const": "evaluator_decision=accept" }
          },
          "required": ["condition_id", "action"]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Reviewer contracts validate identically: the reviewer-mode `contains` clause is structurally identical to the Schema 13 inline `contains`. Writer/evaluator contracts get a mode-appropriate F0 accept pin.

#### 3.3.5 `panel_size` becomes reviewer-conditional

Current state (Schema 13): top-level `required` includes `panel_size` with the base definition `{ "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 }`. The field encodes the size of the reviewer panel for cross-reviewer quantifier evaluation (`cross_reviewer_quantifier ∈ {any, majority, all}` in §3.3.2 is meaningful only when more than one reviewer participates). Generator-mode contracts run a single agent each — `draft_writer_agent` for `writer_full`, `peer_reviewer_agent` for `evaluator_full` — so `panel_size` has no semantic anchor in those modes.

Schema 13.1 change: remove `panel_size` from top-level `required`. The base definition stays unchanged (`{ "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 }`) so any contract that does carry the field still validates structurally. Add it back conditionally for reviewer modes:

```json
{
  "if": {
    "properties": { "mode": { "pattern": "^reviewer_" } },
    "required": ["mode"]
  },
  "then": {
    "required": ["panel_size"]
  }
}
```

Writer and evaluator contracts do NOT carry `panel_size`. Each runs a single agent; the field would either be set to `1` (semantically empty) or omitted, and forcing the field on the template adds no validation power while leaking reviewer-specific vocabulary into generator-mode contracts. The cross-reviewer-quantifier conditional gate (§3.3.2 / allOf branch 1) `require`s `cross_reviewer_quantifier` only for reviewer modes; the field remains a declared optional property on `failure_conditions[].items` for all modes, so a generator-mode contract that mistakenly carries `cross_reviewer_quantifier` (for example, copy-pasted from a reviewer template) still passes schema validation. Shipped `writer/full.json` and `evaluator/full.json` templates omit the field by default, and §4 contract authoring guidance restates the omission. Schema-level strict prevention (declaring the property `false` for generator modes, or adding a top-level `not` clause) is deferred to v3.7.x — see §8.2 R1. The same require-only-not-forbid pattern applies symmetrically to `measurement_procedure` (§3.3.1) and is inherited from Schema 13's existing reviewer-conditional design; v3.6.6 keeps that posture rather than expanding the schema strictness surface in this release.

### 3.4 New fields

Both new fields below are inserted into the schema's **top-level `properties` object**, not nested under `measurement_procedure` or any other existing field. They are declared at top-level (so the outer `additionalProperties: false` does not reject contracts that carry them) but **not** added to the top-level `required` list — their requirement is mode-conditional (gated in §3.5).

#### 3.4.1 `pre_commitment_artifacts` (writer-only, closes L1)

```json
"pre_commitment_artifacts": {
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": ["acceptance_criteria_paraphrase"],
  "$comment": "pre_commitment_artifacts carries only invariant, paper-agnostic policy: how many acceptance_dimensions the writer must paraphrase in Phase 4a paper-blind output. Everything paper-specific lives in upstream runtime artefacts and is read at Phase 4a / 4b runtime, not committed in the frozen contract baseline. Specifically: per-section word counts come from the Paper Configuration Record (intake_agent); section outline comes from the Structure Architect's approved outline (structure_architect_agent); CER chains come from the Argument Blueprint (argument_builder_agent). Embedding any of those in the contract baseline would either force orchestrators to mutate the frozen baseline before Phase 4a or hard-code IMRaD assumptions onto non-IMRaD paper types (literature reviews, theoretical, case study, policy brief — all supported by writer_full per draft_writer_agent's Paper Type Adjustments table). Writer dimensions D1 (section_completeness), D3 (argument_blueprint_fidelity), D4 (total_word_count), D5 (per_section_word_count) phrase their gates against those upstream artefacts rather than against contract-embedded values. The object remains a structured sub-object (rather than promoting acceptance_criteria_paraphrase to a top-level field) so v3.7.x can extend pre_commitment_artifacts with new invariant, paper-agnostic policy without an additional schema-architecture refactor.",
  "properties": {
    "acceptance_criteria_paraphrase": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["minimum_dimensions"],
      "$comment": "This object is a CONFIGURATION declaration, not the paraphrase content itself. It declares how many of the contract's acceptance_dimensions the writer must paraphrase in Phase 4a. The actual paraphrase text is a runtime artifact emitted by draft_writer_agent in its Phase 4a output (analogous to how reviewer paraphrase content lives in <phase1_output>, not in the contract). Mirrors reviewer measurement_procedure.paraphrase_minimum_dimensions semantics.",
      "properties": {
        "minimum_dimensions": {
          "anyOf": [
            { "const": "all" },
            { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 }
          ],
          "$comment": "Default in shipped writer template: 'all'."
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Required for `writer_full` only (gated in §3.5).

**L4 resolution**: `acceptance_criteria_paraphrase` is **a subfield inside** `pre_commitment_artifacts`, not a separate top-level field. This avoids the codex P3 #33 parity question — writer Phase 4a outputs ONE artifact (`pre_commitment_artifacts`) which currently carries one invariant, paper-agnostic subcomponent (`acceptance_criteria_paraphrase`). Earlier drafts of §3.4.1 also nested `structure_plan` and `argument_plan` here; those were evicted to upstream runtime artefacts (Structure Architect output, Argument Blueprint) per the schema $comment above and the design discussion in §4.2 / §8.2 R2. The container shape is preserved so v3.7.x can extend pre_commitment_artifacts with new invariant policy without an architecture refactor. Reviewer Phase 1 still uses the existing `contract_paraphrase` semantics under `measurement_procedure.reviewer_must_output_before_paper`. The naming asymmetry reflects that reviewer is paraphrasing for assessment, writer is paraphrasing for execution.

#### 3.4.2 `disagreement_handling` (evaluator-only)

```json
"disagreement_handling": {
  "type": "object",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "required": ["paraphrase_minimum_dimensions", "scoring_plan", "pre_commitment_check_protocol", "disagreement_resolution"],
  "properties": {
    "paraphrase_minimum_dimensions": {
      "anyOf": [
        { "const": "all" },
        { "type": "integer", "minimum": 1 }
      ],
      "$comment": "How many of the contract's acceptance_dimensions the evaluator must paraphrase in Phase 6a paper-blind output (the contract_paraphrase artifact named in §1 design goal 2 / §4.3). Mirrors reviewer measurement_procedure.paraphrase_minimum_dimensions and writer pre_commitment_artifacts.acceptance_criteria_paraphrase.minimum_dimensions to keep the Phase-6a anti-drift gate hard-required at the schema layer rather than relying on prose-level commitments. Default in shipped evaluator template: 'all'."
    },
    "scoring_plan": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["per_dimension_criteria"],
      "properties": {
        "per_dimension_criteria": {
          "type": "array",
          "minItems": 1,
          "items": {
            "type": "object",
            "additionalProperties": false,
            "required": ["dimension_id", "what_to_look_for", "what_triggers_block", "what_triggers_warn"],
            "properties": {
              "dimension_id": { "type": "string", "pattern": "^D[1-9][0-9]?$" },
              "what_to_look_for": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
              "what_triggers_block": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 },
              "what_triggers_warn": { "type": "string", "minLength": 1 }
            },
            "$comment": "Mirrors reviewer measurement_procedure.scoring_plan_schema four-field structure. Evaluator commits these in Phase 6a paper-blind."
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "pre_commitment_check_protocol": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["check_writer_artifact"],
      "properties": {
        "check_writer_artifact": {
          "const": "pre_commitment_artifacts",
          "$comment": "Pinned to the single writer source for v3.6.6. Field shape exists (rather than inlining the const) for forward compatibility — when v3.6.7+ may add additional writer artifacts, this can relax to an enum without a breaking schema change."
        }
      }
    },
    "disagreement_resolution": {
      "type": "object",
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "required": ["on_dimension_disagreement", "on_structural_drift"],
      "$comment": "Both subfield enums use the fully-qualified evaluator_decision=* vocabulary so values can be passed directly into failure_conditions[].action without runtime transformation. Keeping a single canonical action vocabulary across §3.3.3 and §3.4.2 prevents drift between the two surfaces.",
      "properties": {
        "on_dimension_disagreement": {
          "enum": [
            "evaluator_decision=request_revision",
            "evaluator_decision=accept_with_dissent_note",
            "evaluator_decision=flag_for_reviewer_stage"
          ],
          "$comment": "What the evaluator does when its own paper-blind scoring plan flags a dimension during paper-visible evaluation (the dimension hits its pre-committed what_triggers_block or what_triggers_warn anchors). The disagreement is between the evaluator's pre-committed criteria and its post-paper observation; it is NOT anchored on numeric writer pre-commitments (writer pre_commitment_artifacts carries only acceptance_criteria_paraphrase per §3.4.1; paper-specific section outlines, CER chains, and word counts are read from upstream runtime artefacts — Structure Architect output, Argument Blueprint, Paper Configuration Record — not from the contract). Default in shipped templates: 'evaluator_decision=request_revision' for mandatory dimensions; runtime evaluator may downgrade non-mandatory dimensions to 'accept_with_dissent_note' (see F4 in evaluator/full.json)."
        },
        "on_structural_drift": {
          "enum": [
            "evaluator_decision=request_revision",
            "evaluator_decision=accept_with_dissent_note",
            "evaluator_decision=flag_for_reviewer_stage"
          ],
          "$comment": "What the evaluator does when the actual draft structure deviates from the Structure Architect's approved outline (the upstream runtime artefact from structure_architect_agent that the writer follows in Phase 4b). Drift threshold lives in the evaluator's runtime judgement, not the schema; the contract carries only the default verdict to apply when drift is observed."
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Required for `evaluator_full` only (gated in §3.5).

### 3.5 New conditional gates

Two new `allOf` branches added to the existing two:

```json
{
  "if": {
    "properties": { "mode": { "const": "writer_full" } },
    "required": ["mode"]
  },
  "then": {
    "required": ["pre_commitment_artifacts"]
  }
},
{
  "if": {
    "properties": { "mode": { "const": "evaluator_full" } },
    "required": ["mode"]
  },
  "then": {
    "required": ["disagreement_handling"]
  }
}
```

The full Schema 13.1 `allOf` array therefore has **twelve branches**:

| # | Source | Branch |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | (existing) Schema 13 §3.3 | Reviewer `cross_reviewer_quantifier` requirement |
| 2 | (existing) Schema 13 §3.3 | `override_ladder` three-round shape |
| 3 | (new) §3.3.1 | Reviewer mode requires `measurement_procedure` |
| 4 | (new) §3.3.3 | Reviewer mode pins `failure_conditions[].action` to editorial enum |
| 5 | (new) §3.3.3 | `writer_full` pins `failure_conditions[].action` to writer_decision enum |
| 6 | (new) §3.3.3 | `evaluator_full` pins `failure_conditions[].action` to evaluator_decision enum |
| 7 | (new) §3.3.4 | Reviewer mode F0 `contains` (action = `editorial_decision=accept`) |
| 8 | (new) §3.3.4 | `writer_full` F0 `contains` (action = `writer_decision=accept`) |
| 9 | (new) §3.3.4 | `evaluator_full` F0 `contains` (action = `evaluator_decision=accept`) |
| 10 | (new) §3.3.5 | Reviewer mode requires `panel_size` |
| 11 | (new) this section | `writer_full` requires `pre_commitment_artifacts` |
| 12 | (new) this section | `evaluator_full` requires `disagreement_handling` |

Order is logically grouped (existing first; then reviewer-conditional including `panel_size`; then generator-family triplets for action enum and F0 contains; then mode-specific top-level requirements) but JSON Schema does not enforce `allOf` order semantics.

The branch count is high because two existing constraints (action enum, F0 contains) had to be lifted out of base properties and re-expressed three times for the three mode families, and two further fields (`measurement_procedure`, `panel_size`) had to be lifted from base `required` into reviewer-conditional gates. This is the trade-off for keeping reviewer validation byte-identical (zero-touch promise) while extending the schema to writer/evaluator modes.

### 3.6 Backward compatibility proof

A Schema 13 reviewer contract that was valid before v3.6.6 must remain valid under Schema 13.1. The proof is structural:

| Schema 13 reviewer contract field | Schema 13.1 fate | Validation impact |
|---|---|---|
| `mode: reviewer_*` | Still in enum | Pass |
| `measurement_procedure` (object, all three subfields) | Removed from base `required`; reviewer-conditional gate (allOf branch 3, §3.3.1) re-requires it for reviewer modes | Pass — same effective constraint |
| `failure_conditions[].cross_reviewer_quantifier` | Same conditional as Schema 13 (allOf branch 1) | Pass |
| `failure_conditions[].action` (`editorial_decision=*`) | Base enum lifted; reviewer-conditional gate (allOf branch 4, §3.3.3) re-pins it to the same five `editorial_decision=*` values for reviewer modes | Pass — same effective enum |
| `failure_conditions` `contains` F0 (`editorial_decision=accept`) | Inline `contains` lifted; reviewer-conditional gate (allOf branch 7, §3.3.4) re-pins F0 to `editorial_decision=accept` for reviewer modes | Pass — structurally identical contains clause |
| `panel_size` (integer ≥ 1) | Removed from base `required`; reviewer-conditional gate (allOf branch 10, §3.3.5) re-requires it for reviewer modes; base property definition unchanged | Pass — same effective constraint |
| All other fields (`contract_id`, `stage`, `baseline_version`, `acceptance_dimensions`, `override_ladder`, `agent_amendments`, `generated_at`) | Unchanged | Pass |

The pattern across the lifted constraints (measurement_procedure, action enum, F0 contains, panel_size): each was originally enforced unconditionally in the base; each is now enforced via a reviewer-mode `allOf` branch that re-applies the original constraint. Validation is byte-equivalent for every reviewer contract; the lift only opens room for writer/evaluator modes to satisfy different but mode-appropriate constraints in branches 5/6 and 8/9, and to omit `panel_size` entirely (a single-agent generator has no panel).

`pre_commitment_artifacts` and `disagreement_handling` are absent from reviewer contracts — both are optional at top level and gated only for writer/evaluator modes (allOf branches 11/12), so reviewer contract validation does not require them.

`scripts/test_check_sprint_contract.py` will gain a `test_existing_reviewer_contracts_still_valid_under_13_1` regression test that loads both shipped reviewer templates (`shared/contracts/reviewer/full.json` + `methodology_focus.json`) against the Schema 13.1 file and asserts validation success without modification. A second test, `test_byte_equivalent_validation_for_reviewer_contracts`, will diff the validation result tree (errors + warnings) against Schema 13's result for the same contract and assert empty diff.

### 3.7 What §3 does NOT specify

These are out of scope for §3 and live in later sections:

- Contract template content for writer/evaluator (concrete dimension definitions, F-condition severity tuning) — §4
- Two-phase orchestration (how Phase 4a/4b and 6a/6b actually get invoked) — §5
- Validator code path for new conditionals — §7
- Test fixtures and CI wiring — §7

## §4 — Contract templates

§4 specifies the two new shipped templates introduced in v3.6.6:

- `shared/contracts/writer/full.json` — `writer_full` mode, gated to `draft_writer_agent` Phase 4
- `shared/contracts/evaluator/full.json` — `evaluator_full` mode, gated to `peer_reviewer_agent` Phase 6

Both templates are concrete instances of Schema 13.1 (§3) and demonstrate every new conditional gate (`pre_commitment_artifacts` for writer; `disagreement_handling` for evaluator; mode-specific `failure_conditions[].action` enums; mode-appropriate F0 accept). Each template's acceptance dimensions are extracted from the existing `draft_writer_agent.md` / `peer_reviewer_agent.md` Quality Gates and rubric, preserving the v3.6.2 design philosophy that "contract = pre-existing agent behavior turned into a hard gate", not "contract = new behavior bolted on".

### 4.0 Spec phase vs implementation phase sequencing

> **Spec-branch notice**. While `spec/v3.6.6-generator-evaluator-contract` is the active branch, the JSON files at `shared/contracts/writer/full.json` and `shared/contracts/evaluator/full.json` are **design-time artefacts**: they describe what good will look like at v3.6.6 ship time, but Schema 13.1 has not yet landed in `shared/sprint_contract.schema.json`. The current Schema 13 validator rejects these files by design (see expected errors below). Do not load them as live contracts on this branch. Once the v3.6.6 implementation PR merges to `main`, both files become live shipped templates atomically with the schema upgrade.

The shipped JSON files land on the spec branch as part of this design doc rather than as a follow-up template PR for one reason: §3 and §4 are co-load-bearing. Schema 13.1's eleven new `allOf` branches are only reviewable in the abstract until concrete templates exercise them; the writer's `pre_commitment_artifacts` shape (§3.4.1) is only reviewable once an actual `writer_full` template binds it to acceptance dimensions and `acceptance_criteria_paraphrase.minimum_dimensions`; F-condition severity ordering (§4.2 / §4.3) is only reviewable once mode-specific action enums are populated. Splitting the templates out into a follow-up patch would mean reviewing the schema and the templates against different mental models on different days — the exact drift mode that v3.6.5.2 codex review caught (and fixed in the §3 panel_size patch on this branch).

Expected validator behaviour on the spec branch:

```
$ python scripts/check_sprint_contract.py shared/contracts/writer/full.json --ars-version v3.6.6
ERROR: ['mode']: 'writer_full' is not one of [...reviewer modes only...]
ERROR: []: 'panel_size' is a required property
ERROR: []: 'measurement_procedure' is a required property
ERROR: []: Additional properties are not allowed ('pre_commitment_artifacts' was unexpected)
ERROR: ['failure_conditions', N, 'action']: 'writer_decision=*' / 'evaluator_decision=*' rejected
```

Each of these errors is closed by exactly one Schema 13.1 change in §3:

| Validator error | Closed by |
|---|---|
| `writer_full` / `evaluator_full` not in mode enum | §3.2 mode enum extension |
| `panel_size` required | §3.3.5 reviewer-conditional gate |
| `measurement_procedure` required | §3.3.1 reviewer-conditional gate |
| `pre_commitment_artifacts` not allowed | §3.4.1 new top-level optional field |
| `disagreement_handling` not allowed | §3.4.2 new top-level optional field |
| Writer / evaluator action enum values rejected | §3.3.3 mode-conditional action enum |
| F0 contains action mismatch | §3.3.4 mode-conditional F0 contains |

The implementation PR ships the schema diff and these templates as one atomic commit so the validator transitions from "rejects v3.6.6 templates and accepts reviewer templates" to "accepts both" in a single step, preserving the §3.6 byte-equivalence promise for reviewer contracts throughout the rollout. Staging the templates under a non-live path during the spec phase (e.g. `docs/design/v3.6.6-templates/`) was considered and rejected: it would require a copy or move step at implementation time that risks introducing drift between the spec-branch artefact and the shipped artefact, defeating the co-load-bearing review benefit above. `shared/contracts/README.md` carries a parallel spec-branch warning so anyone reaching the contracts directory through the README has the same context as readers of this section.

Note for cross-model review: codex review against the cumulative spec-branch diff (`origin/main` baseline) repeatedly surfaces this concern because the reviewer reads the JSON files in isolation and cannot see the §4.0 / README treatment unless those documents are themselves in the diff. The treatment above is the project's sustained answer; the design call has been settled twice on the spec branch (§4 patch round-2 and again on the cumulative-diff round-4) and is not pivot-pending.

### 4.1 Authoring conventions inherited from v3.6.2

The two templates follow the v3.6.2 `shared/contracts/reviewer/*.json` conventions:

- `contract_id` matches `^[a-z_]+/[a-z_]+/v\d+$` (schema rule). Writer: `academic_paper/writer_full/v1`. Evaluator: `academic_paper/evaluator_full/v1`. The first segment names the consumer skill (`academic_paper`) rather than the role (`reviewer`), keeping the convention that the path identifies the artefact's home directory under `shared/contracts/`.
- `baseline_version` is `v3.6.6` for both templates (the ARS suite version that introduces them). The `baseline_version` regex `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` accepts `v3.6.6` directly.
- `panel_size` is **omitted** from both templates (per §3.3.5 — single-agent generators do not have a panel; the field is no longer top-level required).
- `acceptance_dimensions[].description` is one sentence, ≤ 1.5 lines wrapped, mirroring reviewer template prose density.
- `failure_conditions[].expression` references dimension priority and score band ('pass' / 'warn' / 'block') in natural language, matching the synthesizer-recognised vocabulary in `academic-paper-reviewer/references/sprint_contract_protocol.md` §4. Generator-mode templates extend that vocabulary with mode-specific verbs (writer: "self-repair", "escalate"; evaluator: "request revision", "dissent note", "reviewer stage") that §7's lint surface and `sprint_contract_protocol.md` extension covers.
- `failure_conditions[].severity` is an ordinal anchor (not absolute), aligned to v3.6.2 reviewer ranges so the synthesizer's severity-precedence resolution behaves consistently across modes: 95 = round-2-exhausted escalation (generator-only; must outrank mandatory-block to break in-pair revision loop — see §4.3 F5 rationale), 90 = mandatory hard-block, 75 = mandatory warn (writer-only F4 — see §4.2), 70 = mandatory warn / aggregation (evaluator F2 / reviewer F2), 60 = high block, 55 = normal-priority block (evaluator-only F6 — see §4.3), 50 = evaluator dissent note (mid-tier non-mandatory warn), 40 = high warn, 10 = F0 accept.
- `override_ladder` and `agent_amendments` are omitted by default (both schema-optional). The shipped reviewer templates also omit them; v3.6.6 preserves that posture.
- `cross_reviewer_quantifier` is omitted from every `failure_conditions[]` entry (per §3.3.2 — required only for reviewer modes). Generator-mode runtime treats every condition as evaluated by a single agent (the writer for `writer_full`, the evaluator for `evaluator_full`), so no panel aggregation is involved.

### 4.2 Writer template — `shared/contracts/writer/full.json`

**Purpose**. Gates `draft_writer_agent` Phase 4 with a paper-blind Phase 4a pre-commitment (acceptance criteria paraphrase, per §3.4.1 — paper-specific section outlines / CER chains / word counts are read from upstream runtime artefacts at Phase 4a / 4b runtime, not committed in the frozen contract baseline) before paper-visible drafting in Phase 4b. Encodes the seven Quality Gates from `academic-paper/agents/draft_writer_agent.md` as `acceptance_dimensions`, with four writer-specific failure conditions plus F0 accept.

**`acceptance_dimensions`** — seven dimensions extracted from draft_writer Quality Gates:

| id | name | description | priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | section_completeness | Every section in the Structure Architect's approved outline is written; no `[MATERIAL GAP]` placeholders remain unresolved at handoff to citation_compliance. | mandatory |
| D2 | citation_density | Every factual claim carries at least one citation; uncited claims either gain a source or are rewritten with hedging language. | mandatory |
| D3 | argument_blueprint_fidelity | Each section follows the CER chains delivered by argument_builder_agent (the Argument Blueprint runtime artefact); topic sentences match the claim, evidence cites assigned sources, and explanation links back to the section purpose. The Argument Blueprint, not the contract, is the source of CER chains. | mandatory |
| D4 | total_word_count | Final draft total stays within ±10% of the target declared in the Paper Configuration Record. | high |
| D5 | per_section_word_count | Each section stays within ±15% of the per-section allocation declared in the Paper Configuration Record. | high |
| D6 | paragraph_structure | At least 80% of body paragraphs follow TEEL (Topic / Evidence / Explanation / Link). Introduction-first and conclusion-last paragraphs are exempt. | normal |
| D7 | register_consistency | Academic register holds throughout; no colloquial mixing; discipline-appropriate phrasing per the Paper Configuration Record. | normal |

`revision_response` is intentionally **not** a v3.6.6 dimension. It is a revision-mode behavior; v3.6.6 covers `academic-paper/full` mode only (§1 in-scope item 1, §2.1 Q1). Revision-mode dimensions and contract are deferred to v3.6.7+ / v3.7.x. `transition_completeness` is folded into D6 description rather than a separate dimension to keep dimension granularity at the same level as the reviewer template (5 dimensions in `reviewer/full.json`); transitions are a sub-property of paragraph structure, not an independent quality axis.

**`pre_commitment_artifacts`**. Writer Phase 4a paper-blind output, structured per §3.4.1:

- `acceptance_criteria_paraphrase.minimum_dimensions: "all"` — writer must paraphrase all seven dimensions before reading the paper context, mirroring the reviewer template's `paraphrase_minimum_dimensions: "all"`.
- Three earlier-draft subcomponents — `structure_plan.section_outline`, `structure_plan.word_count_per_section`, and `argument_plan.claim_evidence_chains` — were intentionally **not** included in `pre_commitment_artifacts`. They are paper-specific runtime values that vary across papers (different paper types, different word-count targets, different argument structures), and embedding them in the frozen contract baseline would either force orchestrators to mutate the frozen contract before Phase 4a (violating v3.6.2's frozen-baseline invariant) or hard-code IMRaD assumptions onto non-IMRaD paper types (literature reviews, theoretical, case study, policy brief — all supported by writer_full per `draft_writer_agent.md`'s Paper Type Adjustments table). Source-of-truth for each:
  - **Section outline** lives in the Structure Architect's approved outline (`structure_architect_agent` output, the Paper Outline runtime artefact). D1 section_completeness is evaluated against that outline.
  - **Per-section word counts** live in the Paper Configuration Record (`intake_agent` output). D4 / D5 phrase their gates as "stays within ±N% of the PCR target".
  - **CER chains** live in the Argument Blueprint (`argument_builder_agent` output). D3 argument_blueprint_fidelity is evaluated against the Blueprint's CER chains, not against a contract-embedded copy.
  The §3.4.1 schema reflects this: `pre_commitment_artifacts.required` lists only `acceptance_criteria_paraphrase`. The `pre_commitment_artifacts` object shape is preserved (rather than promoting `acceptance_criteria_paraphrase` to top level) so v3.7.x can extend the structured object with new invariant, paper-agnostic policy without an architecture refactor. See §8.2 R2 for the eviction pattern as a forward-looking authoring rule.

**`failure_conditions`**:

| id | severity | expression | action |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | 90 | any mandatory dimension scores 'block' | `writer_decision=escalate_to_evaluator` |
| F4 | 75 | any mandatory dimension scores 'warn' | `writer_decision=revise_in_phase_4b` |
| F2 | 60 | any high-priority dimension scores 'block' | `writer_decision=revise_in_phase_4b` |
| F3 | 40 | any high-priority dimension scores 'warn' | `writer_decision=revise_in_phase_4b` |
| F0 | 10 | every mandatory dimension scores 'pass' | `writer_decision=accept` |

Severity ordering rationale:

- F1 mandatory-block uses `escalate_to_evaluator` (not `revise_in_phase_4b`) because mandatory dimension blocks generally signal an upstream gap the writer cannot close in-phase: a missing source for D1 / D2, or a CER chain that the argument_builder did not deliver for D3. The writer hands off to the evaluator, whose `disagreement_handling` (§4.3) decides whether to request_revision (loops back to writer with concrete additions), accept_with_dissent_note (proceeds, logs the gap), or flag_for_reviewer_stage (routes to the external `academic-paper-reviewer` skill).
- F4 mandatory-warn uses `revise_in_phase_4b` (not `escalate_to_evaluator`) because mandatory-warn cases are recoverable in-phase: D1 section_completeness 'warn' typically means a section is short but written (writer expands); D2 citation_density 'warn' typically means uncited factual claims that can be either cited from the assigned source list or rewritten with hedging language; D3 argument_blueprint_fidelity 'warn' means partial CER chain coverage that the writer can complete within Phase 4b. F4 sits between F1 (90) and F2 (60) at severity 75 to mark mandatory dimensions as more severe than high-priority dimensions even at the warn band, while still routing to local self-repair rather than upstream escalation. Without F4, a paper with mandatory-dim 'warn' but no 'block' on any dimension would fall through every other condition and leave the writer phase without a terminal action — a state the synthesizer cannot resolve.
- F2 / F3 high-priority blocks and warns use `revise_in_phase_4b` because high-priority dimensions in this template (`total_word_count`, `per_section_word_count`) are local-state failures the writer can resolve by trimming or expanding within the same phase without upstream replanning. The Paper Configuration Record carries the per-section word-count target; F2 ('block') corresponds to deviations beyond ±20% of the PCR target (writer must restructure section evidence budget); F3 ('warn') corresponds to ±15-20% deviations (writer adjusts paragraph length or transition density).
- F0 severity 10 mirrors the reviewer template; the synthesizer's severity-precedence resolution selects F0 only when no higher-severity F-condition fires.

The five-condition shape (F1 / F4 / F2 / F3 / F0) extends `reviewer/full.json`'s four-condition F1 / F2 / F3 / F0 ordinal density with one additional condition (F4) that closes the mandatory-warn gap surfaced during cross-template codex review. There is still no F-condition for normal-priority dimensions (D6 / D7) — by v3.6.2 convention, normal-priority dimensions inform the synthesizer's narrative but do not on their own fire a failure condition. Synthesizer behavior for normal-priority dimensions is documented in `sprint_contract_protocol.md` §4 and unchanged by v3.6.6.

### 4.3 Evaluator template — `shared/contracts/evaluator/full.json`

**Purpose**. Gates `peer_reviewer_agent` Phase 6 with a paper-blind Phase 6a pre-commitment (contract paraphrase + scoring plan + disagreement-handling plan) before paper-visible evaluation in Phase 6b. Encodes the five-dimension peer-review rubric from `academic-paper/agents/peer_reviewer_agent.md` as `acceptance_dimensions`, with six evaluator-specific failure conditions plus F0 accept.

**`acceptance_dimensions`** — five dimensions mirroring the existing peer-review rubric:

| id | name | description | priority |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | originality | Novel contribution to the field; new framework, new evidence, or unique perspective; not a restatement of existing work. | high |
| D2 | methodological_rigor | Research design matches the question; method is appropriate, replicable, and limitations are disclosed. | mandatory |
| D3 | evidence_sufficiency | Every claim is supported by adequate citations or data; no unsupported assertions; no cherry-picking. | mandatory |
| D4 | argument_coherence | Logic flows across sections; transitions are smooth; thesis-to-conclusion alignment holds; no self-contradiction. | high |
| D5 | writing_quality | Language is clear and precise; grammar, formatting, and citation style are consistent; readability fits the venue. | normal |
