### Step 2 — Write the §3.5 subsection

Target: ≤55 lines (5-line buffer under the 60-line gate). Structure:

```markdown
### 3.5 Audit Artifact Gate (v3.6.7 Step 6)

**Trigger.** At every stage transition where a v3.6.7 downstream agent
(synthesis_agent, research_architect_agent survey-designer mode, or
report_compiler_agent abstract-only mode) just completed a deliverable.

**Decision policy.** Read or merge an audit_artifact[] entry for the
just-completed deliverable, validate against eleven gating checks (§5.2
spec), apply ship/block per verdict status:
- PASS → proceed to next stage; append audit line to FULL checkpoint.
- MINOR → MANDATORY checkpoint; surface findings; user response: iterate.
- MATERIAL → BLOCK; surface findings; user response: another_round /
  ship_with_known_residue / abort_stage (per §5.4).

**Procedure.** Path A → Path B fall-through:
- Path A re-verifies an already-merged persisted entry (recovery on
  resume / re-transition). Failure phases: P-PA-precond, P-PA-schema,
  P-PA-gate, P-PA-verdict-schema, P-PA-verdict-mirror, P-PA-stale-late,
  P-PA-supersede-preempt — all fall through to Path B with reason carried.
- Path B merges a fresh proposal file (first-time merge or supersede a
  failed Path A entry). Failure phases: P-PB-empty, P-PB-supersede-missing,
  P-PB-ambig, P-PB-proposal-schema, P-PB-audit-failed, P-PB-gate,
  P-PB-verdict-schema, P-PB-verdict-mirror, P-PB-stale-late, P-PB-dup-early,
  P-PB-dup-other, P-PB-dup-late, P-PB-snapshot, P-PB-persisted-schema,
  P-PB-passport-write, P-PB-consume-fail, P-PB-crash — most are terminal
  BLOCK; some recover (B1 restart, A7 ship, B10 read existing).

Full procedural detail (A1–A7, B1–B11, A1.5 supersession preflight, B1a
tuple-match recovery, B8a/B8b/B8c late barriers, P-PA-* / P-PB-* failure
state inventory) lives in spec §5.6. Orchestrator follows that procedure
exactly; the inventory is the implementation contract.

**Hard rules.**
- Audit gate cannot be skipped — no "skip audit" option in checkpoint
  command vocabulary.
- Audit gate runs BEFORE collaboration_depth_agent observer dispatch and
  BEFORE integrity_verification_agent dispatch — first transition-time check.
- A verdict_status: PASS does NOT imply integrity check is skipped. Stage
  2.5 / 4.5 integrity gates remain mandatory per existing §3 Hard
  boundaries rule 9.

**Failure surfacing.** Any block message uses the standard FULL/MANDATORY
checkpoint visual (━━━ separator). Block message MUST include: why blocked

```

# ARS v3.7.2 — Trust Provenance Hardening (SHA Gate v2 + Wrapper Enforcement)

> **Status (2026-05-10):** **DESIGN-ONLY, NOT YET IMPLEMENTED.** Follow-up to v3.7.1 (`docs/design/2026-04-30-ars-v3.6.8-trust-provenance-and-drift-transparency-spec.md`). Targets the architectural attack surfaces surfaced by `/codex challenge` round-1 against PR #76 (Step 0+1) and PR #78 (Step 2), tracked in [issue #77](https://github.com/Imbad0202/academic-research-skills/issues/77) and [issue #79](https://github.com/Imbad0202/academic-research-skills/issues/79).
>
> **Release semver:** `v3.7.2` (forward release on v3.7 line). Filename uses release-date date stamp (`2026-05-10`); no roadmap-slot decoupling needed because this spec does not occupy a new roadmap slot — it amends v3.7.1's Step 0 + Step 2 acceptance contracts.
>
> ---
>
> **Why this spec exists:** v3.7.1 PR #76 (Step 0+1) ran `/codex review` 11 rounds to 0-finding sustained, then `/codex challenge` round-1 surfaced **3 P1 + 5 P2 + 2 P3** new attack surfaces against the SHA byte-equivalence gate. v3.7.1 PR #78 (Step 2) ran `/codex review` 14 rounds to 0-finding sustained, then `/codex challenge` round-1 surfaced **2 P1 + 2 P2** against the Scope Report wrapper enforcement and render-side count computation paths.
>
> The `review` rounds confirmed each PR ships correctly against the **stated** v3.7.1 contract. The `challenge` rounds revealed that **the v3.7.1 contract itself has gaps** — the SHA gate's "regex-anchored heading extractor + git-log-derivation + advisory fallback" architecture has structural bypass surfaces (duplicate marker / fork PR / shallow clone / advisory degradation under CI), and the Scope Report contract was enforced on **input prompt** (template lint) but not on **output verdict** (parse_audit_verdict + run_codex_audit.sh wrapper) or on **render-time count derivation** (audit_snapshot still leaves `<N_total>` placeholders for codex to fill).
>
> Per memory `feedback_codex_workflow_consolidated.md` (review-vs-challenge value split): review catches implementation-vs-spec drift; challenge catches architecture-vs-attacker. v3.7.1 closed the review surface; v3.7.2 closes the challenge surface.
>
> Per memory `feedback_architectural_inflection_after_repeated_p1.md`: when 3+ P1 in the same finding family land, escalate from whack-a-mole patch to architectural redesign rather than continuing to add counter-examples.
>
> ---
>
> **What this spec changes:**
>
> | Section | v3.7.1 contract | v3.7.2 contract |
> |---|---|---|
> | §3.1 SHA gate baseline derivation | `git log -1 HEAD <manifest path>` (HEAD-rooted) | `git log -1 origin/<pr-base> -- <manifest path>` (PR-base-rooted) |
> | §3.1 SHA gate heading extractor | `re.search` first match against `^## PATTERN PROTECTION (v3.6.7)` regex | Markdown-aware AST (markdown-it-py + explicit YAML frontmatter pre-strip) MANDATORY in production; strict-single regex demoted to fallback flag only (round-7+9 cap rule, see banner) |
> | §3.1 SHA gate base-ref resolution | Advisory degradation on missing `origin/HEAD` / unset `GITHUB_BASE_REF` | Fail-closed under CI (`$CI` or `$GITHUB_ACTIONS` set); advisory only for local detached state |
> | §3.1 SHA gate byte source | HEAD bytes from `head_path.read_bytes()` (worktree) vs base bytes from `git show <commit>:<path>` | Both sides use `git show <commit>:<path>` to eliminate CRLF normalization variance |
> | §3.2 Scope Report enforcement | Input-prompt template lint only | Wrapper output validation (`parse_audit_verdict.py` requires Section 0 in output); render-side count computation from `literature_corpus[]` frontmatter (not LLM-filled placeholder) |
> | §3.2 Scope Report lint shape | Substring `in` check for required fields and aggregate split | Line-anchored regex per field with placeholder/value semantics |
>
> ---
>
> **What this spec does NOT change:**
>
> - v3.7.1 §3.1 D1 frontmatter schema (7 entry-stored fields + 2 derived) — already MERGED main `5f107c7`, no schema change needed
> - v3.7.1 §3.2 D2 firm rules 1+2 (must-before-summary; aggregate "PASSED" forbidden) — already MERGED main `fed3eba`
> - v3.7.1 §3.3-3.5 (D3 cite-time / D4 drift log / D5 retrieval fallback) — Step 3a/3b already MERGED main `23fb6ac`/`1d0c862`; Step 3c-3e + 4-7 still in v3.7.1 implementation roadmap
> - v3.6.7 PATTERN PROTECTION blocks on the three protected agent files — boundary preserved; v3.7.2 only modifies v3.7.1-tagged surfaces
>
> **Boundary preservation gate:** v3.6.7 lint regression (`check_v3_6_7_pattern_protection.py` 12/12 + 58 mutation tests PASS) is a hard gate on every v3.7.2 PR. v3.7.1 lint regression (`check_v3_6_8_pattern_protection.py` + `check_v3_6_8_audit_scope_block.py`) is also a hard gate (must continue to PASS for the v3.7.1 input-side protections).

**Round-7 Codex Sustaining Check + Architectural Upgrade (2026-05-10, gpt-5.5 high reasoning, 1 P1 + 1 P2):**

Round-7 surfaced 1 P1 (Setext whitespace variants) + 1 P2 (placeholder regex too narrow). Critically, this is the FOURTH consecutive round (R1 P1-4 / R5 P1-1 / R6 P1-1 / R7 P1-1) finding lexical-enumeration gaps in the strict-single mode regex — each round closes one variant family and exposes the next. Per memory `feedback_lint_cap_rule_when_lexical_enumeration_loops` (5+ rounds same lint family triggers cap rule upgrade — and we are at 4 with same convergence pattern), this round promotes the architectural fix from Out-of-Scope to mandatory default:

| F-id | Finding | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| P1-1 (R7) | Setext whitespace variants (paragraph + underline both allow 0-3 leading spaces and trailing whitespace per CommonMark §4.3) slip through round-6 strict-single regex `^=+$` / `^-+$` — decoy + Setext-with-whitespace rewrite still bypasses | **§3.1 axis C: Markdown-aware mode PROMOTED to mandatory default** (markdown-it-py vendored or in requirements.txt; CI fails closed if missing). **The architectural upgrade is the load-bearing change of round-7.** Strict-single regex was always a stopgap; rounds 1+5+6+7 demonstrated the lexical-enumeration arms race converges on Markdown-aware AST being the only stable solution. Strict-single stays as a documented fallback for ops continuity but is explicitly NOT relied on in production.

## 1. Background

v3.7.1 shipped two cross-cutting protections via PR #76 (Step 0+1) and PR #78 (Step 2):

- **Step 0 SHA byte-equivalence gate** (`scripts/check_v3_6_8_pattern_protection.py`): asserts that the v3.6.7-protected PATTERN PROTECTION blocks in the three downstream agents stay byte-equivalent across PR HEAD vs the v3.6.7 manifest's most recent modifying commit.
- **Step 2 Scope Report block** (`shared/templates/codex_audit_multifile_template.md` + `scripts/check_v3_6_8_audit_scope_block.py` + render-side parity in `scripts/audit_snapshot.py::render_prompt`): adds Section 0 disclosure to audit reports stating coverage breakdown (verified-against-source vs description-internally-consistent vs unaudited-due-to-missing-source).

Both PRs ran `/codex review` to 0-finding-sustained (11 and 14 rounds respectively) and merged to main. Post-merge `/codex challenge` adversarial passes — designed to attack architecture, not check spec drift — surfaced finding clusters that the review track had not probed:

**SHA gate (PR #76 challenge round-1, 93k tokens):**
- 3 P1 false-negative attack surfaces: duplicate-marker bypass via `re.search` first-match, anti-self-baseline guard advisory degradation in CI, base commit derived from HEAD history not PR base
- 5 P2 false-positive / correctness gaps: heading regex not Markdown-aware, worktree-vs-`git show` byte mismatch on CRLF auto-normalization, lossy UTF-8 decode, `git log -1` rename-blind, fork PR remote ambiguity
- 2 P3 informational: Unicode normalization low-risk, empty commits / force-push low direct risk

**Scope Report (PR #78 challenge round-1, 1.39M tokens):**
- 2 P1 contract-end-to-end gaps: `parse_audit_verdict.py` accepts legacy Section 6-only verdict shape (audit can omit Section 0 and still classify PASS), `audit_snapshot.render_prompt()` leaves placeholders for codex to fill (LLM-fabricated counts re-introduce the disclosure-fabrication surface D2 was designed to close)
- 2 P2 lint precision: aggregate-split substring-only (prose mention satisfies), required-field substring-only (placeholder semantic not enforced)

Per memory `feedback_codex_workflow_consolidated.md`, this is the canonical review-vs-challenge value split: review confirms implementation matches the stated contract; challenge probes whether the contract itself has architectural gaps. v3.7.1 contracts are correctly implemented; the contracts have gaps. v3.7.2 closes those gaps.

## 2. Goal & Non-Goals

### 2.1 Goal

Harden v3.7.1 D1+D2 attack surfaces by:

1. Re-rooting SHA gate baseline derivation from HEAD-history to PR-base-history
2. Eliminating worktree-side byte comparison in favor of unified `git show` reads on both sides
3. Failing closed under CI when base-ref or merge-base resolution fails (replaces silent advisory degradation)
4. Making the heading extractor MANDATORY Markdown-aware AST (markdown-it-py with explicit YAML frontmatter pre-strip) per round-7+9 cap rule; strict-single regex demoted to fallback only
5. Extending Scope Report enforcement from input-prompt-template-only to **end-to-end**: render-side count computation from frontmatter + wrapper-side output validation
6. Tightening the audit-scope-block lint from substring `in` checks to line-anchored regex with shape enforcement

Target outcome: codex challenge round-2 against the v3.7.2 implementation returns ≤1 P2 and 0 P1 across both attack surfaces (SHA gate + Scope Report wrapper).

### 2.2 Non-Goals (out of v3.7.2 scope)

- **No new D-pattern.** v3.7.2 does not introduce new trust-provenance patterns; D6+ candidates stay future work.
- **No D3-D5 implementation.** Step 3c-3e (cite-time provenance for standalone modes) and Steps 4-7 stay on the v3.7.1 implementation roadmap. v3.7.2 is orthogonal.
- **No v3.6.7 boundary mutation.** v3.7.2 lint changes scope is confined to v3.7.1-tagged surfaces. v3.6.7-protected agent file blocks remain byte-equivalent under v3.6.7 lint regression.
- **No mass refactor of `parse_audit_verdict.py`.** v3.7.2 extends the parser with Section 0 requirement; the legacy Section 6 parser stays in place (additive, not replacement).
- **No new env-flag opt-out.** Hardening rules apply uniformly. Local non-CI runs may still see advisory behavior for ergonomics; the `$CI` / `$GITHUB_ACTIONS` detection is the single switch.
- **No automated remediation of past audit reports.** Historical reports that ran under the legacy Scope-Report-omitted path stay as-is; v3.7.2 protects forward only.

## 3. Pattern Inventory

### 3.1 SHA Gate v2 — closing #77 attack surfaces

**Pattern:** v3.7.1 `check_v3_6_8_pattern_protection.py` defends the v3.6.7 PATTERN PROTECTION block against silent mutation, but its baseline derivation, byte source, base-ref resolution, and heading extraction all have first-class bypasses.

**Mechanism — three architectural axes:**

**(A) Baseline rooting axis.** `_v3_6_7_base_commit()` runs `git log -1 --format=%H <manifest path>` against the local working tree's HEAD history. A PR branch that has not pulled latest main can pass against the OLD baseline even when main has since received a v3.6.7 manifest amendment. Cherry-pick / squash-sync of base changes can also trip false-fail. The fix is to root derivation at `origin/<pr-base>`, not HEAD.

**(B) Byte source axis.** HEAD-side bytes come from `head_path.read_bytes()` (worktree). Base-side bytes come from `git show <commit>:<path>`. On a checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` (Windows default; some macOS configs), worktree CRLF differs from committed LF. The blob itself is byte-equivalent, but the lint rejects the PR. The fix is to read both sides via `git show HEAD:<path>` so the comparison is between **committed** bytes on both sides.

**(C) Heading extraction axis.** `_extract_block_bytes` uses `re.search(r"^## PATTERN PROTECTION \(v3\.6\.7\)$", ..., re.MULTILINE)` and takes the first match. An attacker can:
- Insert a byte-for-byte copy of the original protected block ABOVE the real block. The lint hashes the unmutated copy and passes; the real block (mutated) escapes detection.
- Place the marker text inside a fenced code block, HTML comment, or YAML block scalar. The first match is the in-prose occurrence rather than the structural heading.
- Use Setext-style heading (`PATTERN PROTECTION (v3.6.7)\n===========================`) which the regex does not match at all.

The fix is **Markdown-aware parser MANDATORY in production** (round-7 codex P1-1 amend, lexical-enumeration-loop cap rule; round-10 codex P1-1 amend, this mechanism description aligned with mandate): use `markdown-it-py` AST with explicit YAML frontmatter pre-strip (round-9 P1-2 amend); skip fenced code / HTML comments / indented code blocks per CommonMark spec; recognize all CommonMark §4.2 ATX forms (trailing `#`, 1-3 leading spaces, space-or-tab whitespace) AND all §4.3 Setext forms (1-3 leading spaces, trailing whitespace). Closes all of (C) with proper handling. Strict-single regex rejection (collect-all + reject-if-count!=1) is **acknowledged-incomplete** — rounds R1+R5+R6+R7 demonstrated that lexical enumeration of CommonMark variants does not converge (each round closes one variant family and exposes the next); strict-single is retained ONLY as a `--fallback` flag for AST-unavailable environments and is NOT the production path. See §3.1 axis C (Block extraction) below for the full mandatory contract.

**Protection — v3.7.2 SHA gate v2:**

```
1. Base-ref resolution:
   - Read GITHUB_BASE_REF (CI) or detect via `git symbolic-ref --quiet --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`
   - Under CI ($CI or $GITHUB_ACTIONS set): fail-closed if resolution fails
   - Local detached state: advisory pass with WARNING log (preserves ergonomics)

2. Baseline commit derivation:
   - Compute via `git log -1 --format=%H origin/<base-ref> -- scripts/v3_6_7_inversion_manifest.json`
   - NOT `git log -1 ... HEAD ...` (the v3.7.1 derivation)
   - Fork PR detection (round-3 codex P1-1 amend, aligned with §3.1 firm rule below): when `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.event.pull_request.base.repo.full_name` (or equivalently `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork == true`), require an `upstream` remote pointing at `github.event.pull_request.base.repo.clone_url` and use `upstream/<base-ref>` for baseline derivation, NOT `origin/<base-ref>`. Comparing `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` or `GITHUB_HEAD_REF` against base.repo is INCORRECT (`GITHUB_REPOSITORY` IS the base repo under `pull_request` workflow, and `GITHUB_HEAD_REF` is only a branch name).

3. Block extraction (architectural decision — round-7 codex amend, lexical-enumeration-loop cap rule per memory `feedback_lint_cap_rule_when_lexical_enumeration_loops`): rounds 1+5+6+7 each found additional CommonMark whitespace/variant attack surfaces against the strict-single regex (Setext base, ATX trailing `#`, ATX leading 0-3 spaces, ATX tab whitespace, Setext leading 0-3 spaces / trailing whitespace on paragraph and underline). The lexical-enumeration approach is bottoming out — each round closes one variant and exposes the next. **Markdown-aware mode is now MANDATORY for v3.7.2 implementation**, with strict-single mode demoted to a fallback safety net for legitimate maintainer test environments where markdown-it-py is unavailable. Both modes MUST be implemented; CI workflow MUST run Markdown-aware mode by default.
   - **Markdown-aware mode (MANDATORY default; round-7 amend; round-9 codex P1-2 amend, frontmatter pre-processing pinned)**: pre-process the file by stripping YAML frontmatter BEFORE invoking the AST parser (frontmatter is between `---` markers at file head per common Markdown convention; markdown-it-py CommonMark parsing does NOT skip frontmatter automatically — without explicit stripping, an attacker could place a decoy `## PATTERN PROTECTION (v3.6.7)` heading inside frontmatter, the AST counts it as a real heading, and the duplicate-marker bypass reopens). Then parse via `markdown-it-py` (Python; vendored or pinned in `requirements.txt` so CI fails closed if missing); enumerate all heading nodes with text content `PATTERN PROTECTION (v3.6.7)` (case-sensitive, exact match after AST normalization); ParseError if count != 1. The AST automatically handles all CommonMark §4.2 ATX forms (trailing `#` sequence, 1-3 leading spaces, space-or-tab whitespace) AND all CommonMark §4.3 Setext forms (1-3 leading spaces on paragraph and underline, trailing whitespace, blank-line-before-paragraph requirement). AST also automatically skips fenced code blocks, HTML comments, and indented code blocks per CommonMark spec (but NOT YAML frontmatter — that requires the explicit pre-strip step above). This closes the lexical-enumeration-loop attack surface AND the frontmatter-decoy bypass.
   - **Strict-single mode (fallback, NOT default; testing/audit only)**: collect all of (a) ATX H2 lines matching `^ {0,3}##[ \t]+PATTERN PROTECTION \(v3\.6\.7\)([ \t]+#+)?[ \t]*$`, (b) ATX H1 lines matching `^ {0,3}#[ \t]+PATTERN PROTECTION \(v3\.6\.7\)([ \t]+#+)?[ \t]*$`, (c) Setext H1 form: paragraph line matching `^ {0,3}PATTERN PROTECTION \(v3\.6\.7\)[ \t]*$` IMMEDIATELY followed by underline matching `^ {0,3}=+[ \t]*$` (round-7 amend: paragraph allows 0-3 leading spaces + trailing whitespace; underline allows 0-3 leading spaces + trailing whitespace per CommonMark §4.3), (d) Setext H2 form: same paragraph regex followed by `^ {0,3}-+[ \t]*$`. ParseError if total count != 1. Skip fenced code / HTML comments / YAML frontmatter / indented-by-4+ code blocks. **Strict-single mode is acknowledged-incomplete** — known limitations include CommonMark blank-line-before-Setext-paragraph rules, hard-line-break vs paragraph-continuation distinction, and link-reference-definition disambiguation. CI MUST NOT rely on strict-single in production; it exists only as a `--fallback` flag for environments where markdown-it-py cannot be installed (rare; document as ops escape hatch). Production audits MUST run Markdown-aware mode.

4. Byte comparison:
   - HEAD-side: `git show HEAD:<path>` (NOT `<path>.read_bytes()`)
   - Base-side: `git show <baseline commit>:<path>` (unchanged)
   - Both sides: same extractor function, same SHA-256 hash function
```

**Three firm rules (in addition to v3.7.1 §3.1; round-1 codex P2-1 promoted to firm rule):**

- The SHA gate MUST fail-closed under CI when base-ref resolution or merge-base computation fails. Advisory degradation under CI is forbidden.
- Both HEAD-side and base-side bytes MUST come from `git show <commit>:<path>`. Worktree byte reads are forbidden in the comparison path.
- **Fork PR baseline MUST resolve to the upstream repository, never to the contributor fork** (round-1 codex P2-1 amend, promoted from §6 deferral; round-2 codex P1-1 amend, detection condition corrected): under the standard `pull_request` workflow, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is always the base repository (the repo the workflow is defined in) — comparing it to `github.event.pull_request.base.repo.full_name` is always false and never detects a fork. The correct fork-detection condition is `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name != github.event.pull_request.base.repo.full_name` (head repo differs from base repo) OR equivalently `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork == true`. When CI detects a fork PR, the workflow MUST add an `upstream` remote pointing at `github.event.pull_request.base.repo.clone_url` (the canonical base repo's clone URL) and use `upstream/<base-ref>` for baseline derivation, NOT `origin/<base-ref>` (which on a fork checkout points at the contributor fork). Without this rule, a fork PR's `origin/<base-ref>` resolves successfully but to fork history, the CI fail-closed rule does not fire, and the SHA gate derives trust from untrusted fork content.

### 3.2 Scope Report End-to-End — closing #79 attack surfaces

**Pattern:** v3.7.1 §3.2 D2 firm rules 1+2 (must-before-summary; aggregate "PASSED" forbidden) are enforced on the **input prompt** (template lint) and on **render-time emission** (Section 0 prepended ahead of Section 1). But two ends of the pipeline leak:

- **Output-end:** `scripts/parse_audit_verdict.py` accepts legacy Section 6-only verdict shape (`Round N: 0 findings of any severity. Convergence reached.`). A codex run can entirely omit Section 0 from its output, end with the canonical zero-findings line, and `scripts/run_codex_audit.sh` classifies the run as PASS.
- **Render-end:** `scripts/audit_snapshot.py::render_prompt` inserts Section 0 verbatim from the template, leaving the placeholders `<N_total>`, `<N_with_source>`, `<N_without_source>`, and `<comma-separated list>` for codex to fill at audit time. The spec §3.2 line 129 explicitly says "Coverage breakdown is computable from frontmatter (count entries with `source_acquired: true` vs `false`)" — but the snapshot does not pre-fill these counts. Letting the LLM fill them re-introduces the same hallucination surface D2 was designed to close.

**Mechanism:** the v3.7.1 contract pinned three layers — template, lint, render-side regression test — but did not pin **wrapper-side output validation** or **render-side count computation**. The Scope Report ends up enforced on *what we send to codex* but not on *what codex returns* and not on *what numbers go into the disclosure*.

**Protection — v3.7.2 Scope Report v2:**

```
A. Render-side count computation (closing render-end leak):
   - REQUIREMENT (round-1 codex P1-2 amend): render_prompt() takes a NEW required parameter `passport_path: str` (and parses it inline) OR a pre-parsed `literature_corpus: list[dict]` argument. The caller (run_codex_audit.sh + scripts/audit_snapshot.py CLI entry) MUST pass exactly one passport. The signature change is breaking; v3.7.2 implementation PR-B updates run_codex_audit.sh + the CLI front-end together with audit_snapshot.py in the same commit.
   - Fail-closed semantics: if `passport_path` is missing, points at non-existent file, fails YAML/JSON parse, or carries no `literature_corpus[]` field, render_prompt() raises ScopeReportRenderError before the prompt is sent. run_codex_audit.sh treats ScopeReportRenderError as a wrapper FAIL (NOT a degraded "Section 0 omitted" path). No silent fallback to LLM-filled placeholders.
   - Computes (round-1 codex P2-2 amend: every value other than literal `true` is treated as missing-source — conservative bucketing for legacy / malformed entries that lack the field or have null):
     - N_total = len(literature_corpus)
     - N_with_source = count where source_acquired is literal True (Python bool, not truthy string)
     - N_without_source = N_total - N_with_source (covers false, "none", missing field, null, and any non-true value)
     - refcodes = [entry.citation_key for entry in literature_corpus if source_acquired is not True]
   - Substitutes computed values into Section 0 placeholders BEFORE the prompt is sent to codex
   - Codex still verifies internal consistency but cannot fabricate the disclosure

B. Wrapper-side output validation (closing output-end leak):
   - parse_audit_verdict.py requires Section 0 Scope Report block in the audit output
   - Uses an OUTPUT-MODE regex set (separate from the template-lint regex set; round-1 codex P1-3 amend; round-7 codex P2-1 amend, placeholder pattern broadened to cover multi-word placeholders like `<comma-separated list>`): the template-lint regex allows `<N_total>` placeholder syntax because the template legitimately contains placeholders before render-time substitution; the output-mode regex MUST reject any substring matching `<[^>\n]+>` (any angle-bracket-delimited token, allowing spaces and any non-newline content — covers single-word placeholders `<N_total>`, multi-word placeholders `<comma-separated list>`, hyphenated `<some-text-here>`, and any future placeholder format). At each numeric field, require an integer literal `\d+` (rejects bare `<N_total>` AND any placeholder containing the field name). At the refcodes field, require either an empty list (`(none)` or empty `[]`) OR a non-empty comma-separated list of identifier tokens with NO angle-bracket placeholder. ParseError if any field still contains a placeholder.
   - **Count equality firm rule (round-1 codex P1-1 amend; promoted from §9 Q1; round-2 codex P1-2 amend, retention channel pinned; round-3 codex P1-2 amend, retention pinned BEFORE codex invocation in codex-unwritable location)**: render_prompt() computes the four canonical count fields (`n_total: int`, `n_with_source: int`, `n_without_source: int`, `refcodes: list[str]`). run_codex_audit.sh MUST capture these counts BEFORE invoking codex AND store them in a location codex cannot write (NOT under the bundle directory, NOT under the working directory codex sees). Two acceptable retention channels: (a) **in-memory hash-pin** — the wrapper holds the counts in shell variables / environment for the duration of the codex run and uses them directly at verdict-parse time; (b) **out-of-sandbox file** — write to a path outside any directory codex has write access to (e.g., `/tmp/ars_scope_counts_<run_id>.json` with restrictive permissions, NOT under the audit bundle / repo / passport directory). The wrapper MUST also pre-hash the counts JSON (SHA-256) BEFORE the codex run and verify the hash matches at verdict-parse time, rejecting any tampering. Re-reading the passport at verdict-parse time is forbidden — the passport may have changed between render and parse, and a codex output that mirrors the later counts could pass a fresh-read comparison. Inequality on any field MUST classify the audit as FAIL with `[SCOPE REPORT TAMPERING — codex modified pre-filled disclosure values]`. Equality is byte-equivalent on the integer literals and set-equivalent on the refcode list (whitespace-insensitive). This is THE protection against the disclosure-fabrication attack the v3.7.1 Q1 left open.
   - Returns ParseError (not PASS) if Section 0 absent, malformed, contains placeholders, or fails the count equality check
   - run_codex_audit.sh treats ParseError and count-mismatch as FAIL, not as ambiguous-success

C. Lint shape tightening (closing P2 substring leaks):
   - Required content fields (5; round-6 codex P2-1 amend: `**Audit scope warning:**` was dropped from round-1's regex set — restored to preserve v3.7.1 §3.2 contract that requires the warning disclosure):
     - ^\s*\*\*Total entries audited:\*\*\s+<?[\w_-]+>?\s*$
     - ^\s*\*\*Entries with retrieved original source:\*\*\s+<?[\w_-]+>?
     - ^\s*\*\*Entries description-only.*\*\*\s+<?[\w_-]+>?
     - ^\s*\*\*Affected refcodes.*\*\*\s+<?[\w,\s_-]+>?
     - ^\s*\*\*Audit scope warning:\*\*\s+\S.+$  (round-6 amend: requires non-empty warning text after the bold marker; cannot be substituted with placeholder alone since the warning is descriptive prose)
   - Aggregate-split lines (3): line-anchored regex enforcing `: PASS | FAIL` or `<count>` shape
     - ^\s*-?\s*`?verified-against-source`?\s*:\s*(PASS|FAIL)\b
     - ^\s*-?\s*`?description-internally-consistent`?\s*:\s*(PASS|FAIL)\b
     - ^\s*-?\s*`?unaudited-due-to-missing-source`?\s*:\s*<?[\w-]+>?
   - Negation guards: lines like `Do not output **Total entries audited:**` or `Note: the verified-against-source split is computed by the orchestrator` MUST NOT satisfy the lint
```

**Two firm rules (in addition to v3.7.1 §3.2):**

- The Scope Report MUST be enforced on **audit output** (wrapper-side parser) AND on **rendered prompt** (snapshot-side count substitution), not only on the input template. Substring matches do not satisfy the contract.
- Coverage counts (`N_total`, `N_with_source`, `N_without_source`) MUST be computed from `literature_corpus[]` frontmatter at render time. Letting the LLM fill the placeholders is forbidden — it re-opens the disclosure-fabrication surface.

Add `markdown-it-py` to `requirements.txt`; CI fails closed if missing. Implement strict-single mode as `--fallback` flag for AST-unavailable environments only (acknowledged-incomplete, NOT default). Production CI MUST run Markdown-aware mode.
  - HEAD-side byte read → `git show HEAD:<path>` (replaces `head_path.read_bytes()`)

**New CI workflow steps:**

### Step H2 — Scope Report End-to-End (closes #79)

**Files to modify:**
- `scripts/audit_snapshot.py::render_prompt()` — **breaking signature change** (round-1 codex P1-2 amend): add required `passport_path: str` parameter (or pre-parsed `literature_corpus: list[dict]`). Parse passport, compute `N_total` / `N_with_source` / `N_without_source` / `refcodes` from `literature_corpus[]` per §3.2 rule A conservative bucketing; substitute computed values into Section 0 placeholders before prompt emission. Raise `ScopeReportRenderError` on missing/malformed/empty passport.
- `scripts/audit_snapshot.py` CLI front-end + caller — add `--passport <path>` argument (required when `audit_template` references Section 0); pass through to `render_prompt`. Update CLI usage docstring.
- `scripts/run_codex_audit.sh` — (a) require `--passport` argument, propagate to `audit_snapshot.py` invocation; (b) **capture the rendered counts BEFORE invoking codex** in either shell variables (in-memory) or an out-of-sandbox file (e.g., `/tmp/ars_scope_counts_<run_id>.json`, NEVER under bundle / repo / passport directory). Pre-hash the counts JSON with SHA-256 before codex runs; verify hash at verdict-parse time. Re-reading the passport at verdict-parse time is forbidden (round-2 codex P1-2 amend); reading from a codex-writable on-disk artifact is also forbidden (round-3 codex P1-2 amend); (c) treat `parse_audit_verdict` ParseError AND count-mismatch AND artifact-hash-mismatch as FAIL.
- `scripts/audit_snapshot.py::render_prompt()` — beyond the `passport_path` parameter (P1-2 amend above), MUST return the 4 count fields as a structured Python value (e.g., NamedTuple or dict alongside the rendered prompt bytes) so the wrapper captures them in-memory before codex starts. CLI front-end MAY emit `scope_counts.json` to an out-of-sandbox path passed via `--scope-counts-out <path>`, but the path MUST NOT be under any directory codex has write access to (round-3 codex P1-2 amend).
- `scripts/parse_audit_verdict.py` — require Section 0 in audit output using output-mode regex set (separate from template-lint regex; round-7 codex P2-1 amend: rejects placeholder pattern `<[^>\n]+>` covering ALL angle-bracket tokens including multi-word like `<comma-separated list>`, NOT just `<\w+>` which excludes whitespace. At numeric fields require `\d+`; at refcodes field require `(none)` / `[]` / non-empty identifier-comma-list. **Round-11 codex P2-1 amend**: output-mode regex set MUST also include the `**Audit scope warning:**` line per the same shape as template-mode rule C item 5; output-mode regex required: `^\s*\*\*Audit scope warning:\*\*\s+\S.+$`. **Round-12 codex P2-1 amend**: output-mode regex set MUST also include the three aggregate-split verdict lines (`verified-against-source: PASS|FAIL`, `description-internally-consistent: PASS|FAIL`, `unaudited-due-to-missing-source: <count>`) using the same line-anchored regex set as template-mode rule C aggregate-split; codex returning legacy aggregate "PASSED" summary instead of the three split lines MUST classify as ParseError. **Round-12 codex P2-2 amend**: warning content MUST contain the rendered `N_without_source` literal — output parser extracts the integer from the warning line and compares against the rendered count (rejects misleading content like `0 entries cannot be independently verified` when actual count is non-zero). Output-mode warning regex tightened: `^\s*\*\*Audit scope warning:\*\*\s+(\d+)\s+entries cannot be independently verified.+$` with extracted count compared via compare_scope_counts.); ParseError if Section 0 absent, malformed, contains placeholders, omits any required field including the warning, contains aggregate "PASSED" instead of split verdicts, or warning count contradicts rendered N_without_source. New `compare_scope_counts(rendered_counts, output_counts) -> bool` helper for the equality check.
- `scripts/check_v3_6_8_audit_scope_block.py` — replace substring `in` checks with line-anchored regex per H2c (template-mode regex; allows `<N_total>` placeholder syntax because templates legitimately contain placeholders).
- `shared/templates/codex_audit_multifile_template.md` — no functional change; placeholders stay (rendered at runtime). Inline comment block added (HTML comment) clarifying that placeholders are substituted by `audit_snapshot.render_prompt()` and codex MUST NOT modify the substituted values; any modification is detected by the wrapper-side count equality check.

**New tests:**
- `scripts/test_audit_snapshot_scope_count.py` — render-side test: build a synthetic bundle with N=10 corpus entries (5 source_acquired=true, 5 false); assert rendered prompt contains `**Total entries audited:** 10`, `**Entries with retrieved original source:** 5`, etc.
- `scripts/test_parse_audit_verdict_scope_required.py` — wrapper-side mutation test: feed audit output with Section 0 omitted; assert ParseError raised (not PASS classification). Same with placeholder-unfilled, fabricated-count, malformed-aggregate-split.
- `scripts/test_check_v3_6_8_audit_scope_block_shape.py` — lint shape tests: confirm `Do not output **Total entries audited:**` and `Note: the verified-against-source split is computed by the orchestrator` do NOT satisfy the lint.

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

**Risk 1:** Mandatory Markdown-aware AST mode for `_extract_block_bytes` rejects legitimate maintainer workflows that need to introduce a new H1/H2 with the exact text `PATTERN PROTECTION (v3.6.7)` elsewhere in the file.
**Mitigation:** The AST text-content match targets exact `PATTERN PROTECTION (v3.6.7)` only — exact match including the version parenthetical. Future v3.6.x version markers (e.g. v3.7.2-tagged blocks) use distinct heading text and are unaffected. If a legitimate workflow ever needs to discuss the v3.6.7 marker in prose, the convention is to use inline-code-quoted reference (`` `## PATTERN PROTECTION (v3.6.7)` ``) which the AST renders as a code span inside a paragraph, NOT as a heading node — text-content match against heading nodes does not see it.

**Risk 2:** PR-base-rooted derivation (`origin/<base-ref>`) breaks for PRs whose base branch has been deleted (rare but possible).
**Mitigation:** Fall back to advisory mode in non-CI environments. Under CI, hard-fail with `[ARS-V3.7.2 LINT ERROR: PR base ref unresolvable; cannot determine v3.6.7 baseline]`. The maintainer must rebase or update the PR base.

**Risk 3:** Render-side count computation requires `audit_snapshot.render_prompt()` to read passport schema, coupling the audit pipeline to passport-schema evolution.
**Mitigation:** v3.7.2 reads only `literature_corpus[].source_acquired` and `literature_corpus[].citation_key` — both stable since v3.6.4 / v3.7.1. Passport schema changes that touch these two fields require explicit v3.7.x spec amendment (already required for any passport schema change per CLAUDE.md `## Routing Rules`).

**Risk 4:** Wrapper-side parser requirement (Section 0 must be in output) rejects legitimate codex runs where the codex CLI failed mid-stream and the output truncated before Section 0 could emit.
**Mitigation:** ParseError vs PASS / FAIL distinction. ParseError indicates a wrapper-protocol failure (incomplete output) and is reported as FAIL with explicit `[CODEX OUTPUT INCOMPLETE — RE-RUN]` log. PASS / FAIL distinction is preserved for codex runs that completed normally.

**Risk 5:** The line-anchored regex set is fragile to template formatting changes (e.g., changing `**Total entries audited:**` to `**Total Entries Audited:**`).
**Mitigation:** Template formatting is governed by v3.7.1 §3.2 firm rules + Step 2 lint. Changes to template field names require synchronized lint regex update — both are tested under the v3.7.2 lint shape tests. The lint shape tests serve as the canonical specification of the field names.

The Markdown-aware mode also honors this. The "reject all comment occurrences" defensive posture is dropped because the structural skip is sufficient. |

# ARS v3.7.3 — Claim Faithfulness Locator + Contaminated-Source Advisory Spec

Source: https://github.com/imbad0202/academic-research-skills/blob/main/docs/design/2026-05-12-ars-v3.7.3-claim-faithfulness-and-contaminated-source-spec.md

# ARS v3.7.3 — Claim Faithfulness Locator + Contaminated-Source Advisory Spec

**Status:** Design draft (pre-codex-review)
**Date:** 2026-05-12
**Target release:** v3.7.3
**Scope:** Two orthogonal additions to v3.7.1/v3.7.2 trust-provenance — (L3-1) per-citation quote-or-locator gate, and (L3-2) contaminated-source advisory signals on `literature_corpus[]` entries.
**Precedent doc:** `2026-04-30-ars-v3.6.8-trust-provenance-and-drift-transparency-spec.md` (D1–D5), `2026-05-10-ars-v3.7.2-trust-provenance-hardening-spec.md` (H1–H2)
**External motivation:** Zhao, Wang, Stuart, De Vaan, Ginsparg, Yin (2026-05) "LLM hallucinations in the wild: Large-scale evidence from non-existent citations" (arXiv:2605.07723) — 146,932 hallucinated citations estimated for 2025 alone across arXiv / bioRxiv / SSRN / PMC; inflection point mid-2024; 85.3% of preprint hallucinations survive into the published record; Google Scholar increasingly indexes citation-only entries with no real publication backing them.

## 1. Background

v3.6.8 / v3.7.1 / v3.7.2 hardened the **trust-chain layer** between user, source artifact, and AI-produced descriptions. The frontmatter trust-strength schema (`source_acquired` / `source_verified_against_original` / `human_read_source`), the 4-cell finalizer matrix, the Two-Layer Citation Emission discipline, and the wrapper-side Scope Report enforcement together establish a defensible answer to **"is this reference real, is its description correct, and has anyone actually read it?"**

What that stack does NOT yet answer is **"does the cited reference actually support the claim the prose is making?"** — what the external literature calls *citation faithfulness* or *claim-citation alignment*. Three layers exist:

- **L1 (existence):** does the cited paper exist? Closed by v3.6.8 + bibliography_agent retrieval pipeline + Semantic Scholar lookup.
- **L2 (metadata):** are author / year / venue correct? Closed by v3.6.8 `source_verified_against_original` boolean.
- **L3 (faithfulness):** does the cited paper actually say what the prose claims it says? **Not closed.** A real, correctly-attributed reference can still be deployed to support a claim its authors never made.

Two empirical anchors confirm L3 is the load-bearing gap:

**(a) Zhao et al. 2026-05 (arXiv:2605.07723).** A corpus-scale audit of 111M references across 2.5M papers finds:
- A sharp post-2024-mid rise in non-existent (L1) citations, estimated at 146,932 fabricated references in 2025 alone across four major corpora.
- Existing safeguards leak: arXiv moderation catches 21.2%, bioRxiv→PMC pipeline lets 85.3% of preprint hallucinations through to the published record.
- Google Scholar increasingly indexes "citation-only entries" — references that cannot be linked to any real publication but already appear as references in other papers — creating a feedback loop that contaminates downstream retrieval.
- Section *Discussion*, paragraph 7: *"The harder problem — detecting claims that misrepresent the content of real sources, or hallucinated assertions embedded in unstructured prose — remains far less tractable, and the gap between what verifiers can detect and what LLMs can produce is wide and probably widening."* This is L3 in the authors' own words.

**(b) ARS 2026-04-30 production session (cited in v3.6.8 §1).** The session found a `bibliography_v2.md` derivative artifact containing a fabricated quote attributed to D14 (OECD/UNESCO 2005). The fabricated quote was caught only because the user manually retrieved the original PDF and grep'd for the quoted phrase — i.e., a manual L3 check. v3.6.8 §3.1 D1 (frontmatter trust-strength split) prevents the fabricated quote from being silently amplified through downstream prose, but does not by itself surface the fabricated quote. The downstream synthesis_agent rule "Verbatim quotes only within the verified phrase boundary" (line 170) names the L3 discipline but is not mechanically enforceable in current shape — no finalizer or gate verifies that an in-text citation carries a verifiable quote anchor.

**(c) Retrieval-side contamination.** Zhao et al. Fig. 3c documents a steep rise in "citation-only" Google Scholar entries since 2024 — non-existent references that nevertheless appear as standalone bibliographic entries in Scholar after enough citing-paper accumulation. ARS retrieval_agent currently treats Semantic Scholar / OpenAlex / Google Scholar results as authoritative for the existence check. Post-2024-mid this assumption no longer holds for the long tail.

v3.7.3 therefore adds two orthogonal protections:
- **L3-1 (claim faithfulness locator):** every in-text citation MUST carry either an extracted verbatim quote (≤25 words from the cited source) OR a precise locator (page / section / paragraph identifier in the cited source). Bare citations without either are MED-WARN-NO-LOCATOR and refused by the terminal gate.
- **L3-2 (contaminated-source advisory):** `literature_corpus[]` entries gain an optional `contamination_signals` object carrying two boolean fields — `preprint_post_llm_inflection` (year ≥ 2024 AND venue type is preprint server) and `semantic_scholar_unmatched` (Semantic Scholar lookup returned no match by title or DOI). These signals are **advisory** — they surface in the cite-time finalizer report but do not by themselves block emission. The corresponding marker is `LOW-WARN-CONTAMINATED-SOURCE`, which is acknowledgeable via `/ars-mark-read <slug>` per v3.6.8 §3.6 precedent.

v3.7.3 explicitly does NOT attempt the full L3 audit (running an LLM-as-judge against ref full-text for each (claim, ref) pair). That stays v3.8+ scope. v3.7.3 is the *locator* layer — the minimum infrastructure that makes the full L3 audit possible later by giving each citation a stable anchor to verify against.

## 2. Goal & Non-Goals

### 2.1 Goal

Close two attack surfaces orthogonal to v3.7.1/v3.7.2:

1. **L3-1 locator gate.** Every in-text citation emitted by `synthesis_agent`, `draft_writer_agent`, `report_compiler_agent` MUST be accompanied by a structured quote-or-locator anchor. The Two-Layer Citation Emission (v3.7.1 §3.3 Step 1) gains a third layer (locator). The finalizer 4-cell matrix extends to 5-cell along a new axis. Terminal gate refuses MED-WARN-NO-LOCATOR markers.

2. **L3-2 contaminated-source advisory.** Adapter-produced and AI-produced `literature_corpus[]` entries gain optional `contamination_signals` fields. `bibliography_agent` sets `preprint_post_llm_inflection` at ingest time based on year + venue type. `bibliography_agent` calls Semantic Scholar (per `references/semantic_scholar_api_protocol.md`) at acquisition time and sets `semantic_scholar_unmatched` when no hit. The cite-time finalizer surfaces these as LOW-WARN-CONTAMINATED-SOURCE markers.

Target outcome: the v3.6.8 fabricated-quote incident, replayed under v3.7.3, surfaces a MED-WARN-NO-LOCATOR at the finalizer pass (because the fabricated quote either lacks a page locator or carries one the audit cannot verify). The terminal gate refuses output until the user re-emits the citation with a valid (`<kind>` ≠ `none`) anchor or removes the citation. NO-LOCATOR is NOT acknowledgeable via `/ars-mark-read` — see §3.1 Terminal gate extension + Q5 (resolved).

### 2.2 Non-Goals (out of v3.7.3 scope)

- **No automated L3 claim-ref alignment audit.** Running an LLM-as-judge over (claim, ref full-text) pairs to verify the cited paper actually says what the prose claims stays v3.8+. v3.7.3 only enforces that the *anchor* (quote or locator) exists, making the audit feasible later. Per the external paper's own admission, no reliable L3 detection method currently exists.
- **No OpenAlex / Google Scholar API integration.** The contamination check is single-source (Semantic Scholar). OpenAlex backstop stays v3.7.4 scope (separate retrieval-layer hardening).
- **No mandatory blocking on L3-2.** Contamination signals are LOW-WARN per v3.5 Collaboration Depth Observer precedent. The user can acknowledge and proceed; v3.7.3 surfaces, it does not enforce. L3-1 IS a hard gate; L3-2 is not.
- **No retroactive entry mutation.** Existing `literature_corpus[]` entries without `contamination_signals` validate cleanly (optional field). The bibliography_agent ingestion path adds the field for new entries; old entries can be migrated via a follow-up batch script if the user wants, but no automatic upgrade fires.
- **No new pipeline phase.** Locator emission attaches to existing v3.6.8 Two-Layer Citation; contamination check attaches to existing bibliography_agent ingestion.
- **No v3.6.7 / v3.7.1 / v3.7.2 boundary mutation.** All existing PATTERN PROTECTION blocks, SHA gate v2, Scope Report end-to-end stay byte-equivalent. v3.7.3 is additive.

## 3. Pattern Inventory

### 3.1 L3-1 — Per-citation quote-or-locator gate

**Pattern:** When `synthesis_agent` / `draft_writer_agent` / `report_compiler_agent` emit an in-text citation under v3.7.1 Two-Layer Citation Emission, the citation carries only the slug reference `<!--ref:slug-->`. No structured anchor records *which passage in the cited source supports the surrounding claim*. The synthesis_agent rule "Verbatim quotes only within verified phrase boundary" exists in prose (synthesis_agent.md:170) but is not mechanically extractable and is not enforced by any gate. An author or downstream auditor cannot mechanically verify that a claim is anchored to a specific passage in the cited source.

**Mechanism — three sub-axes:**

**(A) Emission axis.** Current Two-Layer Citation has form `Smith (2024) <!--ref:smith2024-->`. No slot for a quote or page locator. The agent can write any claim adjacent to the citation; the slug is opaque to claim-content alignment.

**(B) Resolution axis.** The cite_provenance_finalizer_agent's 4-cell matrix reads only frontmatter trust state. It cannot detect "claim-without-anchor" because the missing data is in the prose, not the frontmatter.

**(C) Gate axis.** Terminal gate (`cite_provenance_terminal_gate_agent` for deep-research, `formatter_agent` for academic-paper/pipeline) only inspects markers for `ok` / LOW-WARN-acknowledged status. A bare citation with no claim-anchor passes the gate today.

**Protection — v3.7.3 Three-Layer Citation Emission:**

Extend the v3.7.1 Two-Layer form by adding a third hidden layer carrying the locator:

```
<visible layer> <!--ref:slug--><!--anchor:<kind>:<value>-->
```

Where `<kind>` ∈ `{quote, page, section, paragraph, none}` and `<value>` is the corresponding payload:

| kind | value format | example | semantics |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quote` | URL-encoded verbatim text from cited source, ≤25 words | `quote:When%20publishers%20bypass...` | strongest anchor; can be grep'd against retrieved source |
| `page` | page number or range, e.g. `12` or `12-14` | `page:12-14` | medium anchor; locates passage but does not verify content |
| `section` | section identifier, e.g. `3.2` or `Results` | `section:3.2` | medium anchor; relies on cited source's stable section labels |
| `paragraph` | paragraph index from start of section, e.g. `3` | `paragraph:3` | weakest structural anchor; brittle to revision |
| `none` | empty | `none:` | explicit no-anchor declaration; forbidden in production, used only by bibliography_agent during ingest before any prose exists |

Three firm rules:

- **R-L3-1-A (production-mandatory locator):** During `synthesis_agent` / `draft_writer_agent` / `report_compiler_agent` emission, every visible citation MUST be followed by both `<!--ref:slug-->` AND `<!--anchor:<kind>:<value>-->` where `<kind>` ≠ `none`. Emitting `<!--anchor:none:-->` in production prose is a contract violation detected by the finalizer.
- **R-L3-1-B (quote length cap):** When `<kind>` = `quote`, the URL-decoded value MUST be ≤25 words by whitespace split (per v3.6.7 word_count_conventions.md). Quotes exceeding 25 words MUST be replaced by `page` or `section` locator pointing to the passage.
- **R-L3-1-C (no anchor reading by emitting agents):** The emitting agent (synthesis, draft_writer, report_compiler) writes the `<!--anchor:...-->` from its own working knowledge of the cited source. It MUST NOT read frontmatter to discover anchor candidates (v3.6.7 partial-inversion discipline). When the agent cannot produce a verifiable anchor, it emits `<!--anchor:none:-->` and the finalizer marks the citation MED-WARN-NO-LOCATOR (gate-refused).

**Finalizer matrix extension (4-cell → 5-cell):**

The v3.6.8 §3.3 4-cell matrix gains a precedence-zero check on `<!--anchor:...-->`. If `<kind>` = `none`, the resolution is **MED-WARN-NO-LOCATOR** regardless of other trust state. Otherwise the v3.6.8 4-cell matrix proceeds:

| Anchor present | source_acquired | source_verified | human_read | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no (`none`) | — | — | — | **MED-WARN-NO-LOCATOR** (precedence-zero; supersedes other cells). Marker text: `[UNVERIFIED CITATION — NO QUOTE OR PAGE LOCATOR]<!--ref:slug-->` |
| yes | false | — | — | HIGH-WARN-NO-ORIGINAL (unchanged from v3.6.8) |
| yes | true | false | — | MED-WARN-NOT-CROSS-CHECKED (unchanged) |
| yes | true | true | false | LOW-WARN (unchanged, plus contamination-signal annotation if any contamination_signals present — see §3.2) |
| yes | true | true | true | `ok` (unchanged) |

NO-LOCATOR is MED severity (not HIGH) because the citation may still point at a real verified source; it is just unanchored. The fix is locator emission, not source acquisition. Treating NO-LOCATOR as HIGH would conflate two distinct defects.

**Terminal gate extension:**

`formatter_agent` (academic-paper / pipeline) and `cite_provenance_terminal_gate_agent` (deep-research) MUST refuse to emit final output when any `[UNVERIFIED CITATION — NO QUOTE OR PAGE LOCATOR]` marker remains, AT THE SAME PRECEDENCE as the v3.6.8 HIGH-WARN-NO-ORIGINAL refusal. **Remediation path: the user re-emits the citation with a valid (`<kind>` ≠ `none`) anchor.** `/ars-mark-read` does NOT clear NO-LOCATOR — the precedence-zero rule stops BEFORE applying the 4-cell matrix that consumes `human_read_source`, so an unread/read distinction cannot mutate the resolution. This asymmetry is intentional: a locator is a structural property of the prose, not an evidence-state property of the source. v3.7.3 codex review P2-2 closure (2026-05-12); see also Q5 (resolved).

### 3.2 L3-2 — Contaminated-source advisory signals

**Pattern:** `bibliography_agent` and `retrieval_agent` accept Semantic Scholar / Google Scholar / OpenAlex / publisher lookup results as authoritative for the existence check. Post-2024-mid, two distinct contamination vectors are documented in the external corpus-scale literature (Zhao et al. 2026-05 Fig. 1a-d, Fig. 3c):

- **Vector 1: post-LLM-inflection preprint contamination.** Hallucination rate in preprint corpora (arXiv / bioRxiv / SSRN) rose sharply starting mid-2024, 18 months after ChatGPT release. The rise is driven by agentic AI research assistants that synthesize plausible-looking citations from web content rather than from indexed bibliographic data. Any preprint with year ≥ 2024 carries elevated baseline risk independent of any direct evidence of hallucination in that specific paper.
- **Vector 2: citation-only Scholar entries.** Google Scholar increasingly indexes references that cannot be linked to any real publication — entries created purely by accumulated citing-paper references, with no underlying publication. A reference present in Scholar but absent from Semantic Scholar / OpenAlex / Crossref is a strong contamination signal: it suggests the entry exists only as a downstream citation, not as an actual published artifact.

Neither signal individually proves a specific reference is hallucinated. Both are advisory. But surfacing them at cite-time gives the user the information needed to decide whether to acquire the source (`source_acquired: true` path), drop the citation, or acknowledge the risk and proceed.

**Mechanism — two ingestion-time checks:**

**(A) `preprint_post_llm_inflection` boolean.** Set by `bibliography_agent` at ingest time. Computed as `year >= 2024 AND venue is preprint server (arXiv / bioRxiv / medRxiv / SSRN / Research Square / Preprints.org / ChemRxiv / EarthArXiv / OSF Preprints / TechRxiv)`. The venue list is closed (per §6 maintenance note). The threshold year 2024 follows Zhao et al. inflection-point analysis; bibliography_agent prompt cites the source so future amendments to the threshold are traceable. v3.7.3 gemini review F6 expanded the list from 6 to 10 venues.

**(B) `semantic_scholar_unmatched` boolean.** Set by `bibliography_agent` when a Semantic Scholar API lookup (per `references/semantic_scholar_api_protocol.md`) returns no match by either DOI or title. The check fires only when `obtained_via` is NOT `manual` (a user-curated entry is exempted; the user has already vouched for it). The lookup uses the existing protocol's title-similarity threshold; reaching no-match means S2 has no indexed paper matching the entry.

**Protection — v3.7.3 contamination signals schema + cite-time surfacing:**

`literature_corpus_entry.schema.json` gains an optional `contamination_signals` object:

```yaml
contamination_signals:
  preprint_post_llm_inflection: true | false   # year >= 2024 AND venue is preprint server
  semantic_scholar_unmatched: true | false     # S2 lookup returned no match
```

Both fields are optional within the object; the entire `contamination_signals` object is optional at the entry level. An entry with the object absent is treated as "signals not yet computed" (no advisory fires). An entry with the object present but both fields `false` is treated as "signals computed, no contamination evidence" (no advisory fires).

**Finalizer extension:**

When the 5-cell matrix resolves to `ok` or LOW-WARN but the entry's `contamination_signals` has any field `true`, the finalizer adds an annotation suffix to the resolved marker:

| Base resolution | contamination_signals | Annotated marker |
|---|---|---|
| LOW-WARN | none / both false | `<!--ref:slug LOW-WARN-->` (unchanged) |
| LOW-WARN | preprint_post_llm_inflection: true | `<!--ref:slug LOW-WARN CONTAMINATED-PREPRINT-->` |
| LOW-WARN | semantic_scholar_unmatched: true | `<!--ref:slug LOW-WARN CONTAMINATED-UNMATCHED-->` |
| LOW-WARN | both true | `<!--ref:slug LOW-WARN CONTAMINATED-PREPRINT+UNMATCHED-->` |
| `ok` | any contamination flag | `<!--ref:slug ok CONTAMINATED-...-->` (same suffix shapes) |

Contamination annotations are **advisory** — they do not change the gate decision. `ok CONTAMINATED-...` still passes the terminal gate; `LOW-WARN CONTAMINATED-...` is acknowledgeable via `/ars-mark-read <slug>` exactly like plain LOW-WARN.

Two firm rules:

- **R-L3-2-A (advisory only):** Contamination signals never block emission on their own. The user retains discretion. This follows the v3.5 Collaboration Depth Observer + v3.6.8 LOW-WARN precedent. Hard-gating on contamination would amount to refusing to cite mid-2024+ preprints en masse, which is too coarse.
- **R-L3-2-B (no retroactive computation):** bibliography_agent computes contamination_signals at ingest time, not at audit time. Re-running the check post-hoc on existing entries is a separate batch operation (deferred to user invocation; not part of v3.7.3 finalizer).

### 3.3 Interaction with v3.7.1 / v3.7.2

- v3.7.1 §3.3 D3 Two-Layer Citation Emission becomes Three-Layer; the Two-Layer rule remains valid as a subset (a Two-Layer citation is equivalent to a Three-Layer citation with `<!--anchor:none:-->` and is rejected by the production gate per R-L3-1-A).
- v3.7.1 finalizer 4-cell matrix becomes 5-cell along the new locator-present axis (precedence-zero check). Existing 4 cells preserve their semantics conditional on anchor present ≠ `none`.
- v3.7.2 SHA Gate v2 and Scope Report end-to-end are unaffected. v3.7.3 does not touch the v3.6.7 PATTERN PROTECTION blocks.
- v3.6.5 corpus-consumer Iron Rules are unaffected. The new `contamination_signals` field is owned by bibliography_agent (AI-set) per the existing AI-owned fields convention; adapters MAY set it but are not required to.

## 5. Acceptance Criteria

ARS v3.7.3 ships when:

1. Schema validates: synthetic `literature_corpus_entry` with `contamination_signals: {preprint_post_llm_inflection: true, semantic_scholar_unmatched: false}` passes `check_literature_corpus_schema.py`. Entry without the field also passes (backward compat).
2. Synthesis agent emits Three-Layer Citation in a synthetic chapter: visible + `<!--ref:slug-->` + `<!--anchor:quote:...-->` for at least one citation, `<!--anchor:page:...-->` for another. No bare Two-Layer citation in production prose.
3. Finalizer correctly resolves Three-Layer Citation: a synthetic test corpus with one anchor=none citation resolves to MED-WARN-NO-LOCATOR; terminal gate refuses output. A corpus with all anchors present resolves cleanly per v3.6.8 4-cell matrix.
4. Contamination annotation: a synthetic corpus where one entry has `contamination_signals.preprint_post_llm_inflection: true` produces a finalizer output where the resolved marker for that entry carries the `CONTAMINATED-PREPRINT` suffix. The terminal gate emits the output (advisory does not block).
5. v3.6.7 PATTERN PROTECTION blocks remain byte-equivalent. v3.6.7 lint regression PASSES 12/12 + 58/58 mutation tests. v3.7.1 / v3.7.2 lints all continue to PASS.
6. Codex review against this spec doc converges to 0 P1 + 0 P2 (round count not bounded; per `feedback_codex_workflow_consolidated.md` review-vs-challenge split, review confirms contract; challenge probes contract gaps in a follow-up round).

## 6. Out-of-Scope (Future Work)

- **v3.7.4 retrieval-side hardening:** OpenAlex + Crossref triangulation as a second contamination signal. ARS today depends on Semantic Scholar only; adding a second independent index closes the single-source-of-truth gap on L3-2 Vector 2.
- **v3.8 L3 full audit:** an `claim_ref_alignment_audit_agent` that runs LLM-as-judge over (claim, ref full-text) pairs for a sampled subset of citations. Anchors emitted by v3.7.3 become the input to this audit. Open question: how to sample (random N%? all `quote:` kind? all post-2024 preprints?). Defer to v3.8 spec.
- **AI disclosure schema split:** Zhao et al. find LLM-assisted writing signatures correlate with hallucination rate (Fig. 1l). Splitting the AI disclosure field into per-stage (drafting / editing / reference suggestion / data analysis) makes the reference-suggestion stage individually flaggable. Defer to a separate disclosure-protocol PR.
- **Migration tool for legacy entries:** a batch script that walks an existing `literature_corpus[]` and computes `contamination_signals` for entries that lack the field. v3.7.3 ingests new entries with the field; legacy entries can be migrated by re-running bibliography_agent or by writing this script. Defer.
- **Preprint venue list maintenance:** the closed list (arXiv / bioRxiv / medRxiv / SSRN / Research Square / Preprints.org / ChemRxiv / EarthArXiv / OSF Preprints / TechRxiv — 10 venues as of v3.7.3) is encoded in `bibliography_agent.md`. New preprint servers entering the ecosystem require a spec amendment. Track as a recurring maintenance task.

## 8. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Agents emit `<!--anchor:none:-->` reflexively to satisfy the contract, defeating the gate's purpose. | R-L3-1-C mandates that `none` triggers MED-WARN-NO-LOCATOR (gate-refused). Agents that reflexively emit `none` produce gate-refused output; the user notices immediately. The contract is shaped so "emit `none`" is not a free pass. |
| `quote:` anchors fabricated by the agent (quote that does not appear in the cited source). | v3.7.3 does not detect this. v3.8 L3 audit closes it by grep-against-retrieved-source. v3.7.3 establishes the anchor channel; v3.8 verifies anchor content. |
| Page numbers in `page:` anchors hallucinated. | Same — v3.7.3 establishes the channel; v3.8 verifies. v3.7.3 is a necessary precondition for v3.8, not a substitute. |
| Contamination signals fire on legitimate post-2024 preprints, creating noise. | Advisory only. User retains discretion via `/ars-mark-read`. Per Zhao et al., the entire post-2024 preprint corpus DOES carry elevated baseline risk — the noise IS the signal. |
| Semantic Scholar API rate limit / downtime making `semantic_scholar_unmatched` unreliable. | Existing `semantic_scholar_api_protocol.md` covers degradation. When the API is unavailable, bibliography_agent omits the `semantic_scholar_unmatched` field rather than setting it to `false` (which would imply "checked and found"). Absence ≠ negative confirmation. |
| Spec-doc-only delivery (no implementation in v3.7.3 PR-A) creates spec/impl drift. | This spec is committed alongside the agent-prompt and schema changes in the same PR (PR-A). Lint additions in PR-B. CHANGELOG ties them. No spec-only release. |
| Three-Layer Citation breaks existing v3.7.1 finalizer for non-upgraded prose. | Backward compat: a Two-Layer Citation with no `<!--anchor:...-->` is treated as anchor=none (MED-WARN-NO-LOCATOR). Existing v3.7.1 corpus prose gates as MED-WARN until re-emitted under v3.7.3 contract. This is intentional — old prose IS unanchored and SHOULD surface as such. |
| Contamination check delays bibliography_agent ingest. | The S2 lookup is already in the v3.3 pipeline (`semantic_scholar_id` recording). v3.7.3 adds one bit of state derived from the same lookup. Marginal cost zero. |

## 9. Open Questions

- **Q1 (locator format precision):** should `paragraph` index be 0-based or 1-based? 1-based matches human convention; 0-based matches code conventions. Tentative answer: 1-based. Resolve at codex round-1.
- **Q2 (quote encoding):** URL-encoding (`%20` etc.) for quote payloads vs. HTML entity encoding vs. just escaping the HTML comment terminator. URL-encoding is most robust; HTML entity is more readable. Tentative answer: URL-encode, since the anchor lives in an HTML comment and `-->` would otherwise terminate it. Resolve at codex round-1.
- **Q3 (preprint venue list scope):** should the list be hardcoded in `bibliography_agent.md` or extracted into a `shared/references/preprint_venues.md` for reusability? Tentative answer: extract to shared/, since `retrieval_agent` and `citation_compliance_agent` may also consume it. Resolve at codex round-1.
- **Q4 (year threshold = 2024 vs more precise):** Zhao et al. inflection is "mid-2024" (around month 6-7). Should the threshold be `year >= 2024` (loose, catches January 2024 papers that predate the inflection) or `(year, month) >= (2024, 6)` (precise but requires month parsing)? Tentative answer: `year >= 2024` for simplicity; January–May 2024 papers carry slightly inflated false-positive but the noise cost is low. Resolve at codex round-1.
- **Q5 (RESOLVED, codex review P2-2 closure 2026-05-12):** `/ars-mark-read <slug>` does NOT clear NO-LOCATOR. The precedence-zero rule stops BEFORE applying the trust-state matrix, and `/ars-mark-read` only mutates `human_read_source` (a matrix input). The earlier tentative answer ("reuse `/ars-mark-read` for one acknowledgment surface") was a documented but unimplementable promise — the finalizer rules cannot satisfy it. The only NO-LOCATOR remediation is re-emitting the citation with `<kind>` ≠ `none`. The asymmetry is intentional: a locator is a structural property of the prose, not an evidence-state property of the source.

## 10. Spec Traceability

- §1 anchor sources: Zhao et al. 2026-05, ARS v3.6.8 §1 production incident.
- §3.1 R-L3-1-A/B/C: derived from v3.7.1 §3.3 Step 1 firm rules (slug-from-corpus-only, no-frontmatter-read, every-citation discipline).
- §3.2 R-L3-2-A/B: derived from v3.5 Collaboration Depth Observer (advisory not blocking) and v3.6.8 §3.6 (`/ars-mark-read` acknowledgment).
- §4 step ordering: mirrors v3.7.1 spec implementation step ordering (schema → agent → finalizer → gate → docs).
- §6 OOS items: v3.7.4 retrieval hardening, v3.8 L3 full audit, AI disclosure schema split — each scoped to a separate future spec.

# AI Disclosure Schema — Discovery Document

**Author:** Cheng-I Wu
**Scope:** Discovery — NO schema commitment, NO implementation
**Discovery output is a PR adding this document; PR merge closes #106. Implementation issue (deferred) blocked-by #106.**

## 0. Phase tracking

This discovery is split into three execution phases. Each phase ships as a PR commit.

| Phase | Deliverable | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Phase 1 | Doc scaffold + 4 anchor snapshots locked (Wayback + SHA-256) + manifest | shipped (PR #107 c1) |
| Phase 2 | Fill cells for PRISMA-trAIce + ICMJE (32 of 64 cells) | shipped (PR #107 c2) |
| Phase 3a | Fill cells for Nature Portfolio (16 of remaining 32 cells; 48 of 64 total) | shipped (PR #107 c3) |
| Phase 3b.1 | Fill cells for IEEE (remaining 16 cells; 64 of 64 total) | shipped (PR #107 c4) |
| Phase 3b.2 | Deliverable 2 design space (5 dimensions A–E + trade-off matrix) | shipped (PR #107 c5) |
| Phase 3b.3 | Deliverable 3 open questions (6 baseline + 4 surfaced) | shipped (PR #107 c6) |

**Phase 1 explicitly does NOT fill any cells.** Cells carry `phase: 1-scaffold` placeholder until Phase 2/3. This is intentional — Phase 1 builds the provenance infrastructure so Phase 2/3 cell-filling can cite verbatim with byte-level integrity.

## 1. Background

ARS currently has a minimal `ai_disclosure` field (boolean / narrative). Three downstream pressures suggest this **may** need structural expansion:

1. **v3.7.x trust-chain infrastructure** (`docs/design/2026-05-12-ars-v3.7.3-claim-faithfulness-and-contaminated-source-spec.md`) records source provenance + citation anchors. Per-stage AI disclosure has been **hypothesized** as a complement on the production side, but should be tested rather than assumed.
2. **Zhao et al. arXiv:2605.07723 (2026-05)** corpus-scale evidence suggests AI-usage stage **may** correlate with hallucination risk profile. Disclosure granularity has analytical value worth investigating.
3. **External normative anchors** (PRISMA-trAIce / ICMJE / Nature / IEEE, plus expansion candidates) **may** require disclosure beyond ARS's current boolean/narrative form. The actual requirement-vs-recommendation strength varies and must be classified per-item, not aggregated.

**Honest about uncertainty:** discovery output may conclude that the right answer is to align ARS to a single anchor verbatim, construct a hybrid, defer policy mapping to a renderer layer, OR retain the current minimal `ai_disclosure` field. All four outcomes are valid discovery results.

A prior draft attempted to propose a concrete schema directly. Codex pre-open review flagged 5 P1 structural problems. These were symptoms of skipping discovery. This document is the discovery reset.

## 2. Scope

### 2.1 In scope

- Source-by-field disclosure matrix across a minimum required set of normative anchors with auditable provenance
- Design space documentation (enumeration of design choices, NOT a chosen solution)
- Open questions for community feedback

### 2.2 Out of scope (per #106)

- Schema file
- Renderer skill
- Migration tooling
- Lint
- Tests

These are reserved for the follow-up implementation issue, which is blocked-by this discovery's completion.

## 4. Deliverable 1: Source-by-field disclosure matrix

### 4.1 Classification scheme

Each cell carries:

| Field | Required? | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `source_strength` | yes | `explicit-mandate` / `explicit-recommend` / `conditional-mandate` / `implicit` / `not-addressed` / `unknown` |
| `verbatim_quote` | yes for mandate/recommend/conditional cells | Paraphrase forbidden; ≤ 50 words verbatim from primary source |
| `inference_passage` | yes for `implicit` cells | The passage(s) used for inference, verbatim |
| `locator` | yes for mandate / recommend / conditional / implicit cells | Section / item / heading within source (e.g., "PRISMA-trAIce Table 1 M6.a"). `not-addressed` cells use `—` because the read scope is the entire source (per the `not-addressed` rule below); `unknown` cells use `—` because the source was not fully read. |
| `expected_value_type` | yes for mandate / recommend / conditional / implicit cells | boolean / structured / narrative. `not-addressed` / `unknown` cells use `—`. |
| `conditional_trigger` | required for `conditional-mandate` | Plain-text trigger description |
| `snapshot_ref` | required for mandate / recommend / conditional / implicit cells | `{anchor_slug}:wayback={wayback_id}`. `not-addressed` / `unknown` cells do not require snapshot_ref (the read-scope is the full snapshot, recorded once at the per-anchor matrix header). |

**`not-addressed` rule:** a cell may be `not-addressed` only when the matrix author has read the **entire** primary source AND can affirmatively state the field is absent. Cells where the source has not been fully read must be `unknown`.

**`unknown` ceiling:** matrix may close with up to **10 of 64** cells marked `unknown` (subjective ceiling, adjustable upward per #106 acceptance criteria if author finds source genuinely hard to fully read — document why).

### 4.2 Candidate disclosure fields (16-field core list)

These 16 fields anchor the 4×16 = 64-cell minimum matrix. Additional fields may be added during Phase 2/3 if material to ARS's design decision; subtractions require rationale.

1. **AI tool name**
2. **AI tool version**
3. **AI tool developer / manufacturer**
4. **Stage / phase of use**
5. **Specific task within stage**
6. **Affected manuscript sections / content locator**
7. **Date(s) of use**
8. **Prompts** (full text or summary, depending on source)
9. **Human oversight method** (reviewer count, qualifications)
10. **Human responsibility statement**
11. **Performance evaluation method**
12. **Performance evaluation results** (quantitative)
13. **Limitations / known failure modes**
14. **Disclosure location** (acknowledgments / Methods / cover letter)
15. **Copyediting exemption predicate**
16. **AI-generated image / figure / content rights**

### 4.3 Per-anchor matrix — PRISMA-trAIce

**Snapshot:** [`prisma-trAIce` @ wayback 20260513075443](https://web.archive.org/web/20260513075443/https://ai.jmir.org/2025/1/e80247/)
**Source-strength caveat:** PRISMA-trAIce is a **pre-Delphi proposal** (Holst et al. 2025, §Methods: *"this work is explicitly intended as a well-founded proposal that provides an immediate solution and can serve as the foundation for a subsequent, community-driven formal consensus process"*). It has not undergone formal consensus. **No item carries `explicit-mandate` strength** — the framework explicitly invites community refinement. Items within the framework use reporting-guideline directive verbs ("describe", "report", "include") classified here as `explicit-recommend` *within the proposed framework*. The framework itself is `conditional-mandate` on "AI tool used as methodological tool in an SLR" — outside that condition the framework does not apply. Cells below distinguish item-level recommend from framework-level conditional via the `conditional_trigger` column.

| # | Field | Source strength | Verbatim quote (or inference passage) | Locator | Value type | Conditional trigger |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 13 | Limitations / known failure modes | explicit-recommend | "Discuss any limitations encountered in using the AI tool(s) (eg, technical issues, biases identified, challenges in prompt engineering, unexpected outputs, limitations in AI performance for specific sub-tasks)." | Table 1, D1 | narrative | AI tool used in SLR |
